#### Exploring Outbound vs Inbound Marketing: Which Approach Is Right for Your Business
As a marketing professional, I often get asked by an array of clients, “ What IS the difference between outbound and inbound marketing”. Let me explain it to you in simple terms.

Outbound Marketing &#8211; Interrupting Your Audience
Outbound marketing, also known as traditional marketing, is a strategy that aims to reach a broad audience through various channels such as print ads, TV commercials, radio ads, billboards, and cold calling. The primary focus of outbound marketing is to interrupt the audience&#8217;s attention and present them with a message.
While outbound marketing can be effective in reaching a broad audience quickly, it can be costly, and its success rate can be challenging to measure. If your target audience is broad, and you want to reach out to them quickly, outbound marketing may be the right approach for your business.
Inbound Marketing &#8211; The Modern Approach
Inbound marketing is a modern approach that focuses on creating valuable content and experiences tailored to the needs and interests of your target audience. Inbound marketing involves creating and sharing content such as blog posts, social media updates, videos, podcasts, and e-books to attract potential customers to your website or social media pages.
The primary focus of inbound marketing is to create a two-way communication approach, where the company engages with the audience, building relationships and fostering trust. Inbound marketing is all about creating value for your potential customers, educating them about your product or service, and building long-term relationships with them.
The advantage of inbound marketing is that it can be cost-effective, and it&#8217;s easier to measure its success rate. Inbound marketing is a long-term strategy that can help companies build a loyal customer base.
Choosing the Right Approach for Your Business
Choosing the right marketing approach for your business depends on several factors, such as your target audience, budget, and marketing goals. Both outbound and inbound marketing approaches have their advantages and disadvantages, but the key is to determine which approach aligns with your business goals and target audience.
If your target audience is broad, and you want to reach out to them quickly, outbound marketing may be the way to go. However, if you want to build long-term relationships with your potential customers, educate them about your product or service, and build a loyal customer base, inbound marketing may be the better approach for your business.
In conclusion, both outbound and inbound marketing approaches have their place in today&#8217;s marketing landscape. The key is to create a comprehensive marketing strategy that integrates both approaches to maximise your marketing efforts and achieve your business goals.

Decide the geographical location of where your Ad should be targeting, you can also choose certain demographics such as Age and Gender, Facebook will estimate the number of people the Ad will potentially reach. You can be more specific by entering a full street address of your store, and specifying the radius to be reached of that physical address.

Creating Your Ad for the Local Customer:
Include relevant Images that is related to your Ad Campaign. For example, if you have a Promotion or Sale, use attractive images of merchandise that’s on sale – remember the image is a powerful visual that will make the first impression to your potential customers. Your description and headline for the Ad should be convincing and move people to engage with your business. Be sure to include a Call to Action button for the Ad, this can be a “Like Page”, “Learn More”, “Call Now”, “Send Message” or “Get Directions” if you have a street address for your business page- bringing customers to your shopfront.

If you have multiple locations, you can create individual Ads for each area you’re targeting, this will allow you to customise the Ads towards each group and track which areas are responding better than others.

#### Facebook News Feed Changes – what does it mean for your business?
As we’re settling into the New Year and trying new things – or even on-track with New Year Resolutions, Facebook is also revamping its News Feed!
Earlier last week, if you’ve seen Mark Zuckerberg’s post or the News Release from Facebook about bringing people closer, then you’ll know that News Feeds are going through a major change.
Why an Update?
Facebook was built as a social platform, to bring people closer and build relationships. This update is in response to Users feeling that Facebook has shifted too far away from friends and family related content, with the significant growth of business and brand public content overtaking their feeds.
What will the Update be?
We all know that posts with more Likes, Reactions, Comments and Shares tend to appear higher in News Feeds. With this new update however, Facebook aims to ‘bring people closer together’ by prioritising Friends and Family posts with a new algorithm, and show less public content from businesses and publishers. Hence your business page posts may see a decrease in reach, especially if the content is not engaging.
So what should Businesses do?
While this is great for the Users, it is important for businesses to stay on top of the curve, or risk being unseen. Page posts will still appear in feeds, but there will be even fewer spaces! Here are 5 tips to help you break through to your audience:
1, Preferences
People can still see posts from their favourite Pages if they choose “See First in News Feed” in their preferences. So encourage your Followers to set your page as a ‘see first’.
2, Content, content, content!
Yes Content is key! If you are just bombarding people with lots of passive posts, chances are, your Page Posts will start to rank lower and decrease in distribution.
Facebook wants content that connect people by instigating conversation and inspiring back-and-forth discussion. So your posts must provoke your audience to want to interact with it (rather than just passive information).
For example, relevant community updates, events, or news can start conversations. Think of what people want to talk about, tell ‘Stories’ and use real-life situations that people can relate to. “Edu-tainment” is another type of content that provides value and drives engagement especially in Likes and Shares. Be creative and get people talking!
3, Live Videos
Videos generally show higher in News Feeds, and Live Videos tend to generate discussion among viewers, which will give the post a further boost. Consider running a regular informational Live Video, and encourage people to comment with their questions.
4, Beware the Engagement Bait
Now you might think, maybe I can get people to engage by asking them to Like or Tag their friends! Well Facebook is also going to crack down and demote spam posts that goad people into taking action, as these type of content is not a meaningful interaction. Examples include asking people to Vote by reaction, Liking because of a certain characteristic, or commanding people to comment “YES” if they agree with you.

Source: News Feed FYI: Fighting Engagement Bait on Facebook
5, Advertising
If you haven’t already started, now is the time to prepare and budget for Facebook advertising. There really isn’t any way around it anymore. With this new update, you need to pay to play. Don’t be afraid to ask for help or use a marketing agency to get you started.
Remember, there are still two billion users on Facebook, so your market is out there. Don’t be discouraged but be ready for this new change – and Facebook is constantly changing – so who knows what’s next! This clean-up on Facebook will improve user experience and if you step up to the game, your business can even have a more meaningful presence on Facebook!

#### Four Tips to a More Effective YouTube Marketing
Audiences spend more and more time watching videos and they always search for fun, informational, and unique video content. In our Digital Age, if you don’t meet the criteria, it’s more likely that they’ll search for other video content that meets the standards.
So, if YouTube an integral part of your Marketing Channel, this is the blog for you. We’ll share Four Effective Tips to Improve your YouTube Marketing.

 Use Unconventional Videos to Pique Customer’s Curiosity

For your video to be successful, it has to tell an original compelling story that piques interest. Boring infomercials are so outdated that people won’t spend the time necessary to watch them. They may tolerate a dry tutorial if your video offers unique advice that they’ll only find within your content.
A good example would be Volkswagen’s Guerilla Marketing Campaign: Speed Up Your Life &#8211; Take the Slide!
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W4o0ZVeixYU
Whilst this video appears completely irrelevant in a way, it perfectly suits the brand message of the Polo GTi &#8211; the particular car being promoted.
Unconventional videos allow you to take your creativity outside the box for your branding. Make sure to evoke emotions or relate your brand messages in this type of campaign. However, we advise that you don’t go to extremes with this type of content as it may leave your customer confused at the end of it all.
&nbsp;

 Use Keywords to Help Your Customers

Help your market recognise your products and services in the buying process. Audiences that find you on YouTube are usually in the discovery stage and aren’t committed to purchasing just yet.
Choose keywords that are relevant when your audience searches for new information about your product and consider creating an educational video based on the keyword. AdWords Display Planner tool is a great tool you can use to research keywords.
Ever wondered how to narrow down the perfect keywords that you should use? Simply just consider your audience, the keywords both you and they would search if they were looking for your particular product or service, and combined with the research tool, consider the search volume each month. Be sure to target keywords and key phrases that are relevant to your brand and industry.
&nbsp;

 Get Prospects to go to your Website with a Video

The very goal of each video is to send interested prospects to your website to learn more about your products and services and ideally to make a purchase.
Therefore, it’s important to provide an engaging and educational video, but leave them hanging, just enough to need to follow your call to action at the end of your video, and to visit your website for the full information, or for a demonstration of your particular product or service you want them to purchase and use.
&nbsp;

 Optimise Your YouTube Channels

The common thing that many advertisers forget is that audiences also check your YouTube Channels. Completely optimise your channel and also drive traffic to your other online platforms.
Always provide relevant information about the company and include your website and social media links and profiles.
A great feature is to insert clickable links in your banner header, so make sure to include Call to Actions and take full advantage of it!
&nbsp;
Are you in the process of working out the most effective social media tools to use in your marketing strategy? Why not test and measure them all? Like Facebook marketing and Google, YouTube Marketing requires a proactive strategy. Be savvy about your campaigns and make sure to be clear about your key marketing messages and what you want your viewers to do.

#### From Clicks to Conversations: How AI Impacts Lead Quality
[et_pb_section fb_built=&#8221;1&#8243; admin_label=&#8221;section&#8221; _builder_version=&#8221;4.16&#8243; global_colors_info=&#8221;{}&#8221; theme_builder_area=&#8221;post_content&#8221;][et_pb_row admin_label=&#8221;row&#8221; _builder_version=&#8221;4.16&#8243; background_size=&#8221;initial&#8221; background_position=&#8221;top_left&#8221; background_repeat=&#8221;repeat&#8221; global_colors_info=&#8221;{}&#8221; theme_builder_area=&#8221;post_content&#8221;][et_pb_column type=&#8221;4_4&#8243; _builder_version=&#8221;4.16&#8243; custom_padding=&#8221;|||&#8221; global_colors_info=&#8221;{}&#8221; custom_padding__hover=&#8221;|||&#8221; theme_builder_area=&#8221;post_content&#8221;][et_pb_text admin_label=&#8221;Text&#8221; _builder_version=&#8221;4.27.6&#8243; background_size=&#8221;initial&#8221; background_position=&#8221;top_left&#8221; background_repeat=&#8221;repeat&#8221; hover_enabled=&#8221;0&#8243; global_colors_info=&#8221;{}&#8221; theme_builder_area=&#8221;post_content&#8221; sticky_enabled=&#8221;0&#8243;]
For years, lead generation has been measured by clicks, traffic, and form submissions. More clicks generated were assumed to mean more opportunity. But as AI-powered tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Copilot, and Google AI Overviews have become part of everyday research, the link between clicks and quality leads is changing.
AI is shifting lead generation away from volume and towards intent. This means that businesses are seeing fewer empty enquiries and more meaningful conversations, even if website traffic looks different on the surface.
Why Clicks Matter Less Than They Used To
Traditionally, clicks have been the primary indicator of interest. However, today buyers often complete a lot of their research before clicking anything at all. AI tools summarise information, explain options, and help buyers narrow down choices long before a website visit happens.
This means a click now represents a more informed buyer. Instead of browsing, they are often validating a decision they have already considered. The result is fewer clicks, but stronger intent behind each one.
AI Filters Intent Earlier
One of the biggest impacts of AI on lead quality is early intent filtering. When buyers ask AI tools questions like “Which provider is best for my situation?” or “What should I expect to pay?”, the AI helps eliminate options that don’t fit.
By the time a buyer contacts a business, they are less likely to be price shopping or casually enquiring. They know what they want and why they are reaching out.
Better Research Leads to Better Conversations
AI-informed buyers tend to ask better questions. They understand the problem, the potential solutions, and the factors that matter. This changes the nature of sales conversations.
Instead of explaining basics, businesses can focus on fit, approach, and outcomes. This saves time on both sides and leads to higher-quality engagements.
Why Lead Quality Beats Lead Volume
High lead volume can create the illusion of success while draining resources. AI-driven lead generation encourages a shift in focus. Quality leads convert faster, require less education, and are more likely to align with your services.
Businesses that embrace this shift often see improved close rates, even if overall enquiry numbers fluctuate.
Adapting to the New Reality
The mistake many businesses make is trying to optimise AI-driven behaviour using old metrics. Instead of chasing clicks, the focus should be on clarity, authority, and content that supports AI-led research.
When your business is surfaced by AI tools as a credible option, the clicks that follow are more likely to turn into conversations that matter.
AI isn’t removing clicks altogether. It’s redefining what a click represents.
Where This Leaves Businesses
As AI continues to shape how buyers research and compare their options, lead generation is becoming less about chasing clicks and more about earning trust earlier in the decision making process. Businesses that understand this shift will be better placed to attract enquiries that are more informed, more relevant, and more likely to convert. 
If you want to improve the quality of your leads and make sure your business is showing up in the right conversations, Concept Designs &amp; Marketing can help you build a strategy that supports visibility, trust, and stronger results in an AI influenced search landscape.
FAQs: AI and Lead Quality

 How does AI impact lead quality?AI improves lead quality by filtering intent earlier, ensuring buyers are more informed before making contact.
 Why are fewer clicks sometimes better for businesses?Fewer clicks often mean less browsing and more decisive buyers, leading to stronger enquiries and higher conversion rates.
 Can AI-generated leads convert faster?Yes. AI-influenced leads typically have clearer expectations and move through the sales process more efficiently.
 Do AI tools replace traditional lead generation channels?AI tools don’t replace traditional channels but influence how and when buyers engage with them.
 How can businesses improve lead quality in the age of AI?By creating clear, authoritative content that aligns with buyer questions and supports AI-driven research.
 What metrics should businesses track instead of clicks?Businesses should focus on lead quality, conversion rates, deal size, and sales cycle length.

#### Gain a Competitive Edge with a Strategic Market Analysis
Most businesses don’t struggle because they lack ideas. They struggle because they lack clarity. Building a clear marketing plan starts with understanding your business, customers and competitors. 

A strategic market analysis helps uncover insights about your audience’s behaviour, industry trends and what others in your space are doing, so you can make smarter decisions about where to focus. 
This includes identifying profitable customer segments, selecting the right channels, and aligning tactics with your goals. With this clarity, every campaign becomes more purposeful, focused and results-driven.

FAQs
1. What is a market competitor analysis and why does my business need one?
 A market competitor analysis is a structured review of your competitors, customers, and industry landscape. It helps you understand where you sit in the market, what others are doing well, and where opportunities exist so you can build a stronger marketing strategy.
2. How does a competitor analysis improve my marketing strategy?
 A detailed competitor analysis reveals gaps in your positioning, messaging, pricing, and channel selection. This insight allows you to focus your marketing budget on activities that attract the right customers and deliver measurable returns.
3. What does a professional market analysis service include?
 A professional market analysis service typically includes competitor research, customer search analysis, industry trends, and strategic recommendations tailored to your business goals.
4. When should a business invest in a strategic market analysis?
 A strategic market analysis is valuable when launching a new service, entering a new market, refreshing your marketing strategy, refreshing your website, starting a Google Ads campaign, commencing an SEO campaign or starting a GEO campaign. If your growth has plateaued and you need clearer direction, a strategic market analysis can help you identify new opportunities.
5. How can a competitor analysis agency help businesses grow faster?
 A competitor analysis agency brings independent insight, proven frameworks, and industry data that help businesses identify faster growth opportunities, avoid costly trial and error, and make confident strategic decisions.
6. How does competitor analysis help businesses get recommended by AI search tools?
 AI search tools favour businesses with clear positioning, strong authority signals, and consistent messaging. Competitor analysis helps refine how your business is described, compared, and positioned so AI systems can confidently recommend you.
7. Why is strategic clarity important for AI driven search visibility?
 AI platforms interpret patterns across your content, reputation, and market presence. Strategic clarity ensures your services, audiences, and expertise are consistently communicated, making it easier for AI tools to understand and recommend your business.
8. What makes a business more likely to appear in AI generated recommendations?
 Businesses that clearly define their niche, demonstrate expertise, publish helpful content, and maintain consistent digital signals are more likely to appear in AI generated recommendations. A market analysis guides these priorities.
9. Can a competitor analysis improve how my business is compared in AI results?
 Yes. AI tools often compare businesses side by side. A competitor analysis helps shape your differentiators, strengths, and proof points so your business is positioned favourably in AI generated comparisons.
10. How does understanding customer segments improve AI search visibility?
 AI systems match user intent with the most relevant providers. When your customer segments are clearly defined and reflected in your messaging, your business is more likely to surface in AI recommendations for those audiences.

#### Google Ads Data Controls Are Changing in June 2026: What Businesses Need to Know
Google has announced an upcoming change to the way data controls work across Google Analytics and Google Ads.

From 15 June 2026, Google Ads data will be controlled through Ads Consent Mode, while Google Analytics data will continue to be managed through Google Analytics settings, including Google Signals.
Previously, there could be some overlap between the two settings, which made it harder for businesses to understand which controls applied to which data. This update is designed to make the process clearer.
For businesses running Google Ads, the key takeaway is that Consent Mode is becoming increasingly important. A correct setup can support conversion tracking, campaign optimisation, remarketing, and more reliable performance insights.
This change does not mean your ads will stop running. However, it is a timely reminder to review your current tracking setup, consent banner, GA4 configuration, and Google Ads conversion tracking.
Businesses that rely on Google Ads should make sure their measurement foundations are clean, compliant, and ready before the update takes effect.
FAQs About Google Ads Consent Mode and Google Signals
Will my Google Ads stop working after 15 June 2026?
No. Your Google Ads campaigns will continue to run after 15 June 2026. This update does not switch off ads or stop campaigns from serving. It changes how Google Ads data is controlled, especially when Google Analytics and Google Ads are linked.
The main area businesses need to review is their consent mode setup, because this can affect how conversion data, advertising cookies, and campaign measurement are handled.
What is changing with Google Ads data controls in June 2026?
Google is simplifying how data controls work between Google Analytics and Google Ads. After 15 June 2026, Google Ads data will be controlled through Ads Consent Mode, while Google Analytics settings, including Google Signals, will apply to data used within GA4.
This means businesses running Google Ads should make sure their Consent Mode setup, tracking, privacy disclosures, and cookie banner are aligned.
What is Google Consent Mode?
Google Consent Mode is a tracking framework that tells Google tags how to behave based on a user’s cookie consent choices.
For example, if someone accepts advertising cookies, Google may be able to use that data for conversion tracking, remarketing, and campaign optimisation. If they decline, Google adjusts how data is collected and may rely more heavily on modelled conversion data.
What is Google Signals?
Google Signals is a Google Analytics feature that helps with behavioural reporting, cross-device insights, and data associated with signed-in Google users.
After 15 June 2026, Google Signals will no longer be the main control for Google Ads data. Its role will sit within Google Analytics reporting, while Google Ads data will be managed through Consent Mode.
What is the difference between Google Signals and Consent Mode?
Google Signals relates to Google Analytics reporting and user behaviour insights.
Consent Mode controls how Google tags respond to a user’s consent choices, including whether advertising cookies can be used for Google Ads measurement and optimisation.
For businesses, the simplest way to understand the change is this: Google Signals is for GA4 reporting, while Consent Mode is becoming the key control for Google Ads data.
Will my Google Ads conversion tracking be affected?
It may be affected if your Consent Mode setup is incorrect, incomplete, or not aligned with your website’s cookie banner.
Conversion tracking depends on how users provide consent and how your website passes those consent signals to Google. A poor setup can reduce the accuracy of conversion data, which may affect campaign reporting and optimisation.
Do Australian businesses need Google Consent Mode?
Australian businesses running Google Ads should review their Consent Mode setup, especially if they collect user data through website tags, cookies, remarketing, or conversion tracking.
Consent Mode is particularly important for businesses that advertise to users in regions with strict privacy requirements, including the EU and UK. In Australia, businesses should also make sure their privacy policy clearly explains how website data, cookies, and advertising tools are used.
Do I need to update my website privacy policy?
Possibly. If your website uses Google Ads, GA4, remarketing, conversion tracking, or advertising cookies, your privacy policy should clearly explain how user data may be collected and used.
This is especially important if your website activity may be linked with Google advertising services or signed-in Google user data. Businesses should seek legal advice to confirm whether their privacy policy and cookie consent wording are suitable.
What happens if I do nothing before 15 June 2026?
Your ads should continue running, but your tracking setup may not be as clear or reliable as it should be.
The risk is not that your campaigns will suddenly stop. The bigger issue is that your consent settings, cookie banner, privacy policy, and Google Ads tracking may not be properly aligned. This can affect conversion measurement, campaign optimisation, and data clarity.
How can Concept Designs &amp; Marketing help?
Concept Designs &amp; Marketing helps businesses review their Google Ads, GA4, conversion tracking, and consent mode setup so their digital marketing foundations are cleaner and easier to manage.
As Google Ads data controls continue to evolve, having the right tracking structure in place can support stronger reporting, better campaign decisions, and more reliable marketing performance.

#### Google Analytics 4 is Rolling Out &#8211; What Are You Doing to Prepare?
It is time to say ‘goodbye’ to Universal Analytics and ‘hello’ to Google Analytics 4 (GA4). By July next year, Universal Google Analytics will be obsolete and everyone will need to be using GA4. So how are you preparing for this transition?

As an experienced digital marketing agency on the Gold Coast and in Sydney, we’ll use this article to shed some light on Google Analytics 4 and give you some tips on how you can prepare for the upcoming shift.
Why The Change?
Universal Analytics served its purpose for a while, but it can no longer handle modern analytical needs.
Since Universal Analytics’ conception, the internet has changed so drastically. People are using many different types of devices to access the internet, and many new privacy and date laws have been introduced, among many other changes.
For these reasons, Google has built a completely new analytical tool, and GA4 will be able to provide in-depth and accurate analytics for businesses around the world.
Making The Shift
GA4 is already here, and you can move your business over any time before July 2023 (when Universal Analytics will be shut down).
In the past, when updates were made to Universal Analytics, all that was required was a simple migration and change of code. But since GA4 is not an upgrade but an entirely new platform, the shift will be a little more complicated. And that is why it is important that you do not wait until the last minute.
It is recommended that you run both programs simultaneously for a couple of months to make the transition easier.
What Enhancements Does GA4 Offer?
Because GA4 is not just an upgrade of Universal Analytics and is an entirely new platform, you can expect a lot of changes. But at the end of the day, there is nothing that Universal Analytics can do that GA4 won’t be able to do.
GA4 has a major focus on trends and patterns. It will use sample sizes of your audience to provide you with accurate predictions of the success of your current digital marketing efforts and so much more. You can also expect to enjoy enhanced measurement features that give you details on scrolling, clicks and pop-ups.
Tips For Making The Transition To GA4

Transition sooner rather than later.
Be patient, as it will take a while to get the hang of GA4.
If you are currently using code that is 5-10 years old, you’ll need to set up GA4 as its own separate platform.
If you’re using updated code, you can connect the two platforms.
Using Google Tag Manager will simplify the process and help you collect data.

#### Google Is Phasing Out Call Campaigns: What It Means for Your Business
If your business relies on phone enquiries, you may have heard that Google is phasing out Call Campaigns by 2027. While this might sound concerning at first, the reality is that there are strong alternatives already available and most businesses will be able to transition smoothly.

What Are Call Campaigns?
Call Campaigns are a type of Google Ads campaign designed specifically to drive phone calls. Instead of directing users to a website, these ads encourage people to call your business directly from search results.
They’ve been particularly popular with service-based businesses such as plumbers, electricians, and professional services where a phone call is often the fastest path to conversion.
What’s Changing?
Google has announced that:

No new Call Campaigns will be able to be created
Existing Call Campaigns will continue to run for now
All Call Campaigns will be phased out by 2027

This means businesses currently relying on them will need to plan a transition over the next couple of years.
Why Is Google Making This Change?
While Google hasn’t provided one single reason, the shift aligns with broader trends in digital advertising:

More automation
Google is moving towards campaign types that use machine learning to optimise performance across multiple channels.
Broader campaign formats
Campaigns like Performance Max allow ads to appear across Search, Display, YouTube, and more, rather than being limited to one format.
Improved tracking and insights
Newer campaign types provide better visibility into how users interact before converting, not just the final action.

What This Means for Your Business
If you rely heavily on phone leads, this change is important, but it’s not a step backwards.
What you may notice over time:

A shift away from single-purpose campaigns
More emphasis on multi-channel visibility
Greater focus on the full customer journey

The key is to ensure your strategy still prioritises phone enquiries, even if the campaign type changes.
What Are the Alternatives?
There are several effective options already available:

Search Campaigns with call assets
These allow users to call directly from your ads while still supporting website visits.
Performance Max campaigns
These can drive leads across multiple placements, including calls, while using Google’s automation to optimise results.
Landing pages designed for calls
Clear messaging, click-to-call buttons, and strong calls to action can significantly improve phone conversions.
Local SEO and Google Business Profile optimisation
Many phone enquiries come directly from search listings and maps, not just paid ads.

The Bottom Line
Google phasing out Call Campaigns is part of a broader shift towards more integrated and automated advertising. While the change requires some adjustment, it also opens up new opportunities to improve lead quality and visibility.
The most important thing is to plan ahead and ensure your lead generation strategy continues to support how your customers prefer to contact you.
If you’d like help reviewing your current campaigns or planning the transition, Concept Designs &amp; Marketing is here to help. Book in a consultation today to get started.
Frequently Asked Questions
1. What are Google Call Campaigns?
Google Call Campaigns are a type of ad that encourages users to call your business directly from search results instead of visiting a website.
2. Is Google removing Call Campaigns completely?
Yes. Google is phasing them out, with no new campaigns allowed and existing ones expected to be discontinued by 2027.
3. When will Call Campaigns stop working?
Existing campaigns will continue for now, but all Call Campaigns are scheduled to be phased out by 2027.
4. Why is Google phasing out Call Campaigns?
Google is shifting towards more automated and flexible campaign types that can deliver results across multiple channels and provide better tracking.
5. Will this affect businesses that rely on phone leads?
Yes, especially if Call Campaigns are a key part of your strategy. However, there are effective alternatives available that can still generate phone enquiries.
6. What is the best alternative to Call Campaigns?
Search campaigns with call assets are one of the most direct alternatives, allowing users to call your business from ads while still supporting website visits.
7. Can Performance Max campaigns generate phone calls?
Yes. Performance Max campaigns can drive phone enquiries while also increasing visibility across Google’s network.
8. How can I continue getting phone enquiries without Call Campaigns?
By using a mix of Search campaigns with call features, strong landing pages with click-to-call options, and optimised Google Business Profiles.
9. Should I stop using Call Campaigns now?
Not necessarily. They can still perform well, but it’s a good idea to start testing alternative campaign types before the phase-out.
10. Do I need to change my entire Google Ads strategy?
Not entirely, but you may need to adjust your approach to ensure your campaigns continue to generate phone leads effectively.

#### Hashtags 101 For Social Media Marketing
Social media marketing is an ever-changing landscape, and it is difficult to always be on point with the latest updates and trends. It is vital to keep on track as your social media pages attract customers and promote your online profile.

One of the least understood tools for Instagram marketing and LinkedIn lead generation is the effective use of hashtags. Read on to find out more about the effective use of this social media marketing tool.
How Many Hashtags Should You Use?
In Instagram marketing, you can use up to 30 hashtags. Any included after that will not feature in any searches. Yes, you can, but you should have a baseline of at least 15-20 hashtags.
What Sort Of Hashtags Should You Use?
Randomly throwing out 30 hashtags is not the way to go. Instead, you should structure your selection of hashtags according to this basic minimum guideline:

Include 3 &#8211; 5 popular hashtags (popular means those with 300 000 to 1 million posts). Exclude any hashtags over the 1 million mark, as these can open you up to unsolicited messages from spambots.
Add 3 &#8211; 5 well-used hashtags (in the range of 80 000 to 300 000 posts)
Now come up with 3-5 hashtags specific to your offering and are directly related to your product or service, bearing in mind what your customer will be searching for.
Lastly, include up to 2 hashtags of your branding.

If you are thinking of using a specific hashtag, you can check its popularity ranking by typing it into the search bar. Then click on the # symbol in the tabs at the top to get an overview of the number of times it has been used.
How To Choose Appropriate Hashtags
Frequently companies choose the wrong or overused hashtags for their posts that are not going to get hits. You need to expand your thinking out of the box for lateral connections to your type of business. Think of situations that users would find themselves in that would lead them to need your kind of product or service.
Hashtags on Instagram can be included in the caption or comments ? either will work. Hashtags are often included in the comments to prevent the post from having the appearance of being spam.
Cross-posting to Facebook will result in the same hashtags used on these posts, making your post more searchable. For direct posts on Facebook, you can apply the same formula of hashtags as outlined above.
Personally branded hashtags and niche hashtags followed by your ideal audience are two of the best hashtags to use on LinkedIn, preferably at the bottom of your posts (not in the comments).  In addition to your company page, you can add up to 5 hashtags on your personal profile using creator mode.
One or two Twitter hashtags are enough and should be easy to remember and easy to spell (not all in CAPS) for optimum effect. Try sticking to one topic per tweet. The best hashtags will elicit a response, so not necessarily your brand hashtag.
Through Instagram marketing and LinkedIn lead generation, you can successfully drive customers to your website. This is the ultimate goal as your website is one of your most significant business assets.  Social media marketing allows you to connect with your customers, generate awareness and increase sales.
If you are searching for a social media marketing agency, contact Concept Designs &amp; Marketing today. We create highly functional and visually appealing social media pages for top class Instagram marketing and LinkedIn lead generation.

#### How AI Is Changing the Way Buyers Research Businesses
The way buyers research businesses has shifted, and it’s happening faster than many organisations realise. Instead of starting with a Google search and clicking through multiple websites, buyers are increasingly turning to AI tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Copilot, and Google AI Overviews to ask questions, explore options, and narrow down choices.

This change isn’t about convenience alone. It reflects a deeper shift in how people want to make decisions. Buyers want clarity, context, and confidence early in the process, and AI tools are designed to provide exactly that.
From Searching to Asking
Traditional search required buyers to translate their needs into keywords. AI search allows them to ask full questions in plain language. Buyers are no longer just searching for “IT support Sydney” or “commercial builder Brisbane.” They are asking things like, “Who are the best managed IT providers for growing businesses?” or “What should I look for in a commercial builder?”
AI tools respond by summarising information, highlighting considerations, and often referencing businesses they believe are relevant and credible. This means research is happening in conversation form, not through lists of links.
AI Is Influencing Buyers Earlier
One of the most significant changes is how early AI appears in the buyer journey. AI tools are being used before buyers visit websites, fill out forms, or speak to sales teams. By the time a buyer reaches out, they may already have a shortlist, a budget expectation, and a clear understanding of what they want.
For businesses, this means visibility needs to happen earlier. If your business is not present in those AI-generated answers, you may never enter the buyer’s consideration set.
Trust and Authority Matter More Than Ever
AI tools are selective. They prioritise clarity, consistency, and authority when generating responses. Businesses with well-structured content, clear messaging, and demonstrated expertise are more likely to be referenced or recommended.
This is why simply producing more content is not enough. Buyers and AI tools alike respond to depth, relevance, and trust signals. Content needs to answer real questions and demonstrate understanding, not just promote services.
What This Means for Lead Generation
AI is changing not just how buyers research, but the quality of leads businesses receive. When buyers come via AI tools, they are often better informed and more decisive. They have already done the groundwork.
This leads to fewer time-wasting enquiries and more meaningful conversations. Businesses that adapt their content and visibility strategies to align with AI-driven research are seeing stronger lead quality and improved conversion rates.
Responding Strategically, Not Reactively
The biggest mistake businesses can make is treating AI search as a trend to watch rather than a shift to act on. Buyers are already using these tools. The question is whether your business is visible when they do.
By focusing on clarity, authority, and content that aligns with how buyers ask questions, businesses can position themselves where modern research now begins.
FAQs: AI Buyer Research and Search Behaviour
1. How are buyers using AI tools to research businesses?
Buyers use AI tools to ask questions, compare providers, and understand options before visiting websites. AI search often replaces early Google searches.
2. Do people use ChatGPT and Perplexity to find service providers?
Yes. Many users ask AI tools to recommend or shortlist businesses, especially in B2B and professional services.
3. What types of businesses are most affected by AI search?
B2B businesses, professional services, franchisors, and high-value service providers are most impacted due to longer research and decision cycles.
4. How do AI tools influence buyer trust?
AI tools influence trust by summarising information and referencing businesses that appear credible, consistent, and authoritative.
5. Can AI search improve lead quality?
Yes. Leads influenced by AI search are often more informed and closer to making a decision, resulting in higher-quality enquiries.
6. How should businesses adapt their content for AI-driven research?
Businesses should focus on answering real buyer questions, structuring content clearly, and building authority across key service areas.

The way people search for information is evolving rapidly. If your business has relied on Google SEO and Ads to drive traffic, you may have noticed some major shifts: fewer clicks, increased competition, and the rise of AI-driven search results. 40% of Gen Z users now prefer TikTok or AI-powered search over Google.
AI tools summarise answers instantly, reducing the need for users to visit websites.
Google is integrating AI-generated search results to compete with AI tools.

So, what does this mean for your business? You need an adaptive strategy that ensures your brand remains visible across both AI search and traditional search engines.
How AI Search Works Differently from Google
Unlike Google’s search algorithm, which ranks websites based on SEO factors, AI search generates direct responses by pulling from multiple sources. This means that traditional ranking tactics may no longer be enough to secure a strong presence in AI-driven search results.
Key Differences Between AI Search and Traditional Search:

AI tools focus on summarising answers rather than driving users to external websites.
Authoritative and well-cited content is prioritised over traditional SEO-optimised pages.
Multi-platform presence matters more than ever, as AI engines pull from sources such as LinkedIn, and industry news sites rather than relying solely on website rankings.

#### How Can I Make My Website Content More Visible in AI Search Tools?
As AI-powered search tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google’s AI Overviews become increasingly prevalent, the way users discover information online is evolving. These platforms aim to provide direct, concise answers by summarising content from various sources, often reducing the need for users to click through to individual websites. For businesses, this shift means that traditional SEO strategies may no longer be sufficient to maintain online visibility.

1. Understand How AI Platforms Source Information
AI search tools rely on large datasets and trusted sources to generate responses. These sources often include:

Wikipedia
Government and educational websites
Authoritative industry publications
High-quality, well-structured websites

Ensuring your content is present and cited in these types of sources can increase the likelihood of being referenced by AI tools.
2. Optimise Content Structure for AI Comprehension
AI models favour content that is easy to interpret and extract information from. To enhance your content’s visibility:

Use Clear Headings and Subheadings: Organise content with descriptive headings to delineate sections.
Incorporate Bullet Points and Lists: Break down complex information into digestible points.
Implement FAQ Sections: Address common questions in a straightforward Q&amp;A format.
Apply Schema Markup: Use structured data (e.g., FAQ, How-To) to help AI understand the context of your content.

3. Build Authority and Trustworthiness
AI platforms prioritise content from sources that demonstrate expertise and credibility. To establish your website as a trusted source:

Publish High-Quality, Original Content: Provide valuable insights and information that reflect your expertise.
Earn Backlinks from Reputable Sites: Seek opportunities to have your content referenced by authoritative websites.
Maintain Up-to-Date Information: Regularly review and update content to ensure accuracy.

4. Embrace Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO)
Generative Engine Optimisation focuses on enhancing content visibility within AI-generated search results. Key GEO strategies include:

Creating AI-Friendly Content: Develop content that addresses specific queries and provides clear answers.
Ensuring Content is Citable: Structure content so that AI tools can easily reference and attribute information.
Monitoring AI Search Performance: Track how your content is represented in AI results and make necessary adjustments.

Are You Ready to Adapt?
As AI continues to reshape the digital landscape, adapting your content strategy is essential. By understanding how AI platforms source and present information, and by implementing structured, authoritative, and AI-friendly content, you can enhance your website’s visibility and ensure your business remains discoverable in this new era of search.

Frequently Asked Questions
1. How do AI search tools find content online?
AI search tools utilise large datasets and trusted sources, such as Wikipedia and government websites, to generate responses. They prioritise content that is well-structured and authoritative.
2 What kind of websites are most trusted by AI?
Websites that demonstrate expertise, authority, and trustworthiness — such as educational institutions, government agencies, and reputable industry publications — are commonly referenced by AI platforms.
3. Does AI use live web data like Google?
While traditional search engines crawl the web in real-time, many AI tools rely on pre-existing datasets and may not access the most current web content unless specifically designed to do so.
4. Why is my content not appearing in AI search summaries?
If your content lacks clear structure, authority, or is not cited by trusted sources, AI platforms may overlook it when generating summaries.
5. How can I increase the chances of my content being summarised by AI?
Enhance content structure with clear headings, bullet points, and FAQs; implement schema markup; and build authority through high-quality content and reputable backlinks.
6. Do AI tools always show the original source of the information?
Not always. Some AI platforms may provide summaries without direct attribution, while others, like Perplexity AI, include source links for transparency.
7. What is schema markup and how does it help?
Schema markup is a form of structured data that helps search engines and AI understand the context of your content, improving visibility in search results.
8. Is Google still relevant if AI is summarising everything?
Yes, Google remains a significant player in search. However, integrating strategies that cater to both traditional and AI-driven search platforms is becoming increasingly important.
9. Can small businesses compete with big brands in AI search?
Absolutely. By focusing on niche expertise, producing high-quality content, and building authority, small businesses can achieve visibility in AI search results.
10. How often should I update my content for AI visibility?
Regularly review and update your content to maintain accuracy and relevance, which can positively influence your visibility in AI-generated search results.

#### How Clever Use of Directories Can Boost Your SEO
Using directories has always been an important part of boosting SEO. In the past, listing your website on directories could have been all that was needed to optimise your website for search engine rankings.
Today, however, things are a little different.
The algorithms of Google and other search engines have adapted to place less value on directory listings. So while these still feature as a core component of just about any comprehensive SEO strategy, you should never rely solely on directories to get your website onto page one. Make no mistake; you can still use directories to get an edge on your competitors… but you have to be smart about it. Here’s how.
Be Selective
Previously, the majority of SEO strategies concentrated on getting the targeted website onto as many directories as possible. And yes, this worked – in the past. Now, more than ever, quality beats quantity. Search engines often penalise websites that appear on an unrealistic number of directories, especially if those directories are known for being poor quality.
To ensure your directory listings are benefitting your SEO rather than harming it, you should be careful to list your website on directories that:

Have strong reputations
Match the location of your business
Are relevant to your company and industry.
When possible, seek out niche directories that align with your business rather than aiming for broad or unrelated directories. For example, if you were a Gold Coast electrician, a listing on a trades directory in South East Queensland would be far more valuable than five listings on general, non-location-based directories.
Work on Your Website First

The modern, high-quality directories you should be looking for will typically be monitored and edited by a person. This means getting accepted by these directories depends heavily on one thing: your website being accessible to people. If the directory manager can visit your website and easily read and navigate through all your pages, they should have no hesitation in listing your business.
If your current website looks cluttered, outdated, or unprofessional, it is essential you give it a makeover before approaching the directories that could be the key to improving your SEO.

#### How Do AI Platforms Find and Summarise Online Content?
AI-powered search tools are changing the way we access information. Rather than presenting a list of blue links, platforms like ChatGPT, Perplexity AI, and Google’s Overviews (SGE) aim to deliver direct, concise answers. But how exactly do these tools find your content, and what makes it worthy of being summarised?

1. AI Doesn’t Search the Web Like Google
Google sends out crawlers to index web pages and then ranks them based on relevance, authority, and keyword signals. In contrast, AI search tools rely on a different process. They’re often trained on large datasets and use natural language processing (NLP) to understand and generate human-like responses.
2. AI Tools Use Trusted Data Sources
Instead of crawling every page on the web in real-time, AI tools tend to pull from what they “know”, which often means referencing well-known, high-authority, and structured sources. These might include:

Wikipedia
Government and educational websites
Authoritative industry blogs
Sites with strong SEO and E-E-A-T (Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, Trustworthiness)

Some tools also access real-time information through APIs or partnerships with search engines, databases, and news platforms.
3. Structured Content Gets Noticed
AI tools are more likely to extract content from sites that are easy to interpret. This means:

Clear headings and subheadings
Lists, bullet points, and summaries
FAQ sections with question-and-answer formats
Schema markup to signal important information to machines

The clearer your content structure, the more likely AI is to select and summarise it accurately.
4. AI Summarisation Isn’t Perfect
Generative AI tools often paraphrase, summarise, or even “hallucinate” content. Meaning, they might generate information that sounds plausible but isn’t accurate. That’s why it’s crucial to ensure your content is fact-checked, well-cited, and easy to interpret. The more structured and trustworthy your content, the better chance it has of being referenced accurately.
5. The Opportunity for Businesses
To be visible in AI search results, businesses must start thinking beyond Google rankings. Instead, focus on:

Publishing high-authority, structured content
Getting cited in third-party trusted sources
Implementing schema markup
Building your brand’s reputation across multiple platforms

This new landscape rewards content that’s useful, trustworthy, and easy for AI to understand and summarise.
All that said, AI search tools are changing how content is found, understood and shared with users. While it&#8217;s not enough to just publish good content, by focusing on clear formatting, authoritative sources, and strategic optimisation, you increase the chance of your expertise being accurately summarised and surfaced in AI search results.
At Concept Designs &amp; Marketing, we help businesses adapt their strategies for this evolving landscape. Curious about how well your website is set up for AI search? Try our AI Visibility Calculator to find out now.
Frequently Asked Questions About How AI Platforms Find &#038; Summarise Content

How do AI search tools find content online?
AI platforms rely on structured, high-authority sources and datasets, rather than indexing the entire web like traditional search engines.
What kind of websites are most trusted by AI?
Sites with government, educational, or industry authority, and those with strong E-E-A-T signals, are commonly referenced by AI.
Does AI use live web data like Google?
Some AI platforms pull real-time data via APIs or partnerships, but most rely on previously trained data or curated sources.
Why is my content not appearing in AI search summaries?
Your content may not be well-structured, authoritative, or widely cited, which limits its visibility to AI platforms.
How can I increase the chances of my content being summarised by AI?
Use clear headings, FAQs, schema markup, and ensure your content is accurate, well-cited, and valuable.
Do AI tools always show the original source of the information?
Not always. Some summarise without citing, while others like Perplexity AI provide source links for transparency.
What is schema markup and how does it help?
Schema is code that helps machines understand content. It boosts clarity and visibility for AI search tools.
Is Google still relevant if AI is summarising everything?
Yes, Google remains a key source of indexed content that AI platforms often pull from.
Can small businesses compete with big brands in AI search?
Yes. By producing niche, expert content and getting cited on trusted platforms, small businesses can stand out.
How often should I update my content for AI visibility?
Regular updates help keep your information relevant, improve accuracy, and increase your chances of being cited.

#### How Do I Get Cited in AI Search Results?
As AI search tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity become more common, businesses are asking a new question: How do I get my content referenced by these platforms?

Unlike Google, which ranks pages by links, keywords, and technical SEO, AI platforms use a more nuanced approach. They’re looking for trusted, high-quality information they can summarise and cite. So, if you want to show up in AI-generated responses, you need to position your business as a credible source of information.
Step 1: Be Citable
Make your website a source worth quoting. This means publishing original, fact-checked content that demonstrates your expertise. Think articles, whitepapers, and FAQs: content that helps answer real questions. AI platforms prefer clear, structured information that’s easy to summarise and extract.
Step 2: Get Published in Trusted Sources
AI search tools are trained on a wide range of content, but not all sources are treated equally. If your business is mentioned in media outlets, online publications, or respected industry blogs, it increases your chance of being cited. Consider guest posting, collaborating with journalists, or contributing to online discussions in your industry.
Step 3: Leverage Wikipedia and Industry Directories
Although you can’t control Wikipedia directly, being referenced there (or having your own page) increases visibility in large language models. Similarly, citations in government sites, university databases, or high-authority directories improve your discoverability.
Step 4: Use Structured Data
Schema markup, especially FAQ and How-To schemas, helps AI tools understand and extract your content more efficiently. It’s not just about SEO anymore: it’s about being machine-readable for AI interpretation.
Step 5: Build a Personal and Business Profile
AI tools don’t just cite websites &#8211; they cite people and businesses. Building your LinkedIn presence, writing thought leadership pieces, and being active in online forums can help AI platforms recognise you as a subject-matter expert.
Final Thought
Getting cited in AI search isn’t about tricking the algorithm. It’s about being genuinely helpful, credible, and easy to quote. The more useful and visible your content is across the web, the more likely AI is to reference it.
Now’s the time to assess your readiness. Take our free AI Visibility Score to see how well your business shows up in AI-driven search and where you could improve.
FAQ’s
1. What does it mean to be cited in AI search? 
Being cited means AI platforms reference your content or business when generating responses to user queries.
2. Why do AI tools cite some businesses over others? 
AI tools reference content from sources they deem trustworthy, such as news outlets, blogs, or government and educational sites.
3. How can I make my content more likely to be quoted by AI? 
Publish clear, factual, and useful information. Use structured data and ensure your site is technically sound.
4. Do backlinks still matter for AI citation? 
Indirectly. They help boost domain authority, which can influence how your site is viewed by AI systems.
5. Will being on Wikipedia help? 
Yes, many AI models use Wikipedia as a reliable training source.
6. What’s better: citations from websites or social media? 
Website citations, especially from trusted sources, carry more weight in most AI training data.
7. Is structured data important for AI citations? 
Yes, schema markup like FAQ or How-To helps AI easily interpret and extract your content.
8. Can AI quote a person instead of a website? 
Yes, especially if that person has a strong digital footprint and credibility in their field.
9. Do press releases help with AI visibility? 
They can, especially if picked up by credible publications that AI models reference.
10. Should I focus on being useful or ranking? 
Focus on being useful. AI search tools reward helpful, well-structured content over keyword-stuffed pages.

#### How Local SEO Is Different To Regular SEO
SEO (Search Engine Optimisation) is the practice of working on your website’s content and link portfolio to increase its chance of being discovered online organically. In other words, if a potential customer looks for something related to your business on Google (or any other search engine) and they see a link to your website, this is a sign of good SEO.
But what is local SEO and how is it different from standard SEO? Here’s a look at what sets this service apart and a guide to determining which type is the best fit for your marketing strategy.
What’s The Difference
General SEO doesn’t care too much about a browser’s geographic location. If someone in Cairns finds your website on Google, that’s valuable. If a person in the US discovers you online, that’s great too. Think of this as ‘global SEO’ – it helps your website rank well for generic searches.
Local SEO, as the name suggests, is very much focused on getting your website onto the screens of people in your area (as well as any other areas you target). This could encompass a state or territory, a city, or even a specific suburb. The overarching aim of local SEO is informing Google and other search engines that your website is the ideal destination for people who search for your keywords in a particular place or region.
Which SEO Should You Target?
This depends entirely on your business model. If your main source of revenue is your physical shopfront, local SEO will most likely provide the most benefits. On the other hand, if your website has e-commerce features and you can ship around the globe, more generalised SEO tactics are likely to work best. And if your business has a fair mix of both in-store and online transactions, it makes sense to use a little bit of both.
For example, a hairdresser with just one location on the Gold Coast should definitely turn to local SEO to reach people in the relevant suburbs. However, a hair product seller that delivers anywhere in Australia would benefit from a broader SEO strategy. If you’re unsure about which SEO model would best suit your business, please talk to us.
Local SEO Tactics
In addition to the common tools and approaches generally used for SEO, a digital strategy focused on local SEO will typically involve:

Adding your website to local directories
Creating business profiles for Google+ and Bing
Featuring a map and/or store locator on your website
Creating website pages and external links that target location-specific keywords.

#### How to Avoid Website Domain Transfer Headaches
During the process of acquiring or merging with a business, there are many important tasks on your to-do list, but one often overlooked aspect is the transfer of the business’s domain name. As a web designer who works closely with business owners, I’ve encountered several instances where this crucial step was missed, and it caused significant issues down the line.

Why Domain Transfers Matter
One of the key problems is that if the domain name is still registered under the old business’s ABN, your online presence remains tied to the former business owner. This can create complications in maintaining control over your website, emails, and digital assets. Additionally, it can affect your branding efforts if your online presence is still linked to the previous owner&#8217;s ABN.
Ensuring a Smooth Transfer
If you’ve recently acquired a business or are in the process of doing so, it’s worth double-checking whether the domain has been transferred correctly. It is vital to work with a lawyer who understands the intricacies of business acquisitions to ensure that the domain name is properly transferred to your ABN. While there may be a small cost and some processing time involved, it’s a step you don’t want to overlook.
Support for Your Domain Transfer Needs
A smooth domain transfer is essential for protecting your business’s digital presence and preventing future headaches. #### How to Create a Landing Page That Converts: A Step-by-Step Blueprint
If you’re looking to boost conversions on your website, then a highly effective landing page is a must-have. But what makes a landing page truly effective? It’s not just about having the right ads or traffic. It’s about having a landing page that speaks to your audience’s needs and solves their problems.

At Concept Designs &amp; Marketing, we have been building websites and landing pages for 20+ years. Over that time, have built many landing pages and have developed a landing page blueprint that consists of seven key steps. Rest assured your landing page will have a long-lasting impact on conversion of your audience. Whilst we follow our formula, we also tailor the landing page specific to your audience and business goals.
Step 1: The Hero Section
The hero section is what makes or breaks your landing page. It’s the first thing your audience sees, and you have just seconds to get their attention. Use this section to tell them what you do, why it matters to them, and how they can access those benefits.
Step 2: Problem and Solution
Once you’ve captured your audience’s attention, it’s time to talk about their main problem and how you’re going to solve it. Use the classic “pain, agitate, solution” framework to address their pain points, empathise with them, and offer a clear solution to their problem.
Step 3: Benefits
Differentiate yourself from your competitors by highlighting the unique benefits that only you can offer. We use a three-piece format to present each benefit: title, feature description, and a visual to sum it up.
Step 4: Testimonials
Social proof is a powerful tool in marketing. We use testimonials from satisfied customers to build credibility and trust with your audience. This is the perfect opportunity to embed your Google reviews into your website. This creates a live feed from your Google review, so that when people leave you a 5-star review, it automatically populates onto your landing page.
Step 5: Features
After highlighting the benefits, it’s time to dive into the features of your product or service. This is where we can be descriptive and show how your features make your solution possible.
Step 6: Play the Tape Forward
This section is all about showing your audience what their future could look like if they use your product or service. Here we use storytelling to paint a vivid picture of the results they can expect.
Step 7: FAQs
Address the top questions people would typically ask you over a phone conversation. This is also a great opportunity to include any remaining concerns or questions that your audience may have about your product or service. This helps to remove any remaining barriers to conversion. Plus, to be honest, Google loves FAQ’s on websites.
By following these seven steps, we can create a landing page for your business that speaks directly to your audience’s needs and ultimately drives conversions. Remember your key marketing messages need to always focus on your customer and their pain points. That way you’ll be well on your way to engaging your audience where they need you most.
Ready to create a landing page that converts? Reach out to us today, at Concept Designs &amp; Marketing we are ready to discuss your digital marketing needs, and together, let&#8217;s work to elevate your online presence and drive conversions.

#### How to Create a Real Advantage for Your Business in AI Search
[et_pb_section][et_pb_row][et_pb_column type=&#8221;4_4&#8243;][et_pb_text]Being good at what you do is no longer enough if your business is not being understood and recommended early in the buyer decision-making process.

Buyers now have more ways to research, compare, and validate a business before reaching out. AI tools, voice search, answer engines, and summarised search experiences are helping people ask better questions, explore their options faster, and form opinions earlier.

That means visibility is no longer only about being found. It is also about being clearly understood and confidently recommended.

For many business owners, this creates an important question. How do you actually create an advantage in AI search?

The answer is not to panic, overhaul everything, or chase every new platform. The real opportunity comes from understanding where your business stands now, identifying the gaps, and building a strategy from a place of clarity rather than guesswork.

At Concept Designs &amp; Marketing, that is why we always start with a baseline. Before you can improve your visibility in AI search, you need to know how your business is currently positioned, what signals you are sending to the market, and how that compares with your competitors.

Here are five of the most important areas to assess if you want to build a real advantage in AI search.
1. Current visibility
The first step is getting clear on how visible your business is right now.

This is about more than checking whether your website ranks for a handful of keywords. It means looking at how your business appears across the broader search landscape, including traditional search, AI-generated responses, maps, directories, review platforms, and other channels that influence trust and discovery.

If buyers are asking AI tools for recommendations in your category, would your business be likely to appear in those conversations? If not, why not?

Without a clear view of your current visibility, it is difficult to know what needs to change or where your best opportunities sit.
2. Clarity of messaging
Clear signals matter to AI tools, and they matter just as much to buyers.

If your website and digital presence make it hard to understand what you do, who you help, or what makes your business different, you are making it harder for both people and AI tools to interpret your value.

Clear messaging gives your business a stronger chance of being surfaced accurately. It also helps buyers feel more confident, more quickly.

This is where many businesses lose ground without realising it. Their services are explained too broadly, their positioning sounds similar to everyone else, or their website assumes visitors already know what they need.

Clarity creates advantage because it reduces confusion and strengthens trust.
3. Trust and authority signals
AI search is not just about content. It is also about credibility.

Trust and authority signals include reviews, consistent business information, expert content, third-party mentions, case studies, relevant backlinks, and a strong overall digital footprint.

These signals help shape how your business is perceived, not only by potential customers, but also by the platforms and systems interpreting information about your brand.

A business with stronger trust signals is more likely to be taken seriously. A business with weak or inconsistent signals may struggle to be recommended, even if it offers an excellent service.

That is why building authority online is no longer optional. It is part of how businesses stay visible as buyer behaviour changes.
4. Content and website structure
Many businesses think they need more content. Often, what they really need is better structured content.

Your website should make it easy to understand your services, your locations, your process, and the questions your buyers are already asking. Strong structure helps both human visitors and AI tools interpret what matters on the page.

This includes clear service pages, useful FAQs, logical navigation, clean formatting, and content that reflects the language buyers actually use.

Well-organised content improves your chances of being found, summarised, and trusted. Poorly structured content creates friction, even when the service itself is strong.
5. Competitor positioning
Creating an advantage is not only about looking at your own business. It is also about understanding what the market around you is doing.

How are your competitors describing their services? What trust signals are they building? What kind of content are they publishing? Where are they more visible than you, and where are they vulnerable?

This is one of the most overlooked parts of AI search strategy.

If you do not understand the competitive landscape, it becomes much harder to make accurate decisions. You may invest in the wrong content, focus on the wrong channels, or miss clear opportunities to differentiate your business.

A strong strategy comes from knowing both where you stand and what the market is rewarding.
Where the Real Advantage Starts
Creating an advantage in AI search does not start with a trend. It starts with a baseline.

Once you understand your current visibility, messaging, trust signals, content structure, and competitor positioning, you are in a far stronger position to make smart decisions about what to improve next.

That is the difference between reacting to change and responding strategically.

If your business wants to improve visibility across AI-driven search, the best place to begin is by understanding where you stand now.

At Concept Designs &amp; Marketing, our Market Competitor Analysis and AI Search Audit helps businesses see where they are visible, where they are unclear, where competitors are ahead, and which actions are most likely to create impact. When strategy starts from a place of knowing, it becomes much easier to move forward with clarity and confidence.[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

#### How to Deal With Negative Facebook Reviews
In today&#8217;s digital age, online reviews can make or break a business&#8217;s reputation. But what do you do when those reviews take a negative turn? In this blog post, we&#8217;re diving into the art of handling negative Facebook reviews like a pro. With our expert strategies, you&#8217;ll not only salvage your brand&#8217;s image but also turn these challenges into opportunities for growth.

1. Leverage Notifications for Timely Responses
When it comes to managing your brand&#8217;s reputation, staying in the loop is key. Ensure you&#8217;re notified every time a review lands on your Facebook business page. Timely responses show that you&#8217;re actively engaged and concerned about customer experiences. This simple step can prevent negative feedback from snowballing. 
2. Craft Thoughtful Responses
A negative review shouldn&#8217;t spark a defensive attitude. Instead, address the concerns with empathy. Respond within a few hours, conveying your genuine regret for their experience. A personalised approach can diffuse tension and open a channel for resolution. Remember, 53% of reviewers expect a response within a week, and your professionalism can mend fences
3. Transform Critics into Collaborators
Negative reviews can be your ticket to improvement. Invite disgruntled customers to share more about their experience privately. This proactive step allows for personalised solutions. Moreover, your willingness to address issues head-on demonstrates a commitment to growth and customer satisfaction.
4. Amplify the Positive
Don&#8217;t let the negatives steal the spotlight. Encourage satisfied customers to share their experiences through positive reviews. This will shift the focus away from the occasional negative comments and showcase your dedication to delivering exceptional service.
5. Comply with Community Standards
While you can&#8217;t erase a negative review, you can take action against reviews that breach Facebook&#8217;s community standards. Reporting content that promotes violence, hate speech, or fraud can ensure your platform remains a safe space for genuine feedback.
6. Display Positive Reviews Strategically
Turn your website into a hub of positivity by embedding positive Facebook reviews. The Reviews Feed Pro plugin offers seamless integration, allowing you to showcase your brand&#8217;s shining moments while filtering out the negatives. This not only uplifts your online presence but also converts visitors into potential clients.
Navigating negative reviews isn&#8217;t just about damage control; it&#8217;s a chance to showcase your brand&#8217;s integrity and commitment to customer satisfaction. #### How to engage your ideal client (Pt1)
Do you ever find yourself wondering how to provide engaging content for your ideal client? Here are three tips to first discovering who your ideal client is.
Who are you talking to? Who do you serve? Who do you help?
These are the questions you need to answer when creating content for your customers. If you don’t understand specifically who you are marketing to, then your content will not have the impact it could have.
The truth is every potential customer thinks he or she has challenges no one else has. If your company is able to listen and fix the problem, it plays a very important role in your customer’s life. That is the relationship you need your content to foster.
1, Who is your customer?
First, you need to know your market. Your market is more than a demographic. Your customer is not just a married 30-50 year old male with two kids and an office job. Who you need to think about is Sam. Sam is a 45-year-old man who is a bit bored at work. He has two kids, Sarah aged five and Jason aged seven. He likes to read travel magazines and often daydreams about his next adventure.
Sam is not a demographic. He is an individual who has a story. When you write your content, you need to write to the breathing individual with all their quirks.
2, How are you going to solve your customer’s problem?
What’s not working for Sam and how can you make it work better? A great way to answer this question is by sitting down with a pen and paper or your laptop and note down details of who Sam is. Begin by imagining what kind of person is your ideal customer?
3, What traits make your customer ‘ideal’? 
First, you need to make sure your customer can afford your product and loves it too. Can they write the check or pull out the credit card? Do they see your product as a lifesaver and will they not stop telling their friends all about how helpful it is? Once you’ve got these essentials down pat, it’s time to look at your customer’s traits.
Here are a few key traits to consider:

Are they an introvert or an extrovert?
Are they married or single?
How old are they?
Do they have kids?
Are their kids grown up or still young?
What friends do they have?
What are their hobbies?

Sit down and ask yourself these questions. You may think many of them aren’t relevant to your business. But by thinking about somebody’s hobbies and persona it helps you to not just see them as a demographic but as a living breathing person. When you write your content, imagine that person sitting across the table from you and talking to them about the problems they are having. Are they having a beer or a coffee? Think about what makes sense for your customer and write to it.
