#### How to Generate Leads from Facebook
Now that you know about Lead Generation using Lead Magnets and Landing Pages, let’s have a look at generating leads through social media. Did you know that on Facebook, you can create Ads that are specifically for lead generation?

So what are Facebook Lead Ads?
Facebook Lead Ads lets you create simple forms for potential leads to sign up for your offers. For example, someone might see your Lead Ad on Facebook, and based on your call-to-action, they can sign up or ask for more information such as a price quote, newsletters, or products demos.
Customisable Lead Forms: 
The Lead Forms are customisable so you can select what information you’d like from the users. Choose from a list of questions or create optional custom questions that are specifically related to your business or goal.

Pre-filled Contact Details:
When your Lead Ad is clicked on, customers will see the form with contact information that you have requested pre-filled by Facebook, such as their name, phone number and/ or email address. This makes it easy for people to complete your call-to-action. The pre-filled form is mobile optimised and designed to be quick, simple and with little effort for completion from the user. Customers are also able to update or change the pre-filled information before submitting.
Better Targeting with Audiences:
With the inbound enquiries or sign-ups you gain from the customisable pre-filled form, you can then better target your market by creating Custom or Look-alike Audiences with the contact information, allowing you to remarket to those who are interested, or find new leads who are similar to those users who filled out your form to further grow your database.
Ready to get started?
Before you create a Lead Ad, be sure to have your privacy policy ready as you are collecting their personal information. Of course, you may not share or sell the customer information, and there are certain restrictions on the questions you can ask. You will also need to accept the terms of use (Facebook Policy).

#### How to get the most out of your Facebook and Instagram Carousel Ads
&nbsp;
As the market becomes more saturated, finding a way to stand out among the crowd is difficult. Carousel ads tell a story. They are like movie trailers: capture the audience, show fantastic scenes, but never, ever give away the ending. 
Carousel ads feature 3-5 images, links and headlines on the one ad unit. These ads stand out to readers as they showcase the businesses key features in a story. It is also beneficial for the company as they lower costs per click. Below we will examine how to maximise promotion through carousel ads.
#1: Engage the readers
Just like the start of a great novel, the first thing carousel ads must do is to capture the audience. Start the ad off with an image that grabs the reader’s attention. This image should also list the main messages of the ad in order to get your point across immediately.
#2: Keep them swiping
The goal of the carousel ad it to have the readers swipe for the next image until they have reached the end. One great way of keeping the audience engaged is to give an incomplete image. This gets the reader interested in the rest of the message.
#3: Involve readers
When you watch a movie you feel a part of the plot. In a similar way, make your audience feel a part of the scene by relating the product or service to the lives of the readers. Show images in a sequential order where each image results in an intrigued reaction. Make the story relatable for readers by using common language and humour to involve the audience.
#4: Focus on your market
Put yourself in the shoes of your readers. Give them what they want. Design the ad in a way that speaks to your current and potential market. For example, a shoe manufacturer with a main market of sportspeople should have images of athletes and exercising studios, to suit that ideal clientele.
#5: Keep them guessing
Remember, the main goal of a carousel ad is to lure the audience into wanting to know more. Therefore, the last image on the ad should have a call to action under the “learn more” button. Redirect readers to a landing page so you can build a relationship and potentially capture their information.
If you want to stand out from the crowd, why not consider carousel ads for your business. If you need help establishing your business presence on Facebook, contact us today.

#### How To Improve Your Facebook Video Ads
Have you ever used Facebook Video Ads? Have you already got ads on Facebook, but find that they aren’t as effective as you’d hoped? Here at Concept Designs, we know how influential great Facebook video ads can be – let us show you how to improve your reach and grow your business.
1. Use Facebook tools to tailor your ads to your audience
Use Facebook Insights within your Facebook Ad profile to find your audience’s needs that your business or product can fill. Age, gender, lifestyle, relationship status, education level job title, and even location or the composition of their household income can help you understand your audience.
2. Facebook Ads should capture attention quickly
Use the first five seconds of your ad intentionally. What’s the problem? How can you fix it? Strong text, great visuals and a catchy audio will help; generally audio is muted until the user clicks on the ad, and you want to engage them to continue watching.
3. Create Ads that don’t look like ads
Facebook is a social platform- create an easily-shareable ad that is unique, insightful, contains humour or news, and is not too commercially orientated.
4. What’s your message, and how long should it be?
Take about 30 seconds to deliver your message, though if your ad is particularly unique or insightful, up to two minutes may be appropriate. Think about the five W’s:
Who – are you talking to?
What – are you offering?
When – is your product limited or always available?
Where – can people find your product?
Why – does your product fill someone’s need?
5. Create different ads for different audience segments
Create separate ads for different audience awareness of your brand. For new clients/users, build their awareness: be simple and leave them wanting to know more. For people who know about your brand but aren’t yet customers, focus on the additional features or benefits that make your business beat the competition.
6. Run A/B tests to Optimize ads
An A/B test is creating two nearly identical versions of the same video, and testing both on your Facebook page to see which one is more successful.  Split your ads into sections, change just one section, and see which one performs better. Once you have the winner, create another version of the same ad, making another small change, and see which is preferred.

#### How to Repurpose Video Content across many platforms and into many forms of Valuable Content
Creating quality content is a high-demand in this digital age. So repurposing Videos into many forms of valuable content is a great way to increase your engagement through different media and on all your social media platforms.
Here are the different types of content you can produce through your Videos:
1. Plan and Outline your Video Campaign
The first step is to decide the type of video content to create. Then, create both stand-alone and a series of ideas focused on exploring a particular topic. This method would allow you to create an expectation from your audience and turn the video series to a great content asset.
Listed below are a few ideas to inspire you in making your own video series:
&#8211; A line-up of industry experts being interviewed for a particular topic in a video series
&#8211; Create a webinar series sharing tips, tactics, and the latest news related in your industry. Aside from having more content on your website, this also helps you build your position as a trusted source in your industry.
&#8211; FAQs! Written FAQs can also be turned into videos, and what’s best about this is you can feature your employees and customers to increase you and your company’s credibility.
&#8211; Interview customers. It’s great to hear their feedback on your product and services. And to even let them share one to two tips.

Once you’ve outlined and planned your series, make sure to make time for recording each episode based on your scheduled posts for this series. And if you have plans to get a few guests involved, you can always use tools such as Calendly and Zoom to make things easier. However, set and finalise time slots for the interview and have all the information you require completed before the set date (full name, website, contact email, contact number, etc).
As for Calendly, send a link to your guests and let them choose the time and date that works best for them. You can also use this to encourage engagement from your audience and customers and have them participate in interviews. Just embed the link to a landing page or post.
2. Record and Edit your Video
This can be a bit intimidating as a lot of people use high-end equipment to produce high-quality videos. However, smartphones and cameras will do just fine. You can build up while progressing.
To help you doing in-house video campaigns, you’ll be needing two tools: one for recording and one for editing.
Recording tools:
A number of video recording tools can be used for this. However, there are still a few recommended tools depending on the type of video content you choose.
For example, with interviews, you can use Skype or Hangouts on Air with Youtube Live that allows you to engage with your audience in real-time.
For individual shots, you can use Youtube Live. As for Webinars, a lot of reliable tools are available like Click Meeting, Livestream, WebinarJam, and more.
Editing tools:
For Mac users, iMovie is a great option as it’s easy to use. But Youtube Editor (online tool) is also a great tool accessible to everybody. Both have all the basic features for editing such as trimming, audio extraction, transitions, and much more.
As for creating intros or custom thumbnails, use Canva. This online tool allows you to save your templates and simply edit them as you go.
Marketing Tip: Keep dimension of the image at 1280 x 720 in minimum.
And keep in mind to save all your images as a separate file. This would allow you to access them easier and reuse them for your other content later on.
3. Research Keywords for Individual Landing Pages
For each video created, assets are produced for at least 3 landing pages you can optimise for these top three video search engines: Youtube Video Page, Blog post page, and Soundcloud podcast episode page.
Getting ranked for important keywords with these engines in Google is vital as it will help you drive more people to your business and increase traffic on your website.
Add original content, meaning titles and descriptions, for each landing page. The odds of search engines ranking you for these keywords is higher as they prioritise original content.
As each landing page requires original content, it’s also best to create a different name for each asset. However, this can cause a bit of a problem as these landing pages are basically one &#8211; just differently worded.
Marketing Tip: There’s a tool called Serpstat. It has a “Cluster Research Tool” that helps you find alternate terms and phrases to use on your titles. As more results overlap each other, the more related the search queries will be.

Publishing Video to Youtube

&#8211; A maximum of 500 characters can be divided into as many tags as you can use.
&#8211; Create playlists to help your audience find related videos from your channel.
&#8211; Always create eye-catching customised thumbnails. The best image size to use is 1280 x 72o pixels.

#### How To Save 30% With Meta Ads
Earlier this year, Apple updated its App Store policies, and one of the most significant changes affecting businesses is the increased service fee for in-app transactions, including advertising purchases. This change means advertisers who buy Meta ads from within the Meta app on iOS devices are looking at a 30% surcharge added to their costs.

What Is the 30% Surcharge?
The 30% surcharge applies when Meta ads are purchased through in-app transactions on iOS devices. This is due to Apple’s policy of taking a 30% cut on in-app purchases made through the App Store. For businesses buying ads through the Meta app on an iPhone or iPad, this surcharge will now be included in the overall ad cost. As digital marketers, we know that every dollar spent on advertising needs to count, so for businesses managing ad budgets carefully, this fee increase could have a major impact on ROI.
But here’s the good news: we’ve identified five ways to manage and run your Meta ads effectively while avoiding the 30% surcharge.
1. Use Meta Ads Manager on Desktop
The most straightforward way to avoid Apple’s extra fees is by managing and purchasing your Meta ads through the Meta Ads Manager on a desktop browser. By accessing Ads Manager via a web browser, you bypass the App Store altogether, meaning you won’t incur Apple’s 30% fee. Not only will you avoid the surcharge, but you’ll also have access to more advanced targeting, ad optimisation tools, and reporting features that are not always available in the mobile app.
2. Use Meta Business Suite
Meta Business Suite, accessible via both desktop and mobile web browsers, allows you to manage your Facebook and Instagram campaigns without using the iOS app. This tool gives you a comprehensive view of your ad performance and allows you to adjust budgets, audiences, and creatives—again, without the risk of Apple’s 30% surcharge.
3. Avoid In-App Purchases on iOS Devices
A simple yet effective strategy: avoid making any Meta ad purchases directly through the iOS app. Whether you’re tempted to boost a post or purchase ads within the app for convenience, these purchases will come with that additional fee. By sticking to desktop or mobile web browsers, you can steer clear of these extra costs.
4. Set Up Auto-Billing in Ads Manager
To make sure you never inadvertently incur Apple’s 30% fee, set up auto-billing within Meta Ads Manager on a desktop. This way, your ad spend will be processed automatically through the web-based system rather than the mobile app, ensuring that all charges remain fee-free. Setting up auto-billing also simplifies the ad management process and prevents accidental in-app transactions.
5. Keep an Eye on Billing Settings
Another way to avoid the surcharge is to regularly check your billing settings within Ads Manager. Ensure that all payments are set to go through desktop transactions and not mobile in-app purchases. This habit can help you catch any billing issues before they lead to unnecessary fees.
The 30% surcharge on Meta ads purchased through Apple’s App Store doesn’t have to eat into your ad budget. By managing your ads through desktop browsers, using Meta Business Suite, and avoiding in-app purchases, you can keep your costs down and ensure you’re getting the most value from your advertising dollars.

Contact us today for a consultation to discuss managing your Meta ads effectively without the additional costs. You can also learn more about our social media marketing services to boost your online presence and reach your business goals.

#### How to Set Up Your IGTV Channel
Instagram released IGTV last June 2018. It’s a new app for watching 10-minute to hour-long videos of your favourite Instagram creators. Even though it’s a stand-alone app, videos uploaded in IGTV can still be seen and watched from within Instagram &#8211; meaning everyone using Instagram can use it.
If you’ve been using Instagram as one of the main platforms to reach your audience, IVTV is an extension of it. Below we&#8217;ll walk you through what you need to know to add it to your marketing platforms.
#1: Setting up an IGTV Channel
One of the great features about IGTV is that it’s accessible and functional on your desktop. So you can set it up on either your mobile phone or desktop.

* Creating your Channel through your Mobile
a. Download the free IGTV app on your mobile phone (the app is compatible with iOS and Android).
b. Then, open IGTV app and connect your private or business Instagram account.
c. The next step is to set up your channel, so tap on your profile photo and select CREATE CHANNEL from the pop-up menu.
d. Then, follow the prompts to finish the primary set up of your channel.
e. Once you&#8217;re connected, your Instagram account information will automatically be uploaded on your channel and you’ll be asked to upload a video.
* Create your Channel via a Laptop or Desktop
a. Go to Instagram.com and log-in to your account.
b. After logging in, you’ll notice that there’ll be an IGTV tab between the Posts Tab and Saved Tabs. Click IGTV tab and the Get Started button.
c. Follow all prompts then click Create Channel to finish setting up your channel.
2. Uploading Videos to IGTV
Unlike Instagram, videos cannot be directly captured or recorded on IGTV. Only external videos can be uploaded to your channel.
It’s also advisable to have your videos captured in vertical or portrait mode with an ideal size ratio of 9:16. However, squarish videos with a ratio of 4:5 is still supported. But keep in mind that anything with a ratio other than 9:16 won’t fill the screen.
All videos uploaded can be viewed on both IGTV and Instagram by the people that follow you. As they automatically become your followers on your IGTV Channel, the only way to unfollow it is to unfollow you on Instagram as well.
Since there are no restrictions on how many videos can be uploaded on IGTV, the creators recommend that you upload multiple videos to engage new followers and retain your current followers.
* Uploading Video on your Mobile Device
To upload, click on the “plus” icon on the right side above your information and select a video to upload from your gallery.
However, keep in mind that IGTV has set some restrictions when you upload video from a mobile device:
a. The length of your videos must exceed 15 seconds (videos on your Instagram stories can’t be uploaded).
b. The length of videos must be limited to 10 minutes (however, you’ll find exemptions to this limit in the desktop instructions)
c. Live Instagram videos saved to your device won’t be available in your gallery when you upload videos on your IGTV Channel even if it didn’t exceed the 10-minute limit. A workaround is to save the video on a different folder on your mobile device.
After going through your gallery to select a video to upload, create a title, write a description, and edit the cover image.
When creating a title, give it a descriptive and intriguing title to capture your audience’s interest. However, note that title also get cropped as the pixels of a mobile device is limited and can only fit in 20-25 characters. So make your titles short or keep the descriptive information at the beginning of your title.
Once the video content has been uploaded on mobile devices, the video title and description can no longer be edited. So before posting, be mindful of your grammar, typos, and ensure that all information you want to be included is already there. But edits can be done using desktops if needed.
There will be default images that may or may not be ideal for your video. So we encourage you to replace it with a more appropriate and relevant cover photo. To edit, tap on Edit cover. A pop-up screen will appear, and you can choose a separate photo from your gallery or choose a frame from the video that is to be uploaded.
Having done all the necessary edits, click ‘Post’ to finally upload the video on your channel.
After uploading your first video on your channel, you will notice that your profile image will be highlighted. By tapping it, you or any of your followers will be taken to your channel to watch your video and the others you have uploaded.
* Uploading Video on a Desktop
To upload your first video using a desktop, simply drag and drop your preferred video content on IGTV’s upload field on your desktop.
Though most accounts are limited to 15-second videos to 10-minute videos (via a mobile device), “larger accounts and verified accounts” can upload to a maximum of 60-minute long video through a desktop device as ruled out by Instagram’s Help Center. Unfortunately, there’s no way to determine the criteria to pass a “larger account”.
Unlike on the mobile device, you can simply edit the title and description of your video while waiting for it to upload to 100%. Once done, you can edit the cover photo the same way it’s done on the mobile device &#8211; either select a separate photo from your gallery or choose any frame from the uploaded video.
When ready for upload, click post and it’ll be uploaded on your Channel. You also have the option to save the videos as a draft.
And again, you have the option to edit information when using the desktop site &#8211; Title, Description, and such. Simply click the 3-dot button, and a pop-up menu will appear. Click “Edit Video” to edit.
#3. Best Practices to Apply on your IGTV Channel
Like in any social media platform, Instagram is encouraging you as a user to upload new and unique content on your channel. As IGTV has required everyone to upload from external sources, Instagram is assuming that the video to be uploaded is separate from this channel.
Here are some tips to create effective videos on your IGTV Channel &#8211; implement it when editing and uploading your video.
a. Avoid Distracting and Loud Audios
Like in Instagram Stories, uploaded videos on your IGTV Channel will automatically play with audio unless users have turned off the audio volume on their settings.
IGTV has allowed it’s users more freedom as it’s one of the very few platforms that requires video content created to be accompanied by audios. And as videos play with audio, it’s advisable to avoid using loud and distracting noises that may lead to users swiping through your content. Conversational audios, Interviews, and Voiceover type of audios make for good audio strategies.
b. Add Links to your Descriptions
Any link inserted on your description is a clickable link, so maximise this feature to drive traffic to your website &amp; other social media accounts. Just insert any URL to your description and it will be hyperlinked when the content is uploaded.
And though the link inserted is a clickable one, many have not realized that they can click the link so be sure to insert a call to action before the link. Like, click here to check my website or follow me here on Twitter.
Since videos can be long, retention can be a bit of a problem so make sure to include your CTA within your video. And don’t necessarily leave it till the end of the video as practised.
c. Add Hashtags in your Video Description
Hashtags have been used on Instagram as it’s been a golden rule to keep adding them on Instagram’s descriptions to gain more exposure. The same rule applies on IGTV. Adding hashtags help you reach new audiences as they will appear in the search results for the hashtags you listed. And users that tap on your video in the search result will allow them to view your content as an IGTV full-screen video.
d. Reviewing your IGTV Insights
Strategising means analysing your content and the metrics of your content. Fortunately for businesses and entrepreneurs using IGTV as a marketing platform, IGTV has provided insights for all videos within your mobile app.
To view these insights, tap the vertical 3-dot button on any video uploaded on your channel and click Insights.
The Insights allows you to view the engagement your video has generated (view, likes, and comments) and view your audience retention percentage.
e. Respond to User Comments on Your Videos
Like with any other platform, it’s smart to engage with viewers who leave comments and likes your videos. And IGTV will have you notified for each action viewers does on your video.
To respond, click your notifications or click on your video comments and tap reply.
Finding the following steps easy to follow? Let us know about your experience on IGTV and leave a comment on anything we might have missed!

#### How Wiki Pages Can Support Visibility in AI Search Tools Like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Claude
[et_pb_section fb_built=&#8221;1&#8243; admin_label=&#8221;section&#8221; _builder_version=&#8221;4.16&#8243; global_colors_info=&#8221;{}&#8221; theme_builder_area=&#8221;post_content&#8221;][et_pb_row admin_label=&#8221;row&#8221; _builder_version=&#8221;4.16&#8243; background_size=&#8221;initial&#8221; background_position=&#8221;top_left&#8221; background_repeat=&#8221;repeat&#8221; global_colors_info=&#8221;{}&#8221; theme_builder_area=&#8221;post_content&#8221;][et_pb_column type=&#8221;4_4&#8243; _builder_version=&#8221;4.16&#8243; custom_padding=&#8221;|||&#8221; global_colors_info=&#8221;{}&#8221; custom_padding__hover=&#8221;|||&#8221; theme_builder_area=&#8221;post_content&#8221;][et_pb_text admin_label=&#8221;Text&#8221; _builder_version=&#8221;4.27.6&#8243; background_size=&#8221;initial&#8221; background_position=&#8221;top_left&#8221; background_repeat=&#8221;repeat&#8221; hover_enabled=&#8221;0&#8243; global_colors_info=&#8221;{}&#8221; theme_builder_area=&#8221;post_content&#8221; sticky_enabled=&#8221;0&#8243;]
Search behaviour is no longer limited to typing a query into Google and reviewing the results one by one. More people are using AI tools such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Claude to ask detailed questions, compare options, and narrow down which businesses seem relevant before they ever visit a website.
This shift has created a new challenge for businesses. It is no longer enough to only rank well in Google. Your business also needs to be clearly understood, trusted, and referenced by AI tools.
One way to support this is by creating a wiki style resource section on your own website. This is different from creating a Wikipedia page. A website wiki is a knowledge based area of your site that explains your services, answers common questions, defines industry terms, and helps both people and AI tools understand what your business does.
For businesses investing in SEO and GEO, website wiki pages can become an important visibility asset.
Website Wiki Page vs Wikipedia Page: What’s The Difference?
It is important to understand the difference between a wiki page on your own website and a Wikipedia page.
A website wiki page is a resource your business creates, controls, and updates. It might sit within your blog, knowledge centre, resource hub, or glossary. Its purpose is to educate your audience, explain your area of expertise, and answer the questions people are already asking online.
A Wikipedia page, on the other hand, is an independent encyclopedia entry hosted on Wikipedia. It is not controlled by the business and must meet strict requirements around notability, neutral language, and reliable third party sources. A business cannot simply create a promotional Wikipedia page about itself.
Both can support visibility, but they do so in very different ways. A website wiki page helps search engines and AI tools understand your services, expertise, and topic authority. A legitimate Wikipedia page may support broader trust and entity recognition, but only when the business has enough independent credibility to qualify.

Feature
Wiki Page On Your Website
Wikipedia Page

Who controls it?
Your business controls the content, structure, tone, and updates.
Wikipedia editors and the wider Wikipedia community control the content.

Where does it live?
On your own website, usually within a knowledge centre, resource hub, or glossary section.
On Wikipedia, as part of its public online encyclopedia.

Main purpose
To educate your audience, answer questions, explain services, and build topic authority.
To provide a neutral, encyclopedic summary of a notable person, business, organisation, or topic.

Content style
Can reflect your brand voice while still being helpful and informative.
Must be neutral, factual, and non-promotional.

Source requirements
Can include your own insights, website content, FAQs, and supporting references.
Requires reliable, independent third-party sources.

SEO value
Helps your website rank for relevant topics, FAQs, service queries, and long-tail searches.
Can support broader entity recognition and credibility, but should not be treated as a backlink tactic.

GEO value
Helps AI tools understand what your business does, what topics you are associated with, and which questions you answer.
Can help AI tools verify who or what an entity is, especially when the page is well sourced.

Best suited for
Most businesses that want to improve organic visibility, AI search visibility, and client education.
Businesses, people, or organisations with genuine notability and strong independent media or industry coverage.

What Does A Website Wiki Page Have To Do With AI Visibility?
A website wiki page helps organise your knowledge in a way that is easier for search engines and AI tools to understand.
AI tools need clear, structured information. They look for signals that help them understand who you are, what you do, where you operate, who you help, and which topics your business should be associated with.
A well structured website wiki can help explain:

your services
your process
your industry terminology
your locations
your FAQs
your comparison points
your areas of expertise
your answers to common buyer questions

For AI search, this supports entity recognition. In simple terms, AI tools need to understand your business as a clear entity, not just a collection of pages on a website.
Why Website Wiki Pages Are Useful For SEO
Website wiki pages can support SEO because they give your website more depth around the topics your audience is searching for.
For example, instead of only having one service page, your website could also include supporting wiki style pages that explain common terms, related questions, buying considerations, and industry concepts.
They can help with:
Topic authorityYour website becomes more useful and detailed around the services or topics you want to be known for.
Long tail keyword visibilityWiki style pages can target specific questions and definitions that may not fit naturally on a main service page.
Internal linkingA wiki section gives you more opportunities to link between service pages, blogs, FAQs, case studies, and conversion pages.
Search result consistencyClear and consistent explanations across your website help search engines understand your business more accurately.
Why Website Wiki Pages Are Useful For GEO
GEO, or Generative Engine Optimisation, focuses on helping AI tools understand, retrieve, and reference your business in generated answers.
Website wiki pages can support GEO because they provide clear, structured, answer based content. This is the type of content AI tools can more easily interpret when responding to user questions.
A website wiki may help AI tools understand:

what your business does
which services you offer
which industries or locations you serve
what problems you solve
which questions you answer
how your services compare to related options

This does not mean a website wiki page guarantees that your business will appear in ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Claude. It simply helps create a stronger information base that AI tools can understand.
Where Do Wikipedia And Wikidata Fit In?
Wikipedia and Wikidata are separate from a website wiki.
A Wikipedia page can support visibility if the business, person, or organisation genuinely qualifies for one. However, Wikipedia has strict notability and sourcing requirements, so it is not the right starting point for most businesses.
Wikidata is also different. It is a structured knowledge base that helps machines understand entities and relationships. In some cases, a Wikidata entry can support broader entity clarity, but it should only be created when the information is accurate, appropriate, and supported.
For most businesses, the best first step is not Wikipedia. It is building a strong, helpful, well structured knowledge base on their own website.
A Better Strategy For Most Businesses
Most businesses should start by creating educational content they can control.
That might include:

a website wiki or glossary
service based FAQs
comparison guides
how to guides
industry explainers
location based resources
case studies
schema markup
Google Business Profile optimisation
LinkedIn content
PR and third party mentions

Once those foundations are in place, Wikipedia or Wikidata may become relevant later, depending on the business’s credibility, notability, and available independent sources.
AI visibility is not about tricking the tools. It is about making your business easier to understand, easier to verify, and easier to recommend.
Frequently Asked Questions

Do website wiki pages help with SEO?Yes. Website wiki pages can help with SEO by answering common search queries, building topic authority, supporting long tail keyword rankings, and improving internal linking.
Is a website wiki page the same as a Wikipedia page?No. A website wiki page is created and controlled by your business. A Wikipedia page is an independent encyclopedia entry that must meet strict notability and sourcing rules.
What should I include in a website wiki?A website wiki can include definitions, FAQs, service explanations, process guides, comparison content, location information, and educational resources related to your industry.
Can a website wiki help my service pages rank?Yes. A strong wiki section can support your service pages by linking to them from relevant educational content and helping search engines understand the broader topic.
Can a website wiki help my business appear in ChatGPT?It can support visibility, but it does not guarantee inclusion. A website wiki gives AI tools clearer information about your business, services, expertise, and common customer questions.
Why does AI search care about structured website content?AI tools need clear information they can understand, summarise, and compare. Structured website content, such as FAQs, glossary entries, and explainers, can make your business easier to interpret.
Should every business create a website wiki?Many businesses can benefit from one, especially if their services involve education, comparison, technical terms, complex decisions, or frequent customer questions
Should I try to create a Wikipedia page for my business?Not unless your business has genuine notability and strong independent third party coverage. For most businesses, a website wiki, strong SEO content, schema, PR, and consistent third party citations are better starting points.

#### How Will AI Search Impact My Website Traffic?
The way people search online is shifting, and fast. With AI-powered tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini becoming more mainstream, traditional website traffic patterns are changing. But what does that actually mean for your business? And more importantly, should you be concerned?

Let’s break it down.
From Search Engines to Answer Engines
Traditional search engines like Google and Bing operate on a click-based model. A user types a query, receives a list of links, and chooses which site to visit. That’s where your SEO strategy comes in: ranking on page one, optimising for clicks, and drawing users to your website.
AI search tools work differently. They’re less about providing a list of websites and more about generating a direct answer. Instead of driving traffic to your site, AI might summarise your content, which means you might see fewer clicks to your website, even if your expertise is still being used.
Visibility is Changing, Not Disappearing
Fewer clicks doesn&#8217;t necessarily mean less visibility. It means visibility is changing. Your business could be featured as part of an AI-generated answer, putting your expertise in front of potential customers earlier in their decision-making process, even before they visit your website. If your content is referenced or summarised by AI platforms, your brand is still showing up.
That means instead of asking, “How do I keep my traffic numbers up?” the better question becomes:
“How do I stay discoverable in an AI-first search environment?”
How to Respond and Adapt?
So, what can you do now?
Shift how you think about success. It’s not just about pageviews anymore. It&#8217;s about being the trusted source AI tools want to reference. That means:

Creating well-structured, expert-led content that answers real questions. FAQs, how-tos, and question-led blog posts are more likely to be picked up and summarised.
Building your reputation with quality backlinks: getting cited in reputable places like industry blogs, directories, and news sites.
Publishing content with clear, conversational language that aligns with how people ask questions.
Embracing Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) to ensure AI tools can find and understand your content.

A New Way to Measure Success
Yes, your website traffic may look different in the AI era, but that doesn’t mean your reach is shrinking. While AI search will change how you see traffic in your analytics, it also opens up new opportunities to connect with customers. The businesses that adapt early will stay ahead. Instead of asking, “How do I get more clicks?”, ask, “How do I ensure my expertise is discoverable wherever people are searching?”

The common myth that web design and SEO are unrelated is slowly dying away as more and more business owners begin to understand how the two are intrinsically linked. Here’s a quick overview of some ways your web design can influence your SEO results.
Keyword Spread

While more traditional web layouts present search engines with a rich database of URLs with diversified keywords to crawl, this one-page approach tends to cram all a company’s keywords under one URL. This isn’t just a wakeup call in terms of mobile friendliness, though. As search engines invest more and more into tracking how well users respond to different sites (as well as using this information to influence search result rankings), the importance of quality web design in general will only increase.

Great web design involves plenty of visuals. On top of catching attention, the images you use on your website can also enhance your SEO. How? Through image descriptions and alt text. #### Imagine if you could improve your website conversion rates!
What sort of impact would increase website conversions have on your business?
In your website, you have a 24/7 ‘salesperson’ who doesn’t eat, doesn’t sleep and yet may not be converting as well as it could!
It’s time to look at the traffic you are getting to your website, maybe even more importantly, what are people doing when they come to your website &#8211; are you converting them? If not, now is the time to consider Conversion Rate Optimisation and diving deep into what users do when they visit your website.
Wondering what Conversion Rate Optimisation is?
Well, Conversion Rate Optimisation, otherwise known as CRO, is a method whereby analytics is used to collect data, and user feedback is analysed in order to improve the performance of the website. Essentially CRO provides you data to understand your customers better. It is used to improve metrics on your website (i.e., customer acquisition, download, registration, etc).
A conversion is a generalised term which equates to a website visitor who has completed a goal on your website. A website goal ranges between a macro-conversion (primary goal) to a micro-conversion.

To calculate the conversion rate, divide the number of times a web visitor completed a goal by your total web traffic. If a web visitor is a loyal customer, divide the number of conversions by the number of sessions (times the web visitor opened your website). If selling a subscription, the equation is the number of conversions divided by the number of users.
CRO CAN BENEFIT YOUR SEO EFFORTS….HOW?
Though Conversion Rate Optimisation is not directly related to the goals of Search Engine Optimisation (SEO), CRO benefits SEO by providing:
1. Better Customer Insights
Since CRO is about analysing data and user feedback, it can provide SEO with more meaningful data to help target the right audience for your business. It’s not all about the quantity but also the quality of people visiting your website.
2.Increased Return of Investment (ROI)
CRO helps your SEO increase sales through conversions. CRO provides insight on how to maximise SEO’s acquisition efforts. This means a higher conversion rate with the same quantity of customers.
3. Better Scalability
While your audience may not scale as fast as your business grows, CRO helps you grow consistently. In a similar sense, as SEO focuses on visibility and high ranking to acquire more potential customers and retain loyal ones, CRO directs consumers to the point of conversion.
4. Improved User Web Experience
Users spend more time on your website when they feel they can easily acquire the information they are searching for and receive value in what you are offering through your website. SEO increases your website traffic with the marketing efforts undertaken through the optimisation process while CRO helps identify the working points within your website and expands on it to provide a better experience for your users to encourage greater engagement.
5. Trustworthiness
Your marketing efforts should include industry-related content and information within your website. Remember, your website is your 24/7 ‘salesperson’ representing your brand and company. Therefore, it’s also important that your website looks professional and has the element of sophistication. People generally have high expectations of how a website should look nowadays.
Looking at trustworthiness from a security point of view, users share confidential information such as personal details, credit cards or email addresses, so make sure that the website is secure with an SSL certificate to encrypt any information which is passed across your website.

That’s all good and said, but what can be said about the reverse? Can your SEO complement your CRO efforts?
We have 4 tips on how your SEO can complement your CRO efforts. Download it today….

WHAT DOES SUCCESSFUL CRO LOOK LIKE?
A successful conversion rate optimisation has three foundations:
• where to optimise
• what to optimise
• whom to optimise for
Briefly, you first need to gather the data within your website. To name just a couple of data channels you would want to consider &#8211; where do people enter, what features do they most likely engage with, how do people enter your website and using what device.
Secondly, consider feedback from your users.
Finally, what does successful CRO NOT look like? Whatever you do, don’t base your CRO on fads and hunches. You need to study your data.
All these methods and practices lead to one thing: conversions.

#### Increase Your Video Engagement
In addition to images and text, another great way of marketing visually to your audience is through Videos. However, it’s not as simple as just uploading a video on YouTube. How do you go about getting views and engagement? Have a look at our tips:
Part 1 –
Content of Your Video

So how do you know if your videos are good quality?
Apart from the obvious “thumbs up” or “thumbs down” count, YouTube determines the quality and ranks your video by how viewers interact with it, this includes:

Retention Rate – the percentage of your video that people watched (the longer they watched the better, preferably all the way without dropping out), and whether they stay and watch more videos afterwards.
Commenting – whether good or bad, having comments on your video mean that people probably did watch your video.
Subscribers – if people click Subscribe after viewing your video, that’s a great positive sign that they enjoyed it, and can boost your ranking significantly.
Playlist – some people might add your video to ‘watch later’ or ‘favourite’ playlist, which is also a plus sign for your business.

When you look at the web address bar, SSL-secured websites also begin with the prefix “https” rather than “http”.
Even Google acknowledge the importance of SSL certificates. In a recent post on their website, they said:
“We’d like to encourage all website owners to switch from HTTP to HTTPS to keep everyone safe on the web[1]”.

#### Introduction to YMYL and SEO
If you&#8217;re involved in managing a website that provides critical information influencing people’s health, financial stability, safety, or significant life decisions, it&#8217;s essential to understand YMYL SEO. Google&#8217;s &#8220;Your Money or Your Life&#8221; (YMYL) criteria specifically target content that can deeply affect users&#8217; well-being. Due to its potential impact, such content is subject to Google&#8217;s highest standards for accuracy, reliability, and trustworthiness.

This guide aims to educate you on what YMYL means, why it&#8217;s crucial for SEO, and how you can optimise your website to align with Google&#8217;s stringent guidelines. We&#8217;ll explore key practices and provide real-world examples to help you build trust and authority online, ultimately enhancing your site&#8217;s performance in search results.
Understanding YMYL SEO: Boosting Trust and Rankings for Critical Websites
The term &#8220;Your Money or Your Life&#8221; (YMYL) categorises web content that significantly impacts users&#8217; health, finances, safety, or overall well-being. Due to their critical nature, these pages must adhere to higher standards of accuracy, reliability, and credibility to protect users from potential misinformation or harm. This comprehensive YMYL SEO guide will help you meet Google&#8217;s stringent quality guidelines and improve your site&#8217;s ranking.
Categories of YMYL Websites
Google identifies several types of content as YMYL, including:

Medical and Health Information: Advice on illnesses, treatments, medical procedures, and hospitals.
Financial Content: Investment strategies, tax guidance, insurance, banking, and financial planning.
Legal Information: Details about laws, legal procedures, rights, and obligations.
News and Current Affairs: News on politics, science, business, and international events affecting public safety or well-being.
Government and Civic Resources: Information about voting, public policies, government services, and emergency preparedness.
E-commerce: Online stores and shopping platforms, especially those involving significant financial transactions.
Sensitive Personal Topics: Information relating to race, ethnicity, religion, gender, or other demographics.
Life-Altering Decisions: Content about choosing universities, buying homes, parenting, careers, and lifestyle changes.

Given their substantial influence on people&#8217;s lives, Google rigorously evaluates the quality of these sites to ensure they are trustworthy and reliable.
The Significance of E-E-A-T for YMYL SEO
E-E-A-T stands for Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness—four critical metrics used by Google to measure content quality, particularly for YMYL topics. Here’s what each element means:

Experience: Demonstrating first-hand or direct involvement with the topic being covered, providing users with genuine insights.
Expertise: Ensuring content creators have relevant credentials, qualifications, or demonstrable knowledge in the specific subject area.
Authoritativeness: The reputation of both the content creator and the website as reliable sources within their niche or industry.
Trustworthiness: Transparency and integrity of the website, including accurate information, clear disclosures, secure browsing (HTTPS), and responsible data handling practices.

Optimising your site around these metrics will significantly enhance your YMYL SEO performance.
Best Practices for Optimising YMYL Content
To achieve high search engine rankings and earn user trust, YMYL websites should:

Prioritise Content Accuracy and Timeliness: Regularly update content, removing outdated or incorrect information, and clearly marking the date of the last review.
Highlight Author Credentials Clearly: Display authors&#8217; qualifications, experience, and industry affiliations prominently to validate their authority.
Ensure Website Security and Transparency: Implement secure HTTPS protocols, clear privacy policies, and easily accessible contact details.
Encourage and Respond to User Engagement: Provide avenues for user comments, reviews, or feedback, and actively engage to demonstrate transparency and accountability.
Demonstrate Clear Authorship and Editorial Policies: Clarify who writes your content, how editorial decisions are made, and the processes for verifying accuracy.

Practical Steps to Improve E-E-A-T and SEO

Perform Regular Content Audits: Routinely review your site&#8217;s content for factual accuracy and compliance with evolving industry standards.
Strengthen Author Profiles: Build detailed author bios, link to personal or professional social profiles, and highlight relevant qualifications and experiences.
Invest in Quality Link-Building: Earn backlinks from reputable sites to enhance your site&#8217;s perceived authority and trustworthiness.
Enhance User Experience (UX): Optimise page speed, ensure mobile compatibility, and maintain intuitive navigation to retain user engagement.

Real-World Example of Optimised YMYL Content
Consider a medical information website:

Clearly state medical qualifications of authors (e.g., doctors or specialists).
Regularly updated content reviewed by healthcare professionals.
Citing recent medical research and trusted health organisations such as WHO or CDC.
HTTPS secure browsing with transparent privacy and data handling policies.
User-friendly design, fast loading times, and easy-to-find contact details.

Educational Takeaway: Why E-E-A-T Matters
Understanding and implementing E-E-A-T principles not only improves your SEO but also significantly benefits your audience by providing reliable, accurate information they can confidently use to make informed decisions.
Final Thoughts on YMYL SEO
For YMYL content, SEO isn&#8217;t solely about keywords. It&#8217;s about consistently delivering credible, authoritative, and trustworthy information. By understanding Google&#8217;s quality guidelines for YMYL websites and optimising accordingly, your site can significantly enhance its visibility, credibility, and overall impact.

#### Is AI Replacing Google Search? What Businesses Need to Know
Is AI replacing Google search? It’s a question more business owners are asking as tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and Google’s own AI-powered search results become part of everyday research. While the short answer is no, Google isn’t disappearing, the way people search for information, compare options, and choose businesses is changing in a fundamental way.

Search used to be about typing a keyword, scanning a list of links, and clicking through multiple pages to find an answer. Today, many users are starting with a question and expecting an immediate response. AI tools deliver summaries, explanations, and recommendations in seconds, removing friction from the research process. For businesses, this shift changes where visibility and trust are built.
How AI Is Changing Search Behaviour
AI search tools are being used earlier in the buying journey. Instead of jumping straight into Google, buyers are asking AI tools to explain problems, compare providers, and narrow down options. This is especially common in B2B and professional services, where decisions involve higher value, more risk, and longer consideration cycles.
Rather than presenting a list of websites, AI tools synthesise information and highlight businesses they consider relevant and credible. This means buyers may form opinions about a business before visiting its website at all. Visibility now happens inside AI-generated answers, not just on search results pages.
Why Google Still Matters
Despite the growth of AI search, Google remains a critical part of the ecosystem. Google is still the primary gateway for navigation, brand verification, and deeper research. Even AI tools rely heavily on content published on websites and indexed by search engines.
What has changed is how that content is discovered and used. Google is no longer the only starting point, and ranking first for a keyword does not guarantee visibility in AI-generated responses. Businesses need to think beyond rankings and consider how their content is interpreted by both search engines and AI tools.
From SEO to AI Search Visibility
Traditional SEO focuses on keywords, rankings, and backlinks. While these elements still matter, they don’t fully address how AI tools evaluate businesses. AI search prioritises clarity, authority, and trust. It looks for consistent signals that clearly explain who a business is, what it offers, and why it should be trusted.
This is where Generative Engine Optimisation, or GEO, becomes important. GEO complements SEO by structuring content in a way AI tools can easily understand, reference, and recommend. It aligns website content with the questions buyers are actually asking inside AI tools.
What This Means for Businesses
The biggest risk for businesses is assuming this shift is temporary or irrelevant. AI search is already influencing buying decisions across multiple industries. Businesses that wait until AI traffic shows up in analytics may find they’ve missed early opportunities.
The opportunity lies in being proactive. Businesses that focus on clarity, authority, and structured content are better positioned to be surfaced by AI tools during research and evaluation. This leads to higher-quality conversations and more qualified leads.
AI isn’t replacing Google, but it is reshaping how visibility works. The businesses that respond strategically, rather than reactively, will be the ones buyers and AI tools find first.

People use AI tools to ask natural language questions, research services, compare businesses, and shortlist providers. AI search often happens earlier in the buying process than traditional Google searches.

 What is the difference between AI search and traditional search engines?

Traditional search engines return a list of links. AI search tools generate direct answers, summaries, and recommendations, often referencing businesses they consider credible and relevant.
 

 Can AI tools recommend businesses to potential customers?

Yes. AI tools can reference and recommend businesses when users ask for supplier suggestions, comparisons, or solutions, making AI search an important source of qualified inbound leads.

#### Is AI Search a Threat or Opportunity for Small Businesses?
With the rise of ChatGPT, Gemini, and other AI-powered search tools, many small business owners are wondering: Is this shift a threat or an opportunity? The answer, like most things in digital marketing, depends on how you respond to change.

AI search tools are fundamentally changing the way people find information online. Instead of a long list of links like traditional Google results, users now receive summarised, direct answers. These responses are generated using trusted sources from across the web. While that might sound like a threat to your website traffic, it also opens up a massive opportunity to stand out, if you’re ready.
The Threat: Declining Visibility for Generic Content
AI search tools favour high-authority, well-structured, and informative content. This means small businesses that rely on thin or generic content may find themselves missing out. AI doesn’t just scan for keywords. It looks for trust signals such as citations, quality backlinks, and contextual relevance. If your content doesn’t meet these expectations, AI may ignore it.
The Opportunity: Niche Expertise Wins
AI search rewards specificity and depth. If you’re a small business with niche knowledge, such as a local electrician writing about energy-saving tips for older homes, you have a better chance to rank in AI-generated summaries by creating expert-led content that answers real user questions.
In fact, many AI tools are actively looking for trusted, relevant sources beyond major brands. That means you don’t need to compete with the big players, you just need to lead your niche.
How to Make It Work for You

Start creating fact-checked, helpful content tailored to your audience’s questions.
Structure your pages with clear headings, FAQs, and conversational language that aligns with how people ask questions.
Aim to be mentioned in trusted places like media sites, blogs, or directories.
Optimise for GEO (Generative Engine Optimisation) so that AI tools can find and understand your content.
Keep investing in SEO. Google is still a major player and remains a source for many AI responses.

In short: AI search isn’t here to replace traditional methods, it’s reshaping them. And for small businesses willing to adapt, it presents a new and exciting path to visibility.

#### Is Your Business Ready for AI Search? What You Need to Know in 2026
Search is changing. Fast. And it is changing in a way that many businesses can see in their analytics.

For decades, most visibility strategies centred on ranking in Google. That still matters, but it is no longer the whole story. Now, a new player is shifting the rules: AI search.
AI tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity are shaping how people discover services, compare options, and make decisions. In many cases, users receive an answer first, then decide whether to click.
For business owners, that shift matters because it changes where visibility is won. It is not only about being found on page one. It is also about how your business is described, summarised, and referenced across the web.
Here is the practical summary of what you need to know to stay visible and competitive in this new stage of online search.
1. What is AI Search, and How Is It Different from Google?
AI search is conversational and generative. Instead of presenting a list of links, AI tools generate responses based on information they can access from trusted sources. That can include web pages, databases, publications, and sometimes live search results, depending on the tool and the query.
This means your business may appear in an AI answer, even if the user never lands on your website. That’s a huge shift in visibility strategy.
2. How Will AI Search Impact My Website Traffic?
Many businesses are seeing changes in click behaviour. With AI summarising content directly in the search results, users don’t always need to visit multiple websites to compare options.
That doesn’t mean SEO stops working. It means your content needs to be both rank-worthy and reference-worthy.
3. Why Is My Website Getting Fewer Clicks from Google?
You are not alone. Several changes can contribute to fewer clicks, including AI-generated summaries at the top of the page, zero-click search results, and shifts in user behaviour (such as using TikTok for search).
The good news is that you can adapt. With Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO), you can ensure your business stays visible.
4. How Do AI Platforms Find and Summarise Content?
AI tools don’t rank pages the same way Google does. Instead, they pull from sources they can interpret and trust. That often includes well-structured pages, reputable publications, clear explanations, FAQs, and information that is consistent across multiple online sources.
If your business is referenced or cited in credible sources, you have a better chance of being included when AI tools generate answers.
5. How Can I Make My Website Content More Visible in AI Search?
AI visibility comes down to three things: clarity, structure, and trust.

Use FAQ sections that reflect real customer questions.
Structure pages with headings and concise answers.
Make expertise obvious with clear service explanations, proof points, and helpful examples.

AI tools favour content that is easy to understand and easy to summarise accurately.
6. What Is Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO)?
GEO is the strategy of optimising content so it can be discovered, understood, and referenced by AI platforms.
Traditional SEO focuses on rankings and clicks. GEO focuses on being cited, summarised, and surfaced in AI-generated answers across multiple tools, not just one search engine.
7. Should I Still Invest in SEO?
Absolutely. SEO is evolving, not disappearing. Google remains a major source of demand, and your domain authority and trustworthiness still matter.
The difference in 2026 is that SEO works best when paired with GEO. Build authority, create expert-led content, and ensure your information is consistent and easy for AI to interpret.
8. Where Do AI Tools Get Their Information From?
AI doesn’t just rely on your website. It pulls from:

News publications
Wikipedia
Authoritative blogs
Academic journals
Google’s index
Product reviews and forums

Your website is essential, but it is not the only input. A more substantial digital footprint across trusted sources increases the likelihood of being included.
9. How Do I Get Cited in AI Search Results?
Start with content that deserves to be referenced, then build the signals around it.

Publish genuinely helpful answers and resources.
Earn mentions and backlinks from credible websites.
Create pages that explain your service clearly and specifically.
Use FAQs that match the way people search and ask questions.

The goal is to make your business easy to trust and easy to summarise.
10. Is AI Search a Threat or an Opportunity?
It can be both.
Businesses that rely on generic content and a single traffic source may feel the impact first. Businesses that improve content quality, strengthen authority, and broaden their visibility strategy are well-placed to future-proof their marketing.
Where to From Here?
The shift to AI search isn’t a passing trend. It is a transformation in how customers discover, compare, and shortlist.
If your strategy relies solely on Google to bring in leads, you are only seeing part of the picture. A stronger approach in 2026 includes:

Understanding how AI search works.
Auditing your current online presence.
Optimising content for both Google and AI platforms.
Building credibility through citations and trusted mentions.

FAQs
1. What is AI search, and how does it work for business discovery?
AI search tools generate answers based on information they can access from trusted sources, which can influence how your business is described before someone clicks. 
2. Will AI search reduce my website traffic from Google?
It can, especially for informational searches. The focus shifts from clicks alone to being referenced in the answers users see.
 
3. What is the difference between SEO and GEO?
SEO aims to improve rankings in traditional search engines, while GEO focuses on making your content easy for AI tools to understand, summarise, and reference.
 
4. How do I optimise my website for AI search tools?
Use clear headings, concise answers, service-specific pages, and FAQs based on real customer questions: consistency and credibility matter.
 
5. Why are FAQs important for AI search visibility?
FAQs mirror the way people ask questions and help AI tools extract accurate, structured answers from your website.
 
6. What types of content are most likely to be used in AI-generated answers?
Helpful, well-structured content with clear explanations, specific details, and evidence of expertise is more likely to be referenced.
 
7. How can small businesses compete in AI search against larger brands?
By owning a niche, answering specific questions better than anyone else, and building authority through trusted mentions and backlinks.
 
8. Does local SEO still matter in 2026?
Yes. Local relevance and trust signals remain important, and they can also influence how AI tools describe local service options.
 
9. How can I increase the chances of being cited by AI tools?
Publish content worth referencing, then build credibility through reputable mentions, backlinks, directories, and industry sources.
10. What should I do first to improve AI search visibility?
Start with an audit. Identify gaps in clarity, structure, trust signals, and off-site mentions, then prioritise fixes that improve both SEO and GEO.

#### Landing Pages: Why They Matter to Your Clients
What value do you, as a business owner, place on landing pages? In a recent conversation we had with a business owner, they felt they were not necessary. At Concept Designs &amp; Marketing, we’re here to shed some light on how landing pages play a critical role in the success of online marketing efforts.

Unlike a general website page that might serve multiple purposes, a landing page is designed with one specific goal in mind—whether that’s capturing leads, promoting a product, or encouraging sign-ups. This focused approach ensures that visitors are guided directly toward meaningful action, making landing pages an essential tool in turning casual browsers into engaged customers.
A well-crafted landing page is more than just visually appealing; it’s about creating a seamless, targeted experience that aligns with your marketing objectives. From the moment a visitor lands on the page, the messaging and layout should work together to compel engagement, whether it’s through form submissions, CTA clicks, or purchases. The effectiveness of your landing pages can significantly impact conversion rates, making them integral to a successful marketing strategy.
Why They Matter

First Impressions Count: A landing page is often the first interaction a potential client has with your brand. A well-crafted landing page instantly builds trust, effectively communicates your value proposition, conveys the brand’s value proposition, and encourages the visitor to take action. It&#8217;s about creating a seamless experience that guides the user toward the desired outcome, whether that&#8217;s signing up for a webinar, downloading an e-book, or making a purchase.
Targeted Content: Unlike a homepage, landing pages allow for highly targeted content. By customising the message to address specific audience segments, landing pages can address particular pain points and offer tailored solutions. This personalised approach significantly increases conversion rates as it resonates more directly with the visitor&#8217;s needs.
Improved Analytics: Landing pages are pivotal for tracking the effectiveness of your marketing efforts. They enable businesses to monitor crucial metrics such as conversion rates, bounce rates, and user behaviour. With this data, you can continuously refine your strategies and optimise their content for better performance.
Enhanced SEO and Paid Advertising: Landing pages are the cornerstone of successful paid advertising and SEO strategies. A well-optimised landing page with targeted keywords can improve search engine rankings and drive organic traffic. For paid campaigns, these pages maximise ROI by directing users to content that precisely matches their search intent.
Customer Retention: A successful landing page doesn’t just end with a conversion; it can also be the first step in building long-term customer relationships. By offering valuable content, such as free resources or special offers, landing pages encourage repeat visits and interactions, nurturing leads into loyal customers.

Investing in correctly-designed landing pages is crucial for any business aiming to strengthen its online presence. These pages not only drive conversions and improve campaign performance but also play a key role in fostering long-term client relationships. For businesses aiming to stand out in the highly competitive digital space, landing pages are indispensable tools in your marketing toolkit.

#### Lead Generation Funnels and Customer Nurture Strategies
In the intricate dance of digital marketing, lead generation funnels are pivotal in guiding potential customers through their buying journey. This article delves into the anatomy of effective lead generation funnels, which are carefully segmented into three core offers to align with varying stages of the buyer&#8217;s journey. 

From initial engagement to final conversion, each phase is meticulously designed to cater to the evolving needs of prospects. 
We&#8217;ll explore the nuances of crafting these offers &#8211; from understanding your target customer&#8217;s psychology and creating compelling offers, to perfecting landing pages for peak conversion. 
With Concept Designs &#038; Marketing, discover how a well-executed sales funnel becomes a cornerstone for nurturing leads and propelling business growth.
Lead generation funnels consist of three core offers, each designed to motivate action based on where the traffic is in the buyer&#8217;s journey. The first offer is the &#8220;authority beacon,&#8221; like a lead magnet, attracting colder traffic. The second offer converts visitors into leads, typically by getting them on the phone with you. The third offer packages what you sell to leads who are sales-ready.
The 3 Core Offers of Lead Generation Funnels
#1: Research Your Target Customer Psychology
The first step is to understand your target customers&#8217; psychology. This involves extensive research to uncover their core desires, pain points, and preferred language. The goal is to mirror these in your communication with potential customers.
#2: Craft a Strategic Lead Generation Offer
The next step is creating a lead generation offer that converts cold traffic. This should be a strategic offer that motivates a micro &#8220;yes,&#8221; guiding visitors to the next logical step in their journey.
#3: Execute With Optimised Landing Pages
Finally, execution involves creating a dedicated landing page for your offer. This page should be ruthlessly optimised for maximum conversions, focusing on the most critical elements above the fold.
All that to say, an effective sales funnel is vital for nurturing leads and driving business growth. #### Lead Generation to Maximise ROI
Lead Generation is a crucial part of the marketing strategy for many businesses. However, when you hear this term being used, do you understand its true meaning and purpose?

Firstly, a Lead is someone who has shown interest in your products and services but may not yet make the purchase. Therefore, Lead Generation is the process of capturing and gaining the interest of potential customers.
Sounds simple, right?
Many businesses fall into the habit of quick ‘lead generation’ that may gain the interest of the “potential” customer, but fail to see the lead through and gain the long-term growth by increasing sales, i.e. turning those leads into conversions and actual purchases.
So, how should you go about using Lead Generation to maximise your ROI, instead of wasting your marketing budget on just attracting “potential” customers that don’t give you the returns you need?
Let’s take a look at the options of Lead Generation strategies.
Inbound Leads
These are customers with whom you are more likely able to close the sale, as they come directly to you. They would already be quite interested in your products and services to start with. Inbound leads can come from your social media marketing, SEO and Google ads, word of mouth, and other traditional media such as print and TV.
Outbound Leads
These are leads that you seek to attract interest to your business. They haven’t heard about you or may not be looking for your solution, but you try to reach out and create the connection between the potential customer and your products and services. You can get Outbound leads with cold calls and emails, direct mail, and through networking or trade events.
While Inbound Leads may seem to be the better choice when it comes to conversions and a better ROI result, it’s important to not overlook the Outbound leads especially for B2B which can bring in a steady stream of leads for nurturing. One such possibility is by leveraging the networking aspect through LinkedIn.
LinkedIn is one of the best platforms for honing in your target audience and building up a connection with them. #### Lead Generation with Landing Pages – why you need them for your Lead Magnets!
Previously we talked about Lead Magnets, and how they can be used to attract leads and grow your email list. You might even recall signing up to an offer, or downloaded a free e-book at some stage before. Where did you go to receive the offer? Most likely than not, it was on a Landing Page!

So now that you have your lead magnet ideas, next you will need Landing Pages! Why you may ask? Why not just direct people straight to your website?
Rather than sending your potential leads to your home page, your lead magnet will work best on a separate Landing Page:
1. Target your market
A landing page allows you to target specifically to an audience. For example, if your lead magnet offer is targeted towards young people, you can tailor the language, text, and images towards that age group. You can target specific geographical locations and needs as well. They’ve clicked on your offer, so make your landing page engaging!
2. Better insights
Directing potential leads to a landing page instead of your website will also allow you to attribute where the leads came from, which will help you with your marketing insights and analytics. For example, you might advertise your Lead Magnet on Facebook, having a specific landing page will then let you know how many leads came from social media, and how that side of the marketing is performing.
3. No distractions
More importantly, a separate Landing Page will help your visitors stay focused. If you send them to your website, they might get distracted or overwhelmed with too much information, and leave without completing the sign-up process. Your aim is to make sure they sign-up to your lead magnet. You give them one option: Sign-up!
Ideally, your Landing Page should further describe the benefits of your lead magnet, include a testimonial if you have one, with appealing imagery or video, and a BIG Call-to-action! It should complement your lead magnet, reinforcing the value you’re offering, and must be quick and easy to sign-up. Don’t make your visitors jump through hoops to obtain your offer!

#### Link Smarter, Not Harder: Using iFrames to Boost Engagement and SEO
Keep Visitors on Your Website for Longer
When it comes to website performance, time on site matters. The longer someone stays on your website, the better it looks to search engines, and the more likely they are to take the next step. That might be making a booking, completing a form, or picking up the phone. One simple way to keep visitors engaged is to avoid sending them off to external websites.

Sometimes, you need to reference an external platform, such as a booking system, supplier, or industry partner. But when you use a standard external link, your visitor leaves your site the moment they click it. This disrupts the user journey and can reduce time spent on your website, which may affect your SEO. 
What’s The Alternative? Use an iFrame 
An iframe (short for “inline frame”) is a piece of code that lets you display content from another website inside your own. Think of it as a window. Your visitor stays on your website but can still view and interact with external content within that window.
At Concept Designs &amp; Marketing, we can embed an external website or platform inside your own website using an iframe. This way, your visitors can interact with the content they need without ever leaving your site.
How We Use iFrames to Improve Engagement
If you ask us to include a link to an external site, such as a product catalogue, service provider, or booking platform, we’ll check whether the site can be embedded. If it can, we’ll create a dedicated page on your website where the external content appears via an iframe. Your visitors can interact with the content just as they would on the original site, but they stay within your domain.
This improves user experience, keeps your branding consistent, and increases the average time spent on your site, which in turn supports stronger SEO outcomes.
What If the Site Can’t Be Embedded?
Some websites have restrictions that block iframe embedding for security or branding reasons. If the iframe doesn’t load correctly or displays a blank screen, the external site likely has settings that prevent this.
In technical terms, these settings might include:

X-Frame-Options set to “DENY” or “SAMEORIGIN”
A Content Security Policy (CSP) that blocks external embedding

This doesn’t mean it’s a dead end. If the owner of the external site is open to it, they can update these settings to allow iframe embedding on your domain. 
What To Ask Your Web Developer
If you manage the external site, or have a contact who does, you can ask them to allow iframe embedding for your website. Here’s an example message you can use:
Hi [developer’s name], we’d like to embed [external site URL] on our website using an iframe. Could you please update the settings to allow iframe embedding on our domain (e.g. https://www.ourwebsite.com)? This may involve adjusting the X-Frame-Options or Content Security Policy headers. Let me know if you need more information. Thanks!
We’re also happy to collaborate directly with your developer if needed. 
Need Help Embedding an iFrame?
If you’re not sure whether a site can be embedded, or want to explore the best way to keep visitors on your website longer, just get in touch. We can talk through your options and help set everything up so your website is set up to make the most of every visit.
