#### LinkedIn Native Video For Your Business
LinkedIn is known as the official business platform for all people networking and connecting with like-minded professionals and for users looking for opportunities &#8211; business, job, venture and more.
And since LinkedIn released their new feature, LinkedIn Native Video, it has opened new doors for a lot of users.
But Why choose LinkedIn Native Video?
Videos allow people to get a better sense of who you are, build trust much faster, and it reinforces your brand. And because of this, people are more likely to connect with you after seeing the video &#8211; a turning point and start of a relationship.
Video is the perfect way to connect with your audience and to let your personality, knowledge, and expertise shine through.

How to Upload Videos using LinkedIn Native Video?
To upload videos, open the app using your mobile device. And you’ll notice that there is a Video Icon in your share box, net to the camera icon. Tap the video icon.
When done, you can choose if you’ll upload a pre-recorded video or upload a video recorded on the spot. Don’t worry, all video recorded using LinkedIn Native Video will be automatically saved on your mobile device.
However, please be aware as LinkedIn also set rules when uploading a video:
1. Videos to be uploaded should be longer than 3-seconds long to 10 minutes short. However, the best practice is to keep it no longer than 3 minutes.
2. The size of the video that can be uploaded is up to 5GB.
3. It’s advisable to add a descriptive text when uploading videos (can be done before or after the video is uploaded). The limit of 700 characters leaves you to be imaginative in describing what’s in the video or in making sure that you encourage them to watch your video.
4. And links! It’s best to include links, tag people, and include relevant hashtags on your video.
Best Practices for LinkedIn Native Video
Like in any other platforms, there are best practices when it comes to using LinkedIn Native Video.
i. Video can and will amplify your brand. Make it a priority to produce professional looking videos on LinkedIn and all efforts that been put onto it will be rewarded.
ii. Since LinkedIn is a business-focused platform, it best to keep the videos relevant and aligned with the brand.
iii. Keep the content 80% helpful and only 20% promotional. Use LinkedIn Native Video to reach out to a larger audience and let them know more about you, what you do, and what you can do to help.

#### Looking for a fresh digital marketing start this new financial year?
Prioritise a digital marketing strategy for your business
As the new financial year kicks off, it’s the perfect time for business owners to re-evaluate their strategies and investments. One area that should be at the top of the priority list is digital marketing. In today’s fast-paced, technology-driven world, digital marketing is not just a nice-to-have; it’s essential for business growth and success.

The Digital Shift
The digital landscape has transformed the way businesses operate. Here are several reasons why investing in digital marketing is vital for your business:

Enhanced Online Presence A strong online presence is critical. Your website, social media profiles, and online listings are often the first points of contact between your business and potential customers. Digital marketing strategies like search engine optimisation (SEO), content marketing, and social media marketing ensure that your business is visible to your target audience.
Targeted Advertising Digital marketing allows for highly targeted advertising. With tools like Google Ads and Facebook Ads, you can reach specific demographics, interests, and behaviours, ensuring your marketing budget is spent efficiently. This targeted approach results in higher conversion rates and better ROI compared to traditional marketing methods.
Cost-Effectiveness Compared to traditional marketing channels, digital marketing is often more cost-effective. Small businesses, in particular, can benefit from digital marketing strategies that require lower budgets while still reaching a large audience. Techniques like email marketing, social media campaigns, and content marketing provide high value at a fraction of the cost.
Measurable Results One of the significant advantages of digital marketing is the ability to track and measure results. Analytics tools allow you to monitor the performance of your campaigns in real-time. This data-driven approach enables you to make informed decisions, optimise your strategies, and achieve better outcomes.
Adaptability and Flexibility The digital world is dynamic, and trends can shift rapidly. Digital marketing offers the flexibility to adapt your strategies quickly in response to market changes. Whether it’s tweaking your social media approach or adjusting your PPC campaigns, digital marketing provides the agility needed to stay ahead of the competition.
Improved Customer Engagement Digital marketing fosters better engagement with your audience. Through social media platforms, email newsletters, and online communities, you can interact directly with your customers, build relationships, and foster loyalty. Engaged customers are more likely to become repeat buyers and advocates for your brand.

Planning for the New Financial Year
As you plan for the new financial year, consider allocating a portion of your marketing budget to digital strategies. Here are some steps to get started:
&#8212; Evaluate Your Current Digital Presence: Conduct an audit of your website, social media, and other digital channels. Identify areas for improvement and set clear goals.
&#8211; Develop a Digital Marketing Strategy: Create a comprehensive plan that includes SEO, content marketing, social media, email marketing, and PPC campaigns.
&#8211; Invest in the Right Tools and Resources: Utilise digital marketing tools that can help streamline your efforts and improve results. Consider partnering with a digital
          marketing agency like Concept Designs &#038; Marketing to leverage expertise and experience.
&#8211; Monitor and Adjust: Regularly review your digital marketing performance and be ready to make adjustments as needed. Stay informed about the latest trends and best practices.
Starting the new financial year with a robust digital marketing strategy can set your business on the path to success. By enhancing your online presence, targeting the right audience, and engaging with customers, you’ll be well-equipped to thrive in the digital age. #### Malware Attack and Financial Loss
Website Security Part I –
While the internet has opened doors to opportunities for businesses to promote and trade online, it has also provided a means for opportunists to target businesses with unauthorised access and fraudulent activities. A recent Australian survey of 1,436 small businesses, found that 96% owned a computer, 94% connected online, 60% had a website, and 53% received payments online1
You may wonder, is it really necessary to implement security technology? If you have a website for your business, then yes – you are vulnerable!
An ABACUS study, found that in one year alone, 14% of small businesses experienced one or more computer security threats. Negative outcomes were reported by 75% of small businesses. The top five are:

Corruption of hardware or software (42%);
Corruption or loss of data (31%);
Unavailability of service (38%);
Operational losses (24%);
Financial losses (12%);

And with 5% of businesses experiencing critical financial losses that could lead to closure, the average loss to a small business was $2,431 from a malware attack, and many businesses face multiple hacks per year. Can you afford this loss?
So, what happens when you face a malware attack, leading to financial loss?
Blacklisted by search engines:
Your website is monitored for malware by search engines. When any malware is detected, you site will be blacklisted and access will be blocked. Your website will be go offline for days, until you have cleared the infection and submitted a request to be removed from the blacklist. Loss of revenue is especially problematic if you do business transactions online. Even just a few days loss of business can cost you over the long-run, as customers can become weary or reluctant to come back.
This is just the start of what risks malware can pose. More long term damaging consequences include; loss of SEO rankings and reputation, illegitimate links, and information theft – which will be covered in Part II.
In the meantime, it is important to make sure that you are protected. Many businesses misunderstand that their websites are covered through hosting or firewalls, however hackers are adept in finding ways to infiltrate your website. The best way is to have protection that is specifically designed for malware detection and removal.

We provide malware protection services that will scan your website daily, giving you peace of mind and saving you from unnecessary financial loss. Stay tuned for Part II for more information and self-check tips!

#### Mastering Your Target Market: The Key to Marketing Success
Understanding and reaching your target market is fundamental to any successful marketing strategy. Whether you&#8217;re launching a new product or aiming to grow your business, a targeted approach ensures your marketing efforts resonate with the right audience. Let&#8217;s delve into the steps of ensuring target market success.

1. Defining Your Target Audience
The first step in any marketing strategy is to clearly define who your target audience is. This involves:

Gaining a deep understanding of your products and identifying who benefits most from them.
Examining your current customer base and conducting thorough audience research.
Going beyond basic demographic data to include psychographic information.
Segmenting your audience into distinct groups for more focused marketing efforts.
Analysing your competitors and their customer bases for insights.

Understanding your target audience lays the foundation for your entire marketing strategy, informing everything from your messaging to channel selection and campaign development.
2. Identifying Where Your Audience Is Active
Once you know who your audience is, the next step is to find out where they spend their time, both online and offline. This could range from social media platforms like Instagram to industry-specific trade publications. The goal is to deliver your marketing message on the channels where your audience is most engaged.
3. Creating Relevant Content
Your content is the voice of your brand, speaking directly to your target audience. To effectively communicate with them, you need to:

Understand their unique needs and challenges.
Create diverse content such as blog posts, email newsletters, social media posts, and videos.
Ensure your content is helpful, logical, targeted, structured, and easy to digest.
Use an active voice, eliminate filler, and provide unique insights.
Focus on answering the &#8216;why&#8217; and &#8216;how&#8217; in a manner that appeals to your audience.

Great content is not just about what you say, but how you say it, and how it resonates with your audience.
4. Using Targeted Advertising
Merely creating content is not enough; you need to ensure it reaches your target audience. This is where targeted advertising comes in. Using tools like Google Ads and social media advertising, you can:

Reach your audience on platforms where they are most active.
Employ advanced targeting based on demographics, interests, life stages, job roles, and more.
Ensure your ads are seen by those most likely to be interested in your brand and products.

Engaging your Target Market is not a one-off task but an ongoing process that evolves with your business and the market. By continually refining your understanding of your target audience, where they are, and how to engage them, you can make informed marketing decisions that drive real results.

This audit will not only identify your current standing but also highlight opportunities to refine and enhance your approach. #### Maximising Business Growth Through Effective Sales Funnels
Generating leads for business is akin to discovering a valuable resource. However, merely finding this resource is not enough; it must be efficiently utilised. Herein lies the critical role of a high-converting funnel. Without a steady flow of qualified leads into your sales pipeline, achieving growth can feel like an insurmountable challenge. Many businesses face difficulties in consistently generating high-quality leads, leading to the question: What constitutes an effective lead generation funnel, and how is it built?

At Concept Designs &#038; Marketing, we recognise that some business owners may view the idea of &#8220;funnels&#8221; with skepticism, perceiving them as overly aggressive or suited for dubious marketing tactics. However, after 20+ years as a marketing expert we would argue that such a view stems from misunderstandings and misinterpretations.
In reality, every business operates a sales funnel, whether consciously or not. This funnel comprises each interaction a prospective customer has with your brand, from the initial ad exposure to browsing your website and booking calls. It represents the complete journey a customer takes with you.
Understanding this, it&#8217;s evident that funnels can have &#8216;leaks&#8217; where potential revenue can be lost. All of your touchpoints in your funnel, are potential revenue leaks and small leaks can sink big ships.  The mistake many businesses make is obsessing over driving more traffic while neglecting the conversion process. Attracting traffic is relatively straightforward; the challenge lies in converting this traffic effectively.
Funnels, when correctly optimised, significantly enhance the value derived from each visitor. 
Moreover, a robust lead generation funnel gives you a competitive edge. It&#8217;s a unique asset that can&#8217;t be easily replicated by competitors. Your unique sales funnel is like building a moat around your business.
Building Lead Generation Funnels
At Concept Designs &#038; Marketing, we have a tried and tested framework for building effective lead generation strategies from the ground up. From understanding the psychology of your target customer to crafting compelling offers, we have created a process that has helped clients generate millions in pipeline revenue.
A robust and efficient sales funnel fits into the following three phases:
Phase 1: Attract Traffic and Generate Leads
This phase focuses on converting cold website visitors into leads. It involves funnel touchpoints like lead magnets for capturing emails, high-converting landing pages, and paid ads targeting buyer-specific keywords. The key here is to persuade cold traffic to opt-in.
Phase 2: Convert Leads into Customers
Once visitors become leads, the next phase is to guide them through the sales cycle toward a purchase. This stage involves coordinated follow-ups, demos, pricing discussions, and a strong closing.
Phase 3: Maximise Customer Lifetime Value
The final phase is about extracting maximum value from new customers. This involves providing excellent onboarding, securing referrals, and guiding towards repeat purchases and word-of-mouth.
Most businesses focus on the first two phases and neglect the third. However, high-value customers are hard-won, and each phase needs to be maximised.
Our approach starts with attracting leads, as sales and fulfilment are futile without them. Then, you can build a lead generation funnel to increase traffic conversion and secure high-quality leads. With a reliable pipeline, you can expect consistent leads every month.

Through our hands-on approach, you will learn the secrets of crafting high-converting funnels to skyrocket your business growth. Why Targeted Landing Pages Work:

Focused Content: Unlike homepages that cater to a broad audience, targeted landing pages speak directly to a specific audience segment. This focused approach

Better Quality Leads: Targeted landing pages allow for the collection of more qualified leads. Visitors landing on these pages are often seeking specific solutions, making them more likely to convert into customers.
Enhanced SEO and PPC Efficiency: By aligning with specific keywords and ad campaigns, targeted landing pages can significantly improve your search engine optimisation (SEO) and pay-per-click (PPC) campaign performance, leading to better visibility and higher conversion rates.

#### Maximising Leads with Strategic Website Lead Magnets
For businesses looking to capture and convert online traffic, lead magnets are invaluable. At Concept Designs and Marketing, we understand how to effectively utilise these tools on your website to maximise lead generation.

The Power of Lead Magnets:
Lead magnets are incentives offered to potential customers in exchange for their contact information. They can range from free eBooks and webinars to exclusive discounts or trials. The key is to offer something of value that resonates with your target audience.
Strategic Placement for Maximum Impact:
The placement of lead magnets on your website is critical for their success. Based on user experience (UX) analysis, there are prime locations where lead magnets can be most effective:

Above the Fold: This is the visible part of your webpage when it first loads. Placing a lead magnet here ensures immediate visibility.
Sidebar or Footer: These areas are ideal for less intrusive but still noticeable placements.
During the Checkout Process: Offering a lead magnet during checkout can increase conversions, especially if it&#8217;s related to the purchase.
Exit-Intent Pop-Ups: These are effective in capturing the attention of users who are about to leave your site.

Best Practices in Lead Magnet Creation:

Relevance: Your lead magnet should be highly relevant to your target audience’s interests and needs.
Quality: The content or offer should be of high quality to truly engage and convert leads.
Clear Call-to-Action: Your lead magnet should have a clear and compelling CTA to guide users on what to do next.
Tracking and Analysis: Regularly analyse the performance of your lead magnets and make adjustments as needed.

Lead magnets are a powerful tool for converting website visitors into leads and customers. By strategically placing and crafting these magnets, you can significantly enhance your online marketing efforts.

#### Measurement Marketing – Why is Tracking so Important?
In an age of the digital era, marketing has evolved to a range of mediums which now come with handy analytics, insights, and metrics. However, many businesses also feel overwhelmed by this deluge of digital data and unsure how to use them to measure or track marketing efforts efficiently.

Why Should You Track?
Before we look into ways that you can make use of your data, why should you be tracking your marketing? Here are the benefits of collecting and analysing your data:

Providing insights as to what is working and what isn’t
Helps you determine new trends
Allows you to identify engaging content that draw in new customers
Improve your marketing based on past results
Setting more realistic expectations and goals for future campaigns

How Should You Track?
So, how should you go about tracking and measuring your marketing efforts? Do you find yourself staring blankly at the insights or analytics page with an overload of data and not sure what to look for?
Firstly, start with what your goals or objectives are. It can be as simple as the number of visitors to your website, or the amount of engagement on your social media posts. Other goals could include:

Conversions by email or ads
Number of views, comments, and shares
Actions taken eg. Downloading an e-book, signing up to a newsletter
Number of URL clicks to your landing page
Other Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) such as sales figures, bounce rates, and ROIs

Tips on Tracking
You can use more than one type of tracking for campaigns, and experiment with different kinds of tracking metrics you can use to see what makes sense.
For example, you may run a campaign on a new e-book download. In this case, you can track the number of URL clicks to the landing page, the actual number of downloads, as well as where the clicks are coming from (email, social media, or website visitors). You can then further break down the data to different timeframes by daily, weekly or monthly, as well as by demographics.
As you can see, it doesn’t have to be over-complicated or costly, most of these analytics should come with your social media platforms and Google analytics without additional costs. The key is to have a clear objective and know what you are looking for specifically. The best thing is, you can play around with the metrics and learn as you go with trial and error.
Ultimately, you want to improve on your marketing and move forward with better results. The takeaway is to use the data to make changes with the customer in focus. For example, if you notice that most click-throughs are coming from Facebook, then perhaps you need to adjust your direct email message or homepage layout to make the download offer more prominent.

#### Navigating the 2024 Google Updates: Optimising Digital Success
In the digital world, change is the only constant, and Google&#8217;s 2024 updates are a testament to this dynamic environment. As a business, staying informed and adaptable to these changes is crucial. Let&#8217;s dive into what these updates mean for your online presence.

1) The Shift to Interaction to Next Paint (INP):
Google has announced a major change in its Core Web Vitals metrics. Starting March 12, 2024, Interaction to Next Paint (INP) will replace First Input Delay (FID). INP measures the delay in user interactions more comprehensively, focusing on the longest interaction delay observed on a page. This shift emphasises the importance of responsive and interactive web designs.
Understanding INP and Its Components:
INP stands for Interaction to Next Paint and it evaluates three key aspects: Input Delay, Processing Time, and Presentation Delay. It&#8217;s a holistic measure of user interaction delays, including clicks, taps, and key presses.
Enhancing User Experience: The Role of INP:
INP will be crucial for website owners and developers, as it gives a more accurate representation of user experience. To prepare for this transition, it&#8217;s essential to monitor and improve your site&#8217;s INP scores using tools like Google Search Console. Remember, while Core Web Vitals are important, they are one of many factors in Google&#8217;s ranking system.
2) New Search Innovations:
Google&#8217;s 2024 updates also include two major search enhancements:

Circle to Search: Launched for Android users, this feature allows on-screen searches without needing to switch apps. It&#8217;s all about enhancing user convenience and making information access more seamless.
AI-powered Multi-search Experience: Google has further developed its multi-search feature, now providing AI-generated insights for complex queries. This innovation not only enhances the visual search experience but also emphasises the importance of optimising visual content for SEO.

These updates from Google underscore the evolving nature of search engine technology and user experience. For businesses and website owners, staying updated and adapting to these changes is key to maintaining a competitive edge in the digital landscape. #### Navigating the New Terrain: Understanding Google&#8217;s Upcoming Updates on 5 May
On 5 March 2024, Google announced a major core algorithm update, a common occurrence in the SEO landscape. Understanding these updates is vital for maintaining and enhancing your digital strategy. So, let&#8217;s delve into the details of this significant update.

Enhancements in Search Quality and Ranking
The heart of the upcoming Google update is focused on improving the quality of search results. Recognising the tactics of spam websites that exploit Google&#8217;s algorithm, the update aims to prioritise high-quality, relevant information while diminishing unoriginal and low-quality content. By enhancing its core ranking systems, Google is committed to promoting valuable content and reducing the prevalence of less original material.
Updated Spam Policies
Another crucial aspect of this update is the overhaul of Google&#8217;s spam policies. Responding to the evolving nature of low-quality web content, these changes aim to filter such content from search results. This includes targeting specific issues like expired websites repurposed for spam, obituary spam, and the sophisticated abuse of content at scale. For example, businesses that produce extremely high volumes of low-quality, AI-generated content solely for SEO purposes are a key focus of this policy update.
Impact on Digital Marketing and SEO
SEO experts are closely monitoring this update, as its implementation may significantly impact businesses, particularly smaller ones. While the exact effects are yet to be fully understood, the update is anticipated to support websites prioritising quality content and genuine user engagement. Interestingly, if you&#8217;re creating AI-generated content that is both quality and helpful, it&#8217;s likely that Google will continue to reward such content.
As we anticipate these changes, staying informed and proactive is paramount. At Concept Designs and Marketing, we are vigilant about every Google update and its implications for genuine businesses.

#### New Facebook Reactions – what it means for your business
Facebook launched their new range of reaction choices just five days ago, have you noticed anything different on your Facebook Page?
It makes sense that Facebook, being a social media tool that shares information and happenings, should allow users to express their emotions with more than just a “LIKE” button, regardless of whether the posts are exciting, happy, or sad. Now, users can choose from a range of emoticons when they hold down or hover over the LIKE button:
Like, Love, Haha (Laugh), Wow, Sad, or Anger

What does it mean for your business?
Thankfully, these new reactions do not include “Dislike”, so whichever emotions your customers choose will not count as negative feedback on Facebook (will not be classified as ‘Report as Spam’ or ‘Unlike Page’/ ‘Hide Post’). This means you can embrace this new function to boost your business on Facebook!
Analytics and Insights:
With the range of new emotions, you can now see what types of posts provoke certain types of reactions in your followers. Facebook lists the reactions for each emotion and how many of your followers represent that reaction:

Have a look at your newer posts which will more likely have these new reactions, people can also go back to the older posts and add new reactions if they haven’t already done so.
Engaging your customers:
You can create posts that drive customer engagement by asking your followers what their thoughts are. Explicitly invite and encourage them to express their emotions on your post, this will help your posts reach more people with more reactions, and boosts its visibility. For example, say, “What do you think about… Tell us by showing your feelings!” etc.
Don’t be fearful of the “Angry” emotion, instead, think of it as a way to address your customers concerns and feedback – this allows the customer to give a ‘reaction’ or ‘vent’ without actually posting negative comments, a more positive way to deal with issues. Remember, the “Angry” reaction is not counted negatively towards your post.
As you can see, the new Facebook Reaction roll-out opens up many beneficial opportunities for businesses to learn about their customers’ feelings, better engage their followers, and even gain insights on how posts are performing in their industry.

#### New Years Resolutions &#8211; for you and your business!
Now that the New Year has arrived, it is a good time to start fresh and strive to do even better in 2018!
Just like each of us, your business can also have New Year’s Resolutions! Maybe you want to exercise more, eat healthier or be more organised. Well, what about your business? If you want it to be healthy much like your body, then here are some ideas for you:
1, Consistent &amp; Regular Marketing
You’ve decided jogging will help you stay fit. But you also need to be consistent for the exercise to benefit your health. Similarly, if you’re only promoting your business every now and then, it’s not going to have the same effect. Look at the marketing you did last year, what worked and what didn’t? Does something need to change? Find out what promotions work well and do them regularly, it can be easy to forget that you need to attract new customers when the daily business operations get in the way. Be consistent and plan ahead.
2, Planning and Delegation
Which brings us to this next point. In order to be consistent you need to have a plan in place. This is a great time to create your Marketing Plan if you haven’t already done so. Have monthly, weekly, and even down to daily tasks so you can stay on track. If you find that you’re short on time, don’t try to do everything yourself! Delegate and let others help you! It might be worthwhile to enlist a Marketing agency to help with your planning and managing.
3, Who is your Product?
This might sound rather strange, but the people, the “WHO” should come before the product itself. This includes both your Customers and Staff. With so much competition around, simply having a product is not enough. People desire more in the form of experience, personable customer service, and the ‘story’ behind your product. Does your product tell a story? How can you relate that to people? Can your staff sell the story and engage your customers in the experience?
4, Keep up with new tech and learn new things!
With changes happening in marketing so quickly, it’s easy to fall behind. Specifically, online and digital marketing is evolving at a fast pace. Don’t be afraid to try new ways to reach your target market. Keep up with new developments in social media marketing, watch what other businesses are using and implement new strategies. Again, you might find a Marketing agency can help you with this if you don’t have the resources to do so in-house.
5, Community and Networking
Being part of the community is a great way to raise brand awareness. If you are local business, look for charitable causes you can contribute to and be part of, whether it be a homeless shelter, food bank, or local sports club, there are many opportunities for your business to be exposed in a positive and rewarding way. Similarly, join a business networking group to broaden your contacts, it could be industry related or geographical. You will find that these groups can help you build strategic alliances and be inspired with new ideas for your business.
6, Goal Setting &amp; be open for change
When you have thought about what worked and what didn’t last year, it’s now time to move forward and make it happen BUT be realistic in how you will get there. Your Marketing Plan should set a direction which you can achieve with specific marketing and promotional activities. For example, how do you achieve a X% increase in sales using Facebook advertising? What is your budget?
Finally, be open for change –test and measure the results of your promotions, be ready to make adjustments and changes; maybe you need to try a different audience setting. Again, learn new things and try! Test and measure the outcomes for 6 months and see how you go. Don’t get stuck on doing the same things if it’s not moving towards your goals.
So, what are your New Year’s Resolutions? Need a hand in giving your new year’s resolutions a kick start?
Concept Designs &amp; Marketing can help! We can assist you in creating a Marketing Plan so you can stay on track and be consistent, and all our packages, whether websites, SEO or Social Media Marketing, can all be tailored to your budget and goals.
Get in touch with our team today and let’s make 2018 a great year for your business!

#### One vital step most marketing agencies miss when starting a digital marketing campaign
When it comes to setting up digital marketing campaigns for their clients, there is one vital step that even some of the very best marketing agencies leave out, and that is a competitor analysis.

A Competitor analysis is an under-utilised tool that provides a sure-fire way to get quicker leads for your business. Just by implementing this one vital step into your digital marketing strategy, you’re guaranteed to experience quicker SEO results.
As experienced digital marketing in Sydney and Gold Coast, we have seen first-hand the incredible benefits and results that our competitor analysis has offered our clients.
Why is a Competitor Analysis Often Forgotten About?

People think they instinctively know what keywords people are Googling, yet forget to do the analysis to see if there are better keywords they should be using which they haven’t thought of yet
A Competitor analysis requires time and effort
Many agencies do not realise the importance of a competitor analysis
It should always be done before a campaign is started, and some clients may be impatient to get their campaign up and running without doing the due diligence beforehand

Why is a Competitor Analysis So Important?
A Competitor analysis should be the very first step that is taken in any digital marketing campaign. If you do not have this data, you will be kickstarting your campaign blindly.
That may sound a little dramatic, but let’s look at the analogy of a helicopter pilot. What are the four responsibilities of any helicopter pilot?

Plan the safest route to your desired destination
Survey the weather conditions before the trip commences
Ensures that weight is evenly distributed
Determine which path may be the most scenic

In many ways, a good competitor analysis can help your digital marketing strategy in the following ways:

Plans a route to your desired destination (improving your search engine rankings)
Survey the current industry landscape
Finds the ideal balance of which keywords to use for specific campaigns (what keywords to use for SEO and which to use for Google Ads)
Decides which content will be most engaging for your audience

Does this analogy paint a picture of what a competitor analysis can bring to the table? Both flying a helicopter and a competitor analysis give you a bird’s eye view of the broader picture and allows you to see things from a different perspective.
Did you know that through a competitor analysis, it is possible to get accurate answers with regards to what your target market is searching for on Google? This information alone can help you speed up your SEO results by as much as 75%.

#### Optimising Conversion Rates through Funnels
So now that we have an understanding on ‘Conversions’, it’s time to look into optimising your Conversion Rates in a little more detail. But first, you should set up your Conversion Funnel, so you can work out how to target your leads in step by step.
What is a Conversion Funnel?
You might have heard of people talking about Sales Funnels, which are in essence, Conversion Funnels in this case. Remember, we want to ultimately lead people to a sale. The word funnel implies that it is a step-by-step process, or from top to bottom. Typically, people should go through these steps:

Top of the Funnel (ToFu)

= Awareness and Interest

Middle of the Funnel (MoFu)

= Consideration and Evaluation

Bottom of the Funnel (BoFu)

= Action and Retention

Each phase should be optimised for Conversion, with its own set of goals. Last time we talked about the different types of Conversions. The best way to do optimise Conversion Rates is to understand each part of the Funnel and generate suitable content targeting the steps.
TOP OF THE FUNNEL:
This is the ‘widest’ part of the funnel. At this stage you are just trying to raise awareness and educate the general public about your business. Content at this stage are centred towards driving traffic to your website.
What to do – Impress your audience with an appealing front page and valuable content, for example, industry specific blog articles (make sure to use keywords), and invite people to sign-up with their email address using a built-in webform. Build up a social media presence showcasing helpful content, and encourage users to give reviews in order to build trust and referrals. Make yourself seen and known.
MIDDLE OF THE FUNNEL: 
At this stage, you have narrowed down some potential customers for further nurturing, or nudging down the funnel. This is where you need to stand out from your competitors. What makes you different? What is your USP (Unique Selling Proposition) and what extra benefit can you offer?
What to do – Make sure your website Design is not only appealing but also easy to navigate and optimisied for all devices. People are now evaluating and considering your business as a potential choice. They are looking deeper and exploring your site in more detail. You want people to STAY on your page and engage.
How? Throw a bone to hold their attention. For example, offer them a coupon, voucher, or free shipping. Perhaps you have an eBook, free resources, or demo video they’d like to download. Make use of the email addresses you collected at the ToFu and send them an Email Series to keep them interested, include links to specific landing pages designed with strong Call-to-Actions, such as “Shop Now” or “Book Now”.
As you can see, there’s more work to do at this phase as we push for the ultimate conversion, asking them to make a purchase. This is also a good time to make use of reviews, client testimonials, and anything else that gives you an edge over your competitors.
BOTTOM OF THE FUNNEL:
Congratulations! By now, you should have generated customers who are purchasing your product or using your services. However, just because they have made an action (purchase), doesn’t mean your work is over! This is the time to build a relationship with your new customer. You’d want repeat business and loyal customers who tell their friends about you.
What to do – Thank your customers! It’s easy to set up a “Thank You” page to follow up on the conversion, you can even Offer more on the page, to give them a ‘reward’, such as a discount code for the next purchase. This creates good feelings, and positive experiences encourage people to tell their friends about you!
As they are now a customer, you should also get to know them better. Ask them for a bit more information by asking them to update a “Profile” so you can target them with customised promotional offers. Make it sound like you want to help them, rather than just asking for more personal information. For example, say “Let us know what areas you’re interested in, so we can help you with…”
On the social media front, you can create helpful groups and invite your customers to join the community, again this builds relationships and trust. Give them a reason to stay loyal.
NOW TO OPTIMISING CONVERSIONS:
Last but not least, for each step of the way, remember to keep track of the Conversion Rates. For example, if you are targeting people to your website at the ToFu, check where people are dropping off on your pages so you can improve engagement, and set goals for each campaign. If you sent out an Email Series with a Call-to-Action of “Book Now”, track how many bookings are received within the number of emails sent.
Just a quick recap:
Conversion Rate = Number of Goal Achievements / People targeted
Tweak your content as you go to optimise the desired goal, whether it be downloading your eBook, or clicking on the “Shop Now” button. Perhaps it is the wording that needs changing, or an image that’s not working. By keeping track of your Conversion Rates, you can see how effective your content is working at each step of the funnel.
Now that you know what a Conversion Funnel is, and how to create content for each phase, it’s time to get to work! Feeling a bit overwhelmed by the whole process? Let Concept Designs and Marketing help! We have Conversion Rate Optimisation Packages that can help your businesses identify your target market, and ensuring your website is optimised for navigation and user experience, giving you that edge over your competitors.
Get in touch today!

#### Organic Reach Is Getting Tougher, So Your Strategy Needs To Get Smarter
Organic reach has become harder to earn across the major platforms, and the businesses feeling it are not beginners. Marketing teams with strong content, established audiences, and consistent posting schedules are still seeing fewer impressions, fewer views, and less reliable distribution than they did even a couple of years ago. The common thread is not effort. It is the environment.

Industry leaders have been signalling the same shift for a while. Social platforms are no longer primarily “social”. They are recommendation engines. Algorithms decide what people see based on predicted interests, not loyalty to the pages they follow. At the same time, content volume keeps climbing, which means every post competes with more creators, more ads, more formats, and more entertainment options than ever before. The result is a global squeeze on attention, and a growing number of businesses realising that organic reach is no longer something you can assume.
This matters because many businesses still operate like social media is a dependable distribution channel. Publish a post, reach your followers, drive clicks, repeat. That playbook is fading. Today, distribution is earned and re-earned daily, and even then it is not guaranteed. Brands that adapt are not panicking, but they are getting sharper. They are testing more, learning faster, and building visibility systems that do not rely on a single platform behaving the way it did in 2023.
Visibility now comes down to packaging and retention
One of the clearest signals coming out of the creator economy is that tiny details can produce massive differences in results. Leaders in video strategy have been pushing the idea that a strong piece of content can fail purely because the title is wrong, the thumbnail is weak, or the hook does not hold attention in the first few seconds.
Platforms are rewarding watch time, re-watches, saves, and meaningful engagement. That means “good content” is not just what you say. It is how quickly you earn attention and how well you keep it. Businesses need to think like publishers now. Every piece of content is competing in a crowded feed, and the winner is usually the one that is easiest to understand at a glance, makes a clear promise, and delivers value without fluff.
Why YouTube should be a core pillar in a diversified strategy
For businesses, YouTube is one of the strongest antidotes to shrinking organic reach because it plays a different role to most social platforms. It is not only a feed. It is also a search engine and a content library.
Well-structured YouTube content can keep working long after it is posted. It supports long-form authority, short-form discovery, live streaming, and community posts. It also gives businesses more room to teach, demonstrate, compare, and build trust in a way that is hard to do inside a 15-second Reel.
When organic distribution becomes less reliable, evergreen discovery becomes more valuable. That is why we see more industry leaders encouraging businesses to treat YouTube as an asset, not an experiment. One strong video can outperform weeks of short, forgettable posts, particularly if it is built around a clear audience problem and a specific outcome.
Where GEO and AI Search dovetails with this shift
The other major change sitting underneath the organic reach conversation is the rise of AI search behaviour. Buyers are increasingly using AI tools to research, compare, and shortlist before they click through to a website or reach out to a business. In many journeys, social media is no longer the starting point. It is the validation point.
This is exactly where GEO, Generative Engine Optimisation, matters. If AI-driven platforms cannot easily understand who you are, what you do, and why you are credible, your business can be excluded from the shortlists being formed invisibly in the background.
A strong social presence supports GEO because it provides proof of expertise, consistency, and relevance. YouTube supports it even further because it creates long-form content that can be cited, summarised, and referenced across the web. Together, they help your brand show up in more places, for more queries, and at more stages of the buyer journey.
The Concept Designs &amp; Marketing view
The goal is not to chase algorithms. The goal is to build a diversified visibility system.
That system includes platform-native social content that earns attention, YouTube content that builds long-term authority, and a GEO approach that increases your chances of being surfaced in AI search results. When one channel dips, the system still holds.
Organic reach is not “dead”, but it is harder, noisier, and more competitive. Businesses that win in 2026 will be the ones that stop relying on a single platform for consistent results, and start building visibility that travels.

#### Out-of-Date Websites are Easy Targets: Why a Spring Refresh Matters
If your website hasn’t been updated in a while, it is not just slow, it is unsafe. WordPress itself is solid, yet outdated plugins and themes create gaps and vulnerabilities that attackers routinely exploit.

What Happened in the Last Month

Weekly surge in disclosures. Wordfence recorded 43 vulnerabilities (38 plugins, 3 themes), jumping to 441 vulnerabilities (393 plugins, 16 themes), then another 93 vulnerabilities (83 plugins, 2 themes). These swings show how quickly risk can escalate.
High-profile plugin risk. On 11 Aug 2025, researchers submitted an Arbitrary File Read flaw affecting Slider Revolution (impacting over 4 million installs). Sites running older versions needed urgent patching.
Sustained researcher activity. Wordfence’s August 2025 monthly report logged 438 vulnerability submissions, underscoring the volume of issues found and fixed each month.

Why Older Sites are at Higher Risk

Unsupported software. Old PHP, CMS cores, themes, and plugins miss security patches.
Compatibility breaks. Newer patches can fail on outdated stacks, so owners delay updates, increasing exposure.
Attack automation. Once a flaw is disclosed, bots scan and exploit vulnerable versions within hours.

A Simple Plan to Get Safe and Stay Safe

Audit your website. Inventory plugins, themes, PHP version, and hosting configuration.
Patch and replace. Update supported tools, replace abandonware and plugins that are no longer being updated, and remove what you do not use.
Harden security. Review your website admin users, enable a Web Application Firewall, set daily off-site backups, and add uptime monitoring.
Modernise performance. Improve Core Web Vitals with image optimisation, caching, and consider a CDN. Faster sites convert better and are easier to protect.
Schedule maintenance. Monthly updates, quarterly plugin reviews, an annual platform refresh keep technical debt low and 6-monthly speed optimisation.

Hosting Matters &#8211; the Hidden Cost of Cheap Hosting

FAQs
1. Why is my WordPress website at risk if I haven&#8217;t updated it? 
Outdated plugins, themes, and core files create security gaps that hackers exploit. Even if WordPress itself is secure, failing to update components puts your site at risk.
2. What happens when a plugin vulnerability is disclosed? 
Once a vulnerability becomes public, bots can scan for and attack affected websites within hours. Fast patching is critical to avoid compromise.
3. How often are new WordPress plugin vulnerabilities found? 
Every week. In August 2025 alone, Wordfence reported hundreds of plugin and theme vulnerabilities. Unmaintained sites are highly exposed.
4. Can cheap hosting increase my security risk? 
Yes. Low-cost hosts often skip essential updates and security hardening. This leaves your website vulnerable to malware, slowdowns, and downtime.
5. What is the best way to secure an outdated WordPress site? 
Start with a full audit. Update all plugins, themes, and core files, remove unused tools, and enable daily backups and a web application firewall.
6. How often should I update my website plugins and themes? 
Update plugins and themes monthly. Review your plugin stack quarterly and refresh your platform annually to minimise risk.
7. Why do older websites load slower? 
Outdated sites lack image optimisation, modern caching, and performance tuning. This affects user experience, SEO, and AI visibility.
8. Does site speed affect my ranking or visibility in AI search? 
Yes. Site speed plays a role in how search engines and AI tools assess quality and reliability. Faster websites are easier for crawlers and AI models to process, which can improve visibility, indexing accuracy, and citation likelihood.
9. What’s the risk of keeping abandoned plugins on my site? 
Abandoned plugins no longer receive security patches. Keeping them installed gives attackers a known way to gain access to your site.
10. How can I improve my website&#8217;s visibility and security this spring?

#### Search Engine Marketing with Google AdWords
So your business has a website, and you might have done SEO on it. Now you can sit back and wait for your customers to find you, right? Well, SEO is certainly important, but let’s not forget SEM, or Search Engine Marketing. Increasingly businesses are turning to Google AdWords for SEM, on top of SEO. Why you may wonder? Have you heard of AdWords but not sure if it’s for your business? Read on…
How it works:
AdWords are paid searches that position your Ad in Google search results, Google products (eg. YouTube), and thousands of websites in Google Adsense. By matching keywords with the Ads you create, your Ad shows when someone searches for similar terms, or visits a website with related content. AdWords is designed to be shown on multiple devices; including desktop, laptop, tablet or mobile device, making it highly flexible with great potential for reach.
Pay only for clicks:
With cost-per-click (CPC) bidding, you&#8217;re charged only when someone clicks on your Ad and go to your website. You have control over your AdWords budget that suits your campaign. You tell AdWords the most you&#8217;re willing to pay for a click on your Ad and you decide the average amount you want to spend each day.
Targeted &amp; more immediate results:
SEO can take time to build organic traffic, so if your business is quite new in the market and want to gain exposure quickly, or if you just want a boost on your existing business, then AdWords can help you achieve more immediate visibility. Your Ad appears when someone searches for terms related to your product or service, and the advertising is targeted to your specific demographic audience at the time you want.
AdWords is actually a very cost-effective way to complement SEO for any business, and it’s no wonder that AdWords has evolved into Google’s main source of revenue at close to $50 billion per year. When you advertise with AdWords, you&#8217;re making a financial investment in your business. However it takes more than just money to see success. It is important that your AdWords campaign is implemented wisely and that you regularly examine the analytics, performance, and make adjustments to bring you a successful ROI.

#### Sell More on Instagram Organically
Social media platforms have transformed the way we do marketing and promotion. While using the paid advertising features can be helpful, you should also build an organic marketing strategy to complement your promotional efforts.

Many are misled to believe that it’s impossible to sell on Instagram without paid advertising. However, this is not true. Instagram is an essential part of your brand presence and many direct-to-consumer brands have built successful businesses on Instagram, using an organic strategy and turning it into their main sales channel.
Let us look at some ways that you can grow your business organically on Instagram:
People and Community
First things first, start with clearly defining your target audience. Without knowing who your audience is, you cannot formulate a consistent and effective strategy. This means figuring out the age, gender, location, problems they are facing and how your product or service can provide a solution.
When you know whom you’re trying to reach, then you need to build up your community. This includes allocating time responding to comments, messages, and feedback, as well as interacting with followers and encouraging discussion. Remember, Instagram is a social networking platform after all, and posts that build community are not only preferred but also contribute to organic growth.
Plan Your Posts
Next, you need to plan your posts and ensure that each post you publish counts. Before you post, ask yourself what it is trying to achieve, what is the objective and purpose? For example, are you aiming to announce a new product, or start a conversation? It is important to set a clear goal and direction for each post.
While having a variety of content helps with engagement (and no one wants to see pushy sales posts every time!), it is important to have a consistent image and style. Keep to your brand colours and content style, whether it be images, videos, and even the content wording.
If you’re stuck on ideas, you can always check out other successful Instagram accounts for inspiration. See what type of content works, for example, you can always provide helpful suggestions, instructions, tips and interesting titbits that relate to your industry.
More than a Link in Bio
Unlike other platforms such as Facebook where you can paste a clickable link in the post, Instagram takes a bit more effort. However, that doesn’t mean you should leave out your CTA. There are various ways to ask followers to ‘click’ through other than just the link in your bio, such as putting links in:

Instagram Stories
Shopping tags on images that feature your products or services
Direct messaging with followers
In the captions of your IGTV or reel videos
Extended “Link in Bio”, where you can use multi-link landing page tools such as LinkTree or Link-in Profile to create that drive traffic to specific areas of your website

#### SEO vs GEO: Why Your Strategy Needs Both
For years, SEO has helped businesses show up in the right place at the right time. But the way people search is evolving. With AI now playing a growing role in how content is discovered and presented, a new approach is taking shape. It’s called GEO, and it’s designed to complement—not replace—your SEO efforts.

What is SEO?
Search Engine Optimisation (SEO) is the process of improving a website’s visibility in organic search results, primarily on Google. It’s about understanding what people are searching for, and ensuring your website provides valuable, relevant answers. SEO focuses on optimising content, keywords, meta data, website structure, mobile responsiveness, speed, and backlinks to improve rankings.
What is GEO?
GEO, or Generative Engine Optimisation, is a newer approach that prepares content to be discoverable by AI-powered search engines like Google’s Search Generative Experience (SGE) also called Google Overviews, and AI assistants such as ChatGPT or Perplexity AI. Rather than relying only on keywords, GEO focuses on structuring content in a way that Large Language Models (LLMs) can interpret, summarise, and serve up directly in response to user prompts.
Why GEO Matters Now
AI-powered search is changing how users find information. Instead of browsing through search results, users increasingly receive direct answers in the form of AI summaries. That means your content needs to be formatted in a way that LLMs can understand and trust.
Google has made it clear that it values content with clear authorship, expertise, and structure. GEO is how you align with those expectations. It’s not about replacing SEO. It’s about adding another layer to your search strategy so your content is discoverable across both traditional and AI-generated results.
SEO vs GEO: What&#8217;s the Difference?
Let’s take a look at some of the key distinctions between SEO and GEO:

It’s Not SEO or GEO: It’s Both
You don’t have to choose between SEO and GEO. In fact, if you want to future-proof your visibility online, you need both. SEO helps your audience find you through traditional search, while GEO ensures your content is accessible to AI models shaping the future of search.
At Concept Designs &amp; Marketing, we help businesses navigate this evolving digital world with strategies that combine SEO fundamentals with AI-readiness. If you haven’t thought about how AI search is impacting your visibility, now is the time.

#### SEO, AEO and GEO Explained for AI Search Visibility
Why Search Visibility Is No Longer Just About Ranking On Google
After more than 24 years in digital marketing, I have seen plenty of changes.
I have watched businesses move from print directories to websites, from websites to Google rankings, from rankings to paid search, from paid search to social media, and now into a new phase where AI is influencing how people find, compare, and choose who they want to work with.

Some shifts feel like a change in platform. This one is bigger than that. It is changing the way buyers make decisions.
People are no longer only typing a few words into Google, clicking through to websites, and building a shortlist themselves. They are asking better questions. They are using AI tools to compare options. They are reading summaries before they ever contact a business.
That does not mean SEO is no longer important. Quite the opposite.
It means SEO now needs to work alongside two other layers of visibility: AEO and GEO.
SEO helps search engines find and rank your website.
AEO helps your content answer the questions buyers are already asking.
GEO helps AI tools understand, summarise, and recommend your business.
The businesses that understand all three will be in a stronger position as search behaviour continues to change.
Why This Matters To Your Business
Most of my work in digital marketing has always come back to one core question.
How do we facilitate the right people find the right business?
The answer used to be more straightforward. Build a good website. Optimise it properly. Create content around the right keywords. Improve rankings. Drive traffic. Convert enquiries.
That still matters. But it no longer tells the whole story.
A buyer can now ask an AI tool who the best providers are, what questions they should ask, what red flags to look for, how businesses compare, and which option might be the best fit.
That means part of the decision making process can happen before someone ever lands on your website.
Over the past few years, our team at Concept Designs &amp; Marketing has completed more than 200 market competitor analyses. That work has given us a very clear view of how businesses are positioned online, how competitors are showing up, and where gaps are forming.
Since 2023, we have been looking closely at how businesses appear across AI search tools, including ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Gemini, Claude, and Perplexity.
One of the most interesting things we are seeing is this:
The best business in a market is not always the business being recommended.
That can be confronting for business owners, because many have strong reputations, excellent client relationships, years of experience, and genuine expertise. But their online presence does not always communicate that clearly.
Their website may look professional, but the wording is too broad. Their services may be valuable, but the content is too thin. Their difference may be obvious in conversation, but almost invisible online.
AI tools can only work with what they can find, understand, and verify.
If your digital footprint does not clearly explain who you help, what you do, why you are credible, and how you are different, your business may be left out of the conversation.
SEO Is Still The Foundation
Search Engine Optimisation is the part most business owners are already familiar with. SEO is the work that helps your website show up when someone searches on Google or another search engine.
Good SEO helps search engines crawl, understand, and rank your website. It also helps people find the right information quickly once they arrive.
Strong SEO usually includes:
Clear service pages
Keyword research
Page titles and meta descriptions
Technical website health
Internal linking
Helpful blog content
Local SEO
Google Business Profile optimisation
Website speed and user experience
Reviews, links, and authority signals
SEO gives your website structure, and it helps each page focus on the right topic. It makes your services clearer. It gives search engines stronger signals about what your business should be found for.
This foundation still matters because AI tools also need information to draw from. They need clear signals about who you are, what you do, who you help, and why your business is credible.
A weak website foundation makes everything else harder.
If your content is vague, outdated, duplicated, or too generic, search engines and AI tools have less to work with.
3. Trust and authority signals
AI search is not just about content. It is also about credibility.
Trust and authority signals include reviews, consistent business information, expert content, third-party mentions, case studies, relevant backlinks, and a strong overall digital footprint.
These signals help shape how your business is perceived, not only by potential customers, but also by the platforms and systems interpreting information about your brand.
A business with stronger trust signals is more likely to be taken seriously. A business with weak or inconsistent signals may struggle to be recommended, even if it offers an excellent service.
That is why building authority online is no longer optional. It is part of how businesses stay visible as buyer behaviour changes.
AEO Helps You Answer The Questions Buyers Are Asking
AEO stands for Answer Engine Optimisation.
This is less about chasing short keywords and more about answering the questions your buyers are already asking.
People rarely move from problem to purchase in one step. They research. They compare. They ask questions. They look for reassurance before they take action.
AEO is about building content around these kinds of questions.
That may include detailed FAQs, question based blogs, practical guides, comparison content, clear service page sections, and plain English explanations.
The goal is not to fill a page with keywords. The goal is to be genuinely useful.
Good AEO content helps buyers understand their problem, consider their options, and feel more confident about what to do next.
It also gives search engines and AI assisted search experiences clearer content to use when they generate answers.
GEO Is The Newer Layer Of Search Visibility
GEO stands for Generative Engine Optimisation.
This is the newer piece of the puzzle.
GEO looks at how your business appears when AI tools generate answers, recommendations, summaries, and comparisons.
The answer an AI tool gives may be shaped by your website, but it is rarely only shaped by your website.
AI tools may also look at your reviews, directories, articles, interviews, social profiles, business listings, case studies, media mentions, and other third party sources.
This is why GEO is not just a website task.
It is about your wider digital footprint.
Your business needs to be clear and consistent across the places AI tools may use to understand who you are and why you should be considered.
What We Are Seeing In Our AI Search Work
Our AI Search Audit and Market Competitor Analysis work has highlighted a few common patterns.
The first is that many businesses assume AI tools will understand them because their website looks good, and that is not always the case.
A visually polished website can still have weak content. It may not explain the services clearly. It may not include the questions buyers are asking. It may not show enough proof, detail, or authority.
The second pattern is that many businesses use broad language.
They say they are experienced, trusted, client focused, and results driven. Those phrases may be true, but they do not give search engines or AI tools enough specific information.
The third pattern is that competitors are sometimes being recommended because they have clearer content, stronger third party mentions, better structured answers, or more consistent information across the web.
The fourth pattern is that AI visibility can vary between platforms.
A business may appear in Perplexity but not ChatGPT. It may be mentioned in Google AI Overviews but not Gemini. It may be recommended for one search prompt and completely missing for another.
This is why AI search visibility is not a one time fix, it needs ongoing review, content improvement, competitor tracking, and authority building.
The Difference Between SEO, AEO, And GEO
A simple way to think about it is this.
SEO asks, can search engines find, understand, and rank your website?
AEO asks, can your content answer a buyer’s question clearly?
GEO asks, can AI tools understand your business well enough to include it in a generated answer?
Each one supports the others.
SEO gives your website the foundation.
AEO makes your content more useful and easier to extract into answers.
GEO strengthens how your business is understood across AI generated search experiences.
Businesses that only focus on SEO may miss opportunities inside AI tools and answer based search results.
Businesses that only focus on AI search without fixing their website foundation may struggle because AI tools still need reliable information to work with.
The strongest approach is to build all three together.
Where Concept Designs &amp; Marketing Fits In
This is the work we have moved deeper into at Concept Designs &amp; Marketing.
We help businesses understand how they are being found, compared, and selected across both traditional search and AI search.
Our Market Competitor Analysis looks at where a business sits in the market, who they are competing against, what competitors are doing well, and where opportunities exist.
Our AI Search Audit looks at how a business appears across AI tools, where it is missing, which competitors are being recommended instead, and what content or authority gaps need attention.
This gives business owners a clearer starting point.
Instead of guessing what to write, what to optimise, or which marketing activity to prioritise, they can make decisions based on insight.
That has always been my approach to marketing&#8230;&#8230;Strategy first. Activity second.
More content, more ads, or more website changes will not solve the problem if the direction is unclear.
Frequently Asked Questions About SEO, AEO, And GEO
What is the difference between SEO, AEO, and GEO?
SEO helps your website rank in search engines. AEO helps your content answer specific buyer questions. GEO helps your business appear in AI generated responses, summaries, comparisons, and recommendations.
Is SEO still important now that AI search is growing?
Yes. SEO is still essential because search engines and AI tools both need clear, well structured, and credible content to understand your business. SEO gives your website the foundation needed for broader search visibility.
What does AEO mean in marketing?
AEO means Answer Engine Optimisation. It focuses on creating content that answers the questions people ask before they choose a business, product, or service.
What does GEO mean in digital marketing?
GEO means Generative Engine Optimisation. It is the process of improving how your business is understood, cited, summarised, or recommended by AI tools and AI powered search experiences.
Why is my business not appearing in ChatGPT or AI search tools?
Your business may not have enough clear, consistent, or credible information online. Your website content may be too vague, your services may not be explained in enough detail, or competitors may have stronger content and external signals.
How can I improve my business visibility in AI search?
Start by improving your website content, service pages, FAQs, reviews, case studies, directory listings, and external mentions. AI tools need clear signals from multiple sources to understand and recommend a business confidently.
Do FAQs help with AI search visibility?
Yes. FAQs can help because they match the way people ask questions in search engines and AI tools. Clear question and answer content makes it easier for your business to be understood and referenced.
How does a Market Competitor Analysis support SEO and AI search?
A Market Competitor Analysis shows how your business compares against competitors, what they are doing well, where your gaps are, and what opportunities exist to improve your visibility.
What is an AI Search Audit?
An AI Search Audit reviews how your business appears across AI tools and AI assisted search experiences. It can identify where your business is visible, where it is missing, who is being recommended instead, and what content or authority gaps need attention.
Should businesses focus on SEO, AEO, or GEO first?
Most businesses should start with SEO because it creates the foundation. AEO and GEO can then build on that foundation by improving how your content answers questions and how your business appears in AI generated search results.

#### Should I Still Invest in SEO?
With AI tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Google’s Overviews (Search Generative Experience) changing how people find information online, many business owners are starting to ask: Is SEO still worth it? It’s a fair question. But the answer isn’t yes or no &#8211; it’s about evolving your strategy to suit how people search now.

SEO Isn’t Over. It’s Evolving.
Search engine optimisation (SEO) remains a core part of digital marketing. It helps your website appear in Google search results, builds authority, and drives traffic. But the search landscape is changing.
Today, AI-powered tools often summarise answers directly on the results page. Users might get what they need without clicking through to your website. That shift doesn’t mean SEO is obsolete. It means your approach needs to include Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO), a strategy focused on visibility in AI search.
Why SEO Still Matters
Google still dominates search, especially in Australia. AI tools rely heavily on content from trusted websites, and many of those gain credibility through strong SEO performance.
Good SEO not only improves your search rankings, it also strengthens your domain authority, brand trust and user experience. All of these remain essential for traditional search and for ensuring AI tools treat your content as a reliable source.
The Future: SEO + GEO
The most future-ready strategy combines both. GEO focuses on making your content readable and referenceable for AI. This involves:

Structuring your content clearly
Using long-tail and question-based keywords
Getting cited in reputable sources
Publishing expert-driven, fact-checked content

SEO builds the foundation. GEO builds visibility in new search spaces. Together, they keep your brand discoverable across all forms of search.
What to Do Now
So, should you keep investing in SEO? Absolutely. But it is important to diversify your digital marketing strategy by including a GEO campaign, to stay ahead of where search is heading.
Check your readiness now. Try our free AI Visibility Calculator and find out how well your business shows up in AI search.
FAQs
1. Is SEO still important for future digital marketing?
Yes. SEO continues to improve your Google rankings and helps AI tools trust and understand your content.
2. What’s the difference between SEO and GEO?
SEO targets Google rankings. GEO (Generative Engine Optimisation) focuses on getting your content cited in AI-generated answers.
3. Can I do GEO without SEO?
Not effectively. SEO builds the authority that AI tools rely on when generating responses.
4. Will SEO alone help me show up in AI search?
Not always. You will also need structured content, expert insights and citations from trusted sources.
5. Does Google still matter for search?
Absolutely. Google holds more than 90% of Australia’s search market and remains a key source for AI platforms.
6. Is GEO replacing SEO?
No. GEO builds on top of SEO. The two work best when used together.
7. How do I optimise for both SEO and AI search?
Use clear headings, FAQs, structured data, expert sources and build reputable backlinks.
8. Will SEO help me appear in ChatGPT?
Indirectly, yes. AI tools often pull from reputable websites, and strong SEO helps establish that reputation.
9. Should I stop my SEO campaigns?
Not at all. But you should update your approach to include GEO and AI-readability.
10. How do I get started with SEO and GEO together?
Begin by auditing your content’s clarity and structure, improve on-page SEO and explore your AI visibility using our free score tool.

#### Should You Boost Post or do Facebook Ads? What’s The Difference?
Facebook is a great social media platform for marketing, you can gain exposure and engagement by simply posting content. However, many businesses also rely on paid advertising to increase reach and boost their presence on Facebook.
Why? If you can post for free, why pay for advertising? With digital technology and mobile devices widely available, it makes sharing content much easier. This leads to a staggering increase in posts that appear in a user’s newsfeed. That is, on average, 1,500 stories each time a user logs on! And if your users happen to have many ‘friends’ or follow many pages, then as many as 15,000 potential stories could appear!1
As you can see, organic reach (unpaid, free reach) is becoming less reliable in getting your posts exposed, imagine competing with the average of 1,500 stories for the attention of your user! If your business isn’t advertising on Facebook, you’re missing out!
So what’s the difference between a Boost Post and a Facebook Ad?
A Boost Post is simply having your published post appear in front of more people (hopefully leading to more engagement in terms of Likes, Comments, or Shares), by paying Facebook to extend its reach. Boost Post allows you to select your audience (such as location, gender, age, interests). It is very easy to set up on your company page with the click of a “Boost Post” button located at the bottom right of your post:

A Facebook Ad on the other hand, has a lot more options. You will need to set up a Facebook Ad in ‘Ads Manager’, where you’ll be asked to specify an Objective for your Ad. This could range from Awareness &#8211; such as ‘reach’; Considerations – such as ‘engagement’ (eg. Page Likes); or Conversion – to get people to take action and make a purchase for example.

In some instances, you can even do a “Split Test” to see which Ad performs better.
In short, Facebook Ads have many more features to tailor your Ad with a specific goal and to the right people by the way it looks. You can create a video Ad, a slideshow, carousel, or use multiple images adding information and captions. The post will also have an extra button based on your Objective, such as a “Sign Up” button for people to take action. Depending on the Ad itself, it can also appear on Instagram and the Right Side bar of the user’s page. Boost Posts do not have that ability.
Lastly, as Facebook Ads are created specifically to be an Advertisement, it will not appear on your Business Page. This allows you to monitor your Ad strictly for the purpose of advertising, you can even exclude those who’ve already Liked your page so you can focus on just reaching those new customers.
In summary, if you just need some extra reach and engagement for your posts, then Boost Post is easy to get started in giving you some exposure. However, if you’d like something specific to happen, for example, increasing the number of followers on your page, or getting them to take action such as ‘Sign Up’ for an event, then Facebook Ads are better suited.
Still unsure which way to go or simply don&#8217;t have the necessary time to spend on Facebook for your business? We will sit down with you to discuss your goals, your social media marketing plan and where you can improve your overall Facebook marketing to optimise the advertising budget. Get in touch today!

#### Simply Understanding Duplicate Content
Duplicate Content is a common problem in the cyberspace. In fact, Raven has conducted a study between 2013 and 2015 and found that 29% of crawled pages are duplicates ratio being 71 pages out of 243 pages have been duplicated.
For Site Owners: Does it Matter if the content published is Duplicated?
Yes. For site owners, it would really matter. Duplicate content plays a big role in impacting web traffic and search engine rankings. How so?

Search engines such as Google, Bing, and Yahoo only shows one version of the same content that is most likely to provide the best content for every enquiry searched &#8211; diluting visibility of duplicates published.
Inbound links from other websites is a factor too. Imaging posting an original piece of content and having multiple websites duplicate it. Chances are some of your supposed inbound links and generated traffic would be transferred to them as they duplicated content from your website to theirs.

How can you avoid Duplicate Content?
Listed below are multiple ways and most common ways to avoid this from happening:

Use 301 redirect
As a site owner, using 301 redirects is one of the best options to increase relevance and popularity as the potential to rank a page is being focused to one main page.
Use Rel=”canonical”
A canonical version simply means a preferred version out of the many duplicates. It helps search engines identify which page should get the ranking point.

Other methods that can be done to fix duplicate content issues are:

Usage of Meta Robots NoIndex which allows all contents published to be crawled but not indexed by search engines.
Making sure that there is consistency in internal linking within a website.
Adding a self-referential canonical link to all published pages within the website to thwart off scrapers.
Reminding syndicating website to add complete URL of your content rather than a variation of the URL.
