#### Six Key Ideas to Graphic Design
‘A Picture says a Thousand Words’, but what words do they say?
If you doubt the power of images then look at these trademarks which are recognised all around the world
• McDonalds
• Nike
• Cross
• Starbucks
• Crescent
Already for good or bad, you have associated meaning to these symbols but what it is not is neutral. For some people it has positive meaning, for others negative.
When considering your graphic design and logo, take a moment to ask yourself these following two questions:

What does my audience see when they see my logo, my brochures and my advertising?
How do I define myself, my service and my product to my customers?

&nbsp;
Here are six graphic design tips to consider when branding your product or service:
&nbsp;
1. Keep your graphic design simple
By simple I do not mean dumbing down your ideas but rather creating ideas that are profound and yet simple.
To do this you need to define what is core to your business. It could be value for money, quality workmanship, a high level of experience, that you are innovative, that you are an award winner.
What is it that you want people to know? Search for the one or two key things that make you stand out from the rest and that you can deliver on.
&nbsp;
2. Have an unexpected twist in your graphic design
How do you hook your audience to pay attention to your ideas and sustain their interest? For an idea to endure you must generate interest and curiosity, don’t make your message predictable, cliché nor gimmicky.
&nbsp;
3. People need to know you are credible
How do you make people believe you service, brand or product is better than your competitor? In your graphic design, reveal the credentials of your business or event. Who are you associated with? Are you a member of any groups or associations?
Space is key to any graphic design you prepare so always drive people to your website where they can flick through the pages of your business and find the pieces to complete your picture.
&nbsp;
4. Make your graphic design and images clear and concrete
Research suggests that our brains are wired to remember concrete data but the question is how do we make our ideas clear so they mean the same thing to everyone in our audience? Always include concrete imagery to accompany your carefully crafted message, mission statements, strategies and visions.
&nbsp;
5. Tap into an emotive experience
We are all naturally wired to feel things for people, not abstractions. So how do you encourage people to care about your product, your service or your brand? Key to this is helping people to feel something and to evoke an emotion. It may be an emotion of enjoyment, anticipation, security, workmanship or belonging. The key is determining which emotion to evoke in your designing.
&nbsp;
6. Use graphic design to tell a story
How do you get people to act on your ideas? You tell stories. Help people see themselves in the story of your brand, product or service. Help people dream about the story and help people complete the end to the story you are advertising.
&nbsp;
As Steve Jobs said, “Creativity is connecting things”. Take these six tips and connect them together and make your idea, brand, product or service stand out more than the business that follows you. When scanning Google or trolling the internet, remind me why I should pick your product and not the next person.
Feel free to contact us if you have any further questions regarding this article or if we can help in any way with your graphic design needs.

#### Social Media is Here to Stay – Embrace it for your business!
If you haven’t noticed, social media has changed the world over the recent years! And if your business hasn’t embraced social media as part of your marketing strategy, it’s not too late to start now and take advantage of this great tool to reach your market.
Social Media is Changing the World:
Social Media has made a great impact in the way we communicate and relate to each other. You can connect with friends across the globe, share your life with others, and create online communities that bring people together without geographic boundaries with the click of a button.
Before Social Media came along, we relied on more traditional forms of individual contact, such as phone calls or letters. #### Staying Competitive with Innovation
Nowadays and more than ever, business owners are faced with the challenge of adapting and keeping up with a rapidly evolving digital world. The marketplace has become increasingly competitive thanks to digitalisation, and to stay competitive you need to be innovative.

In other words, you need to be come up with ways to provide enhanced customer experiences, by solving problems and adding value through creative solutions, especially through the use of new technologies!

#### The Five Things Business Owners Need to Do for a Successful Marketing Campaign
Despite the growing popularity in entrepreneurship and new start-ups, data tells us that unfortunately, over half of businesses do not succeed beyond the first three years, with 20% failing in their first year^.
While there are varied factors that contribute to this statistic, Marketing is often one of the key reasons. 
What many businesses owners don’t realise, is that successful marketing requires solid elements in a campaign.
Here are 5 things that you need to do before you start marketing:
1) Why your Business?
This might seem like a simple question. However, if you cannot think of how you are providing a solution, then you cannot build a strong campaign. Why should people choose your business? What makes you better than others, and how are your products or services helping people?
2) Who are your customers?
It goes without saying, a business can not continue, without customers, but it’s super important to determine your target market so that you can direct your marketing efforts towards them. Is your business serving the local community, or do you have an online business that cover a wide area? What are the characteristics and demographics of the audience you want to reach? Be specific and come up with a ‘typical customer avatar’ that you can envision buying your product or service.
3) Communicating to your customers
Now that you know who and where your customers are, what message do you want to communicate? How would they typically receive your key messages, and what channels would be the best way to reach them? This will help you formulate your marketing strategies for your campaign, and also keep you on track and focused on building your customer base.
4) Intentional Marketing
Reactive marketing tends to be a default for many business owners, which causes them to fall into the trap of spending money unnecessarily on marketing avenues that may not be the best fit for their business. This is like taking a stab in the dark and having a scatter-gun approach. While it’s a good idea to try different marketing methods, nothing beats intentional, proactive marketing.
A solid marketing plan that has been developed for the months ahead prevents the pitfalls of reactive marketing and causes you to take a purposeful look at your marketing and the avenues that are best suited to your business.
5) Marketing Strategy Mix 
Again, while your marketing campaign should include a combination of strategies, they need to be the right mix for your audience. Even if your budget is limited, you need to consider the extent of your resources, and identify the best strategy for you to be focusing on. For example, if your business is serving a local area, then a combination of social media marketing, local SEO/ Google My Business, and word-of-mouth referral strategies may suit.

AI Search Strategy

Get cited in authoritative sources like news sites, Wikipedia, and industry blogs.

In the dynamic world of digital marketing, change is a constant. Our previous blog delved into Google’s big algorithm updates and how often Google released updates. Given the relentless access millions have to the digital space every second, it&#8217;s understandable why Google, the world’s largest search engine, continually refines its algorithms to effectively manage its ever-growing user base and to try to provide the best user experience.
If you&#8217;ve ever been frustrated searching for, as an example, the perfect sofa bed on Google and you’ve been coming up short, you&#8217;ve experienced the fluctuating nature of Google’s search engine algorithms. #### The Importance of Optimising Your New Website Before Going Live: Avoiding the Pitfalls of Losing Google Rankings
Launching a new website is an exciting milestone for any business. However, amidst the excitement, it is crucial not to overlook a critical aspect: optimising the website for search engines before going live. Failure to do so can result in the loss of hard-earned Google rankings, which can significantly impact your online visibility and organic traffic. In this blog, we emphasise the importance of optimising your new website and highlight the potential consequences if this crucial step is neglected.

Preserve Your Google Rankings: Your existing website may have gained valuable rankings on search engine results pages (SERPs) over time. However, without proper optimisation of your new website, you risk losing these rankings overnight. To prevent this, it is essential to ensure that your new website is search engine-friendly and aligned with SEO best practices.
Prioritise On-Page SEO Elements: Before going live with your new website, conduct a thorough review of on-page SEO elements. Pay close attention to optimising meta titles, descriptions, header tags, URLs, and image alt text. Implementing relevant keywords, creating unique and compelling content, and ensuring proper internal linking can significantly impact your website&#8217;s search visibility and user experience.
Redirect Old URLs: When launching a new website, URLs may change or be restructured. Failing to redirect the old URLs to their corresponding new pages can result in a high number of broken links and negatively impact user experience. Implementing proper 301 redirects will not only maintain the user journey but also preserve your previous search rankings and authority.
Mobile Responsiveness and Page Speed: In today&#8217;s mobile-centric world, optimising your website for mobile devices is paramount. Ensure that your new website is fully responsive, providing an optimal browsing experience across various screen sizes. Additionally, prioritise optimising page speed by compressing images, minifying code, and leveraging caching techniques. A fast-loading website not only improves user experience but also contributes to higher search engine rankings.
Conduct a Competitor Analysis: A competitor analysis is a valuable exercise that provides insights into how Google perceives your website compared to your competitors. Before going live, conduct a thorough analysis of your competitors&#8217; SEO strategies, keyword rankings, backlink profiles, and overall online presence. This analysis will help identify areas for improvement, refine your SEO approach, and stay ahead of the competition.

Optimising your new website before going live is a crucial step that should not be overlooked. Failing to do so can result in the loss of Google rankings, which can have a significant impact on your online visibility and organic traffic. By prioritising on-page SEO elements, redirecting old URLs, ensuring mobile responsiveness, and conducting a competitor analysis, you set the stage for a successful website launch and continued search engine success.

#### The Winning Formula: How AI Search, Google SEO &#038; Google Ads Work Together
AI Search tools are changing how people find and interact with businesses online. While Google remains a dominant platform in search, AI-driven search engines like ChatGPT and PerplexityAI are capturing more attention, especially among younger users. To stay competitive, businesses need more than a one-track approach. The solution? A hybrid search strategy that combines the strengths of AI search, Google SEO, and Google Ads.

Why a One-Dimensional Search Strategy Won’t Work Anymore
Google SEO Alone Isn’t Enough
While Google continues to drive significant traffic, AI search is shifting how content is consumed. Instead of browsing multiple websites, users now receive AI-generated summaries, which reduces click-throughs from traditional search results.
AI Search Alone Won’t Cover Everything
AI search excels at surfacing quick answers, but it isn’t yet a full replacement for intent-driven searches that lead to conversions. Google remains a high-performing channel for lead generation, and its advertising capabilities offer fast visibility you can’t get through organic means alone.
How to Create a Well-Rounded Search Strategy
1. Optimise for AI Search

Publish content in formats that AI engines prioritise: FAQ-style pages, expert blogs, and concise answers to direct questions.
Get cited on reputable sources like Wikipedia, news outlets, and industry sites.
Build a presence on platforms commonly scraped by AI, such as LinkedIn, YouTube, and Google Business Profile.

This approach is part of what’s now known as Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) &#8211; a method for positioning your content so it’s discoverable by AI tools and included in generative search responses.
2. Strengthen Your Google SEO

Target keywords that still deliver strong traffic through Google Search.
Optimise your Google Business Profile and keep your NAP (Name, Address, Phone) details up-to-date for local SEO.
Build internal links, improve page load speeds, and secure backlinks to increase domain authority in the long term.

3. Use Google Ads to Capture High-Intent Leads

Launch campaigns targeting users with strong purchasing intent.
Retarget visitors across YouTube and Google Display Networks to keep your brand top of mind.
Experiment with AI-assisted ad formats to align with evolving user behaviour.

The Result? A Comprehensive Search Strategy That Works Across All Platforms.
Why Integration is the Key
No single channel can carry your entire digital marketing strategy anymore. AI is reshaping how users find and consume content, but Google’s scale and paid reach still play a crucial role. Integrating AI search optimisation or GEO, SEO best practices, and Google Ads ensures your business is covered from all angles.

#### UGC Ads in 2026: What They Are, Why They Work, and How Businesses Should Use Them
User generated content, often shortened to UGC, is still a valuable part of digital advertising. The difference now is that it is no longer a new trend. It has become a standard part of how many businesses approach paid social, short form video, and creator led campaigns.

Getting this right matters. It helps businesses create better campaigns, choose the right ad format, and produce content that supports both ad performance and AI search visibility.
What are UGC ads?
UGC ads are paid ads that use content designed to feel real, relatable, and natural to the platform. This content may come from a genuine customer, a creator working with a brand, or a business producing content in a casual, social first style.
Where UGC style ads are being used

Meta Ads: Businesses use testimonial clips, creator videos, founder content, and partnership ads across Facebook and Instagram placements.
TikTok Ads: TikTok remains one of the strongest platforms for natural, creator led content that blends into the feed.
YouTube and short form video campaigns: Social style video can work well in YouTube Shorts and other video campaigns where attention needs to be won quickly.
Website landing pages and remarketing: UGC style content can also improve trust on landing pages, support remarketing campaigns, and create better message consistency across channels.

Types of UGC
Many businesses now use UGC as a broad label, but there are actually a few different content types that sit within this space.

Customer UGC: This is content created by real customers who are sharing their own experience with a product or service.

Creator content: This is content made by a creator or influencer for a brand, usually as part of a paid collaboration.

UGC style creative: This is brand or agency produced content that is designed to feel organic, personal, and native to the platform.

Why this content still works
UGC style ads continue to perform well because they reflect how people consume content online. Most users are more likely to engage with content that feels direct, human, and easy to understand than with polished ad creative that feels overly scripted.
This type of content can be effective because it helps businesses:

Build trust faster: People often respond better to someone showing a real experience than to a highly polished brand message.
Fit naturally into social platforms: Short form, conversational content often feels more at home in Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube feeds.
Explain products and services more clearly: A person demonstrating a product or explaining a service can communicate value quickly and simply.
Strengthen social proof: Real experiences and real voices can make a brand feel more credible and more approachable.

What has changed in 2026
In 2026 UGC is still relevant, but it is no longer enough to talk about it as one simple category. Businesses now need to be more precise about what type of content they are using and how it is being delivered through ad platforms.
Today, many brands are not running pure customer generated UGC. They are running:

creator made ads
UGC style videos
partnership ads
paid amplification of approved creator posts

That does not make the content less valuable. It simply means the strategy is more mature. The strongest campaigns are now built around the right mix of creative format, creator fit, platform placement, permissions, and messaging.
What businesses often get wrong
UGC does not automatically outperform traditional ads. Some businesses assume that if content looks casual, it will perform well. That is not always true. Weak hooks, unclear messaging, poor creator fit, or a bad landing page can still lead to poor results.
Businesses also run into problems when they:

treat all creator content as UGC
rely on authenticity without a clear strategy
use vague testimonials with no real message
ignore permissions or usage rights
focus on style instead of substance

A good UGC style ad may look simple, but it still needs a clear purpose.
How businesses should use UGC more effectively
A better approach is to stop asking, “Do we need UGC?” and start asking, “What kind of content would make our offer easier to understand and easier to trust?”
That could include:

client testimonials
creator demonstrations
founder videos
FAQ style clips
simple before and after explanations

Ready to Try UGC in Your Next Campaign?
Ready to explore the right approach for your business? Book a consultation today and let’s talk through your goals, your audience, and the type of content that can support stronger ad performance.
FAQs

 Are UGC ads still relevant in 2026?
Yes. UGC style ads and creator led content are still highly relevant, especially in paid social and short form video campaigns.
 What is the difference between UGC ads and creator ads?
UGC ads usually refer to content that feels like it came from a real user. Creator ads are made by creators or influencers for a brand. Many businesses are now using creator content or UGC style creative rather than pure customer generated content.
 What are partnership ads?
Partnership ads are ad formats that allow brands to promote approved creator content through formal permissions and platform tools.
 Do UGC ads work for service businesses?
Yes. Service businesses can use testimonial videos, founder videos, client stories, and FAQ style content to make their offer feel more trustworthy and easier to understand.
 Do I need permission to use customer content in ads?
Yes. Businesses should always get clear permission before using customer or creator content in paid advertising.
 Which platforms are best for UGC style ads?
Meta, TikTok, and YouTube are some of the most common platforms, but the best fit depends on your audience, your offer, and the type of content you can produce.
 Do UGC ads always outperform traditional ads?
No. They can perform well, but results still depend on the offer, message, targeting, creative quality, and landing page experience.
 What makes a strong UGC style ad?
A strong UGC style ad usually has a clear opening, a relatable message, natural delivery, and a specific goal.
 Can UGC style content support AI search visibility?
Yes, especially when the content is well structured, clearly written, and answers common questions directly.
 What should a business do before launching UGC ads?
Start by clarifying your audience, your offer, and your message. Then decide whether customer content, creator content, or UGC style creative is the best fit.

#### Understanding Google&#8217;s October 2023 Algorithm Updates
October 2023 has been a whirlwind month for digital marketers and website owners alike, with Google rolling out two significant updates back-to-back: the spam update and the core update. These changes have sent waves through the SEO community, causing notable fluctuations in search rankings and website visibility. Let&#8217;s dive into what&#8217;s been happening and how it might affect your online presence.

The October 2023 Spam Update: A Cleanup Operation
The spam update, which began on October 4th, targeted cloaking, hacked content, auto-generated content, and scraped spam. Google&#8217;s crackdown on spam is a move to improve the quality of search results and penalise those who violate their policies. If your website employs none of these spam techniques, you&#8217;re in the clear, but if it does, it&#8217;s time for a clean-up to align with Google&#8217;s spam policies.
The October 2023 Core Update: A Quest for Relevance
Following closely on the heels of the spam update, the core update started rolling out on October 5th. Unlike the spam update, the core update is not a disciplinary measure but a refinement of Google&#8217;s ranking processes. It aims to enhance the relevance and quality of search results by rewarding sites that offer genuine value to users. This update caused significant ranking volatility, which has kept the SEO community on its toes.
Impact and Insights: What Webmasters Are Saying
The SEO landscape is abuzz with reports of ranking upheavals. Many webmasters have observed their pages disappearing from Google&#8217;s index, significant traffic drops, and a frustrating game of hide and seek with their content&#8217;s visibility. Despite the turmoil, some have seen silver linings, with recoveries from previous penalties and unexpected traffic boosts.
The Overlap Confusion: Core vs. Spam
Google&#8217;s recent release of two updates at the same time has caused some confusion. It can be tricky to figure out how these updates affect your website, but Google&#8217;s guidance is straightforward: If you&#8217;ve made changes that have nothing to do with spammy tactics, it&#8217;s probably because of the core update. On the other hand, if your website engages in spammy practices, you should pay close attention to how the spam update might be impacting your search visibility.
Best Practices Moving Forward
In the wake of these updates, it&#8217;s more crucial than ever to focus on creating high-quality, user-centric content. Steer clear of spam tactics and invest in the kind of helpful, informative content that Google&#8217;s algorithms are designed to reward. Remember, SEO is a long-term game, and adherence to best practices will help weather the storms of future updates. Google&#8217;s algorithms will continue to evolve, and so should our strategies for staying visible and relevant in an ever-changing digital landscape.

#### Understanding the Impact: Website Security Breaches and Their Consequences
With the growing sophistication of cyber threats, website security has never been more paramount. From brand reputation to financial loss, a compromised website can bring a host of detrimental consequences. Let’s dive deeper into the implications of website security breaches.

1. Brand Reputation
Trust is Fragile. Whether you&#8217;re a sole trader or a large company, your brand&#8217;s reputation is invaluable. It takes years to build trust, but only a momentary lapse in website security to shatter it. Once customers feel their data is vulnerable or compromised due to a hack, regaining that trust becomes an uphill battle.
2. Financial Loss
For businesses, a hacked website often translates to financial losses. This could result from downtime, lost sales, or even hefty fines from regulatory bodies for data breaches. Even if you&#8217;re a non-commercial site, a breach can lead to unforeseen costs related to website repair, data recovery, and other remediation processes.
3. Emotional Distress
Beyond the tangible losses, a website breach can lead to immense emotional distress. Owners and stakeholders grapple with questions like: &#8220;Why didn&#8217;t I prioritise security?&#8221;, &#8220;How do I restore customer trust?&#8221;, or &#8220;What have I lost permanently?&#8221;. The emotional strain can be overwhelming, especially for businesses that heavily rely on their digital presence.
4. Blocklisting &amp; Loss of Traffic
If search engines detect malware or phishing scams on your site, they&#8217;re likely to blocklist it to protect users. A blocklisted site can lose up to 95% of its organic traffic. For many, this is a critical blow, especially if search engine rankings have taken years of effort to achieve.
5. Legal Consequences
Data breaches, especially those compromising personal user data, can lead to legal consequences. Depending on the jurisdiction, organisations can face lawsuits, fines, and other penalties for failing to secure customer data.
So, What&#8217;s Next?
The digital realm is evolving, and so are the threats. Passive measures are no longer sufficient. Today&#8217;s websites need proactive, monitored security solutions.
Don&#8217;t Leave Things to Chance. With the stakes this high, entrusting your website&#8217;s security to professionals isn&#8217;t just an option; it&#8217;s a necessity.

#### Unlocking Leads: Mistakes to Avoid and Strategies to Succeed
Generating leads isn’t just about numbers &#8211; it’s about attracting the right audience and converting them into loyal customers. However, many businesses unknowingly sabotage their lead generation efforts. At Concept Designs &amp; Marketing, we specialise in helping businesses navigate the digital landscape, ensuring they reach the right customers at the right time. Whether you&#8217;re refining your marketing strategy or looking for ways to improve your lead generation efforts, avoiding these common mistakes can make all the difference.

1. Weak or Generic Call-to-Actions (CTAs)
A vague “Contact Us” button isn’t enough to drive action. Instead, use clear and compelling CTAs that create urgency and value, such as “Book Your Free Strategy Session” or “Get Your Custom Marketing Plan Today.” Strong CTAs encourage immediate engagement and set expectations.
2. Complicated Lead Capture Forms
Long or complex forms can discourage potential leads from completing an enquiry. Simplify your forms by requesting only essential details. The easier it is to sign up, the higher the conversion rate.
3. Ignoring the Power of Email Marketing
Many businesses underestimate the effectiveness of email marketing. Consistent, personalised email campaigns help nurture leads, build trust, and guide potential customers through the decision-making process. From welcome sequences to targeted promotions, emails keep your brand top of mind.
4. Overlooking Social Proof
Trust is a major factor in lead conversion. Showcasing client testimonials, case studies, and real customer success stories builds credibility and reassures potential leads. Don’t be afraid to highlight your wins &#8211; social proof can be a game-changer.
5. Forgetting About Retargeting Ads
Most website visitors won’t convert on their first visit. Retargeting ads help re-engage these warm leads by reminding them of your services and encouraging them to take the next step. A well-placed ad can turn hesitation into action.
6. Prioritising Quantity Over Quality
A high volume of leads means little if they aren’t the right fit for your business. Instead of chasing numbers, focus on attracting qualified leads who are more likely to convert into paying customers. Quality over quantity leads to better long-term growth.
The Concept Designs &amp; Marketing Approach
Effective lead generation requires a strategic approach. Avoiding these common mistakes can significantly improve your ability to attract, nurture, and convert leads. By focusing on strong CTAs, simplified forms, retargeting strategies, and leveraging email marketing, your business can create a lead generation system that works.

#### Using Social Media Buttons To Boost Your Seo
How is your website performing? Do you know if you are ranking on Page 1 when people search for keywords related to your business and website?
If you’ve been doing SEO for your website, then you’re on track to moving up the ladder and be seen. However, even organic SEO can take some time to build. Help your SEO with the power of social media!
You might have noticed that many websites nowadays have a range of social media share buttons displayed on their pages and blog articles. These encourage readers to take action and make it easy for them to share. So, you should just go ahead and plaster buttons everywhere on your website pages, right?

While share buttons drives traffic to your website and create a cycle of re-sharing – hence driving even more traffic and increase opportunities for natural links to your pages thereby boosting your SEO, there is a danger of overdoing share buttons and potentially limiting their impact. Here are some tips to help you strategically place your social media share buttons.
Catch the discerning reader:
Place social share buttons at the end of your blog or article, usually these careful readers will share if they believe the content is useful and beneficial to others after reading all the way through to the end.
Grab the lazy reader:
With today’s information overload, many people have become ‘skimmers’ and don’t have the patience to completely read though an entire page. However, you can still grab their attention if the page contains a catchy title or topic. Place buttons near the title as skimmers tend to be more impulsive and can quickly share if they think the information is relevant.
Choose your pages:
Do you think you will be sharing a ‘contact page’ of a business? If you’re not going to share it, then don’t add share buttons. Placing excessive share buttons everywhere can be outright annoying and discourage shares. Think of the pages that are shareable on your website. For example, people generally like to share real life stories such as case studies or testimonials. Or perhaps you have some research findings that will benefit the community, or have written an article that contains interesting and relevant information.
Depending on the content, you might also need to adjust which social media buttons should be displayed more prominently. For example, if you have artwork or imagery, then Pinterest and Instagram buttons should be placed near the images. An article or blog would be more suited to have LinkedIn, Facebook and Twitter buttons, in addition to Google+ (if you have one) which can also help with Google SEO.

#### Valuable Content &#8211; The Difference It Can Make
There’s been a lot of talk around ‘Content’ and that ‘Content is King’. Look at your marketing plan and strategy, and you should see that Content is the foundation of many marketing activities. When you publish a Blog, that’s content marketing; how about a podcast, video, newsletter, emails, landing pages, or even your social media posts? They are all content marketing!
However, not all Content is created equal. You might see businesses that have great success in content marketing, whereas not quite so much for another. Perhaps you’ve been doing content marketing but not seeing great results. At the end of the day, even a great piece of Content won’t help you unless it’s valuable, fits in with your business goals and marketing strategy.
So what is Valuable Content and why does Valuable Content work?
1. Relevance &amp; Leadership
Is the Content relevant to your business and industry? Generally speaking, your content should align with your business image, and be useful, interesting, and relevant. By regularly providing your audience with valuable content, it builds their trust and relationship with you. It shows that you care about engaging them. You also show that you are a thought leader – or a known expert in your industry.
Make your content the ‘go-to’ in your market, and compel users to share, engage, and interact. This is also a great way to bring in new leads through social media sharing – let your content be found by new people and see your customer base grow!
2. Problems &amp; Solutions 
One step above from being useful and interesting, is that you actively address issues and problems while providing the solutions with your business. What concerns and issues do your audience face? If you’re a fresh grocer delivery service, perhaps your customers are busy mums who have no time to shop, or even simply not knowing what to make for dinner. In this case, your business can show your customers how you can ‘solve’ their problem – provide fresh vegetables delivered to your door, recipe cards and ideas, flexible delivery times etc.
You may even ask your customers what they’d like to know more, through comment sections in social media, opinion polls, or email feedback. Find out what your customer wants and tailor your content to make their voices heard.
3. Relatable User Experience
While it’s great to demonstrate in your content that your business is helpful and relevant, make sure your Content is relatable as well. Stories and case studies are a great way to illustrate real life experiences with using your product or service. It also creates the desire for people to want to use your business. Using descriptive wording and imagery can greatly enhance the experience. For the above example of the fresh grocer, you can illustrate the experience by saying “Imagine the freshest, organic local produce handpicked and delivered to your door, a wholesome and healthy meal the family can enjoy…”
Make content relatable and be as descriptive as possible, the idea is to have people ‘feel’ the use of your products or services.

Now that you’re on board with creating Valuable Content, go have some fun and come up with new ideas to freshen up your content marketing campaign!
Having Valuable Content can also benefit your SEO, if your readers find your content useful. Distribution is also key so your Content can be seen. It is worthwhile to examine your marketing plan and channel at the same time.

#### Website Security Part II
Previously, we talked about the dangers and potential financial losses from a malware attack, which included being blacklisted by search engines. Apart from harming your business, malware can also harm your customers, lower your SEO rankings and damage your reputation:
Loss of SEO Ranking and Reputation:
Search engines keep information on websites that are infected with malware, and Google will drop your site from the index. A “warning’ also appears on search results alerting users that your site may be hacked. Your customers will steer clear of you, especially if their computers are infected by your website, and as a result your reputation can be severely damaged. Your hard-earned SEO rankings will drop and it may take weeks, or even months, to climb back up the SEO ladder.
Illegitimate Links and Information Theft:
Another issue with malware is that it can install illegitimate links on your website and direct the traffic from your site to theirs. Customers will end up on a totally different site, which is usually rather ‘distasteful’. Some malware will also infect your visitors’ computers, stealing confidential and sensitive information, such as passwords and credit card data. This can also lead to more headaches, such as identity theft, or worse yet, long term legal issues that will cost you a fortune.
Close to 10,000 websites get blacklisted from malware infection daily, so it’s not a matter of whether your site gets hacked nowadays, it’s a matter of when your site will be hacked! You may think it won’t happen to you, but malware is often circulated by legitimate websites – some 90% of the time!
You might think, I have a small business, hackers won’t bother with me! Well, hackers actually like to target small to medium size businesses, because they usually don’t have security measures in place. Criminals are very capable of finding weaknesses in your website to place the malware. So, how do you know if your website is compromised what can you do to protect yourself and your clients?

Use Google Chrome to search and visit your website, and check if there’s a warning of malware. You can also check by using this link- http://www.google.com/safebrowsing/diagnostic?site=(insert your website here)
Your website designer or developer can also help you check for malware, and update the platform that you are using to strengthen your website’s security. It is a misconception that you will be protected through just hosting or firewalls.

Still unsure if your website is safe and secure? Don’t take chances! Concept Designs and Marketing can help. #### What Are The Key Differences Between Facebook Ads &#038; Boosted Posts?
Have you or someone in your business considered doing your social media marketing yourself and wondered what the difference is between boosting a post and doing Facebook ads? I was asked this question by a business owner who is very active on social media and has been spending significant money on Facebook. They are now looking for a digital marketing agency to help them gain more visibility with Facebook ads, but they wondered about the difference.
If you’re in the same boat and have tried to do this yourself, you may have noticed that there are two options: Create a Facebook ad or boost a post. Thanks to the question from this business owner, this blog aims to explain the difference between the two so you know exactly how and when to apply each strategy for the best results

Facebook Ads Vs Boosted Posts 
When you create a Facebook post, you can boost that post to a targeted audience at a set rate. Boosted posts are still ads since they are paid for and they will show up as ads on your followers’ Facebook feeds.
A Facebook ad is also paid for and will reach a targeted audience. The difference is that it’s created in Meta Ads Manager, which you will find in your Facebook management toolbar. It offers many more customisations, filters and opportunities to reach a broader yet targeted audience.
Benefits For Your Business 
The most significant benefit of Facebook ads is that they are fully customisable. The ads manager allows you to tick or untick several boxes to customise your advert according to the audience you want to reach, the geographic location, age group, gender and much more.
However, a boosted post also brings its own benefits, like saving time on creating a new ad from scratch and simply boosting an existing post in just a few clicks. Both methods benefit from cost savings and flexibility as you can set your desired budget based on what works for you as a business.
Consider These Pros And Cons
Facebook Ads
Pros:
Customised ads
Determine your own budget
Creative control
Placement on Instagram or Messenger
Cons:
Takes a bit of time and technical know-how to create an ad using Meta Ads Manager, but a social media agency in Sydney like ours can help with this.
Boosted Posts
Pros:
Creates awareness, encourages audience engagement
Flexible ad spend
Professional-looking ads
Reach a specific audience
Cons:
Not as customisable as Facebook ads
Not suitable for long-term campaigns
Still not sure which way to go? Below are a couple of comparisons that may help bring clarity:

Boosting is like using Wix for your website and Ad Manager is more like WordPress
Or like Microsoft Publisher for boosting vs InDesign for Ads
Or perhaps even Canva (boosting option) vs Photoshop (Meta Ads Manager)

Both can get the job done&#8230; but one has a lot more bells, whistles, and ultimately control which is great for those who want to maximise the potential, and ultimately understand how to use it but it may be too much for those who just want to put a little effort in and see what happens.

#### What is AI Search and How is it Different from Google Search?
In a world where information is at our fingertips, the way we search online is shifting. For years, traditional search engines like Google have dominated the online landscape, indexing billions of web pages and ranking them based on keywords, authority, and user behaviour. But now, a new player is gaining momentum: AI search.

What is AI Search?
AI search refers to the use of artificial intelligence, particularly generative models like ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity AI, to understand user questions and respond with direct, conversational answers. Instead of returning a list of links, AI search tools generate summarised responses that are contextual and often draw from multiple sources across the internet.
Key Differences Between AI Search and Google Search
1. Results Format

Google Search: Returns a ranked list of web pages for you to explore.
AI Search: Provides a direct response or summary, often without showing where the information came from.

2. Source Transparency

Google: Highlights credible sources, showing URLs and metadata.
AI: May not always cite sources, which can raise trust and accuracy questions.

3. User Experience

Google: Searchers scan, click, compare, and read.
AI: Offers conversational interaction, often answering follow-up questions seamlessly.

4. Content Optimisation

Google SEO: Focuses on keywords, backlinks, and site structure.
AI GEO (Generative Engine Optimisation): Focuses on structured data, expert content, and being cited in authoritative sources.

Why It Matters to Businesses
AI search tools are already changing how people find products, services and information. They’re especially popular among younger audiences, tech-savvy consumers, and those using tools like voice assistants or AI apps.
If your content isn’t optimised for AI-driven discovery, you risk being invisible where future customers are searching. That’s where GEO (Generative Engine Optimisation) comes in. While SEO helps your content rank in Google, GEO ensures it’s findable by AI tools.
Takeaway
Google isn’t going anywhere—but it’s no longer the only search game in town. Businesses must now optimise for both SEO and GEO to stay relevant.
Want help making your content AI-friendly? Learn more about GEO or book a free consultation to get started.

#### What is Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO)?
As AI search tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google’s Search Generative Experience/Google Overviews become more widely used, a new branch of digital strategy has emerged: Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO).

So, What is GEO?
Generative Engine Optimisation is the process of tailoring your content and online presence so that it can be discovered, understood, and summarised accurately by AI tools. Unlike traditional SEO, which focuses on ranking in Google search results, GEO focuses on being cited and referenced by AI platforms that deliver answers directly to users, often without linking back to your website.
Why GEO Matters
AI tools don’t “rank” websites the same way Google does. Instead, they scan the web for information from trusted sources, then generate responses using that information. This means if your content isn’t appearing in those trusted sources, or isn’t structured in a way AI can easily interpret, you may be missing out on visibility.
Including GEO in your marketing strategy helps your business get picked up in AI-generated summaries, which is where more people are turning for quick answers. In fact, Australians conducted over 38 million AI-powered searches in recent months, and that number continues to grow. 
How GEO Works
A GEO strategy typically includes:

Long-tail and question-based keywords: These match how people phrase their queries in AI search tools.
Clear, structured content: AI platforms prioritise content that is easy to summarise, such as FAQs, how-to guides, and clearly labelled sections.
Schema markup: Structured data (e.g. FAQ or How-To schema) helps AI correctly interpret your content’s context.
Citations from credible sites: AI tools favour sources that are mentioned or linked by other reputable platforms.

GEO vs. SEO
While GEO and SEO share some similarities, they serve different roles. SEO remains essential, especially since Google’s AI systems often reference top-ranking websites. However, GEO is about being found by a variety of AI tools that don&#8217;t rely on traditional rankings. Your content must be structured for clarity, credibility, and summarisation. 
Key Takeaway
If your digital strategy focuses only on Google rankings, you risk falling behind. GEO ensures your business stays visible across emerging AI platforms. It’s not a replacement for SEO: it’s the next layer of your strategy.

FAQs About GEO
1. What is Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO)?
GEO is the process of making your online content easy for AI tools to find, understand and summarise in search results.
2. How is GEO different from traditional SEO?
SEO focuses on ranking in Google, while GEO focuses on being cited by AI tools like ChatGPT and Perplexity.
3. Why is GEO important for my business?
More people are using AI search tools. GEO helps your business stay visible in this fast-growing search environment.
4. Do I still need SEO if I’m doing GEO?
Yes. SEO builds trust and authority, which GEO relies on. The two work best together.
5. What kind of content works best for GEO?
FAQ sections, how-to articles and clearly structured, expert-driven content are ideal.

Yes. GEO increases the chance that AI tools will pull accurate content from your site when generating summaries.

#### What You Should Look Out for When Choosing a Hosting Provider
Do you have a website and looking at your options for a hosting space? How do you know if you are comparing apples with apples? Finding the right hosting provider can feel overwhelming with such a large number of hosting services to choose from.

Amongst the features and price, there are also considerations to look out for, and most importantly, security. If you are not sure where to start, here are some of the Key Security issues to consider:
1, SSL Certificate
You might have seen the little ‘padlock’ icon in front of a URL in the address bar, this indicates a security protocol SSL (Secure Sockets Layer) in place that governs the encrypted connection between your website to the visitor. Having an SSL is essential, as it demonstrates that your website is safe for customers to visit, it gives them peace of mind that any content passed across your website will be encrypted. Some browsers will give a warning or block websites that do not have an current SSL Certificate.
2, Malware Protection
Another area to look out for, is whether the hosting provider and server is in the best position to be protected from malware. You might have heard about malicious malware attacks on large corporations, and even demanding ransoms. If you think that your small business is not going to be a prime target, think again. The truth is, everything online can be attacked. Malware is malicious software that can be disastrous to your business, and you don’t want your website to suddenly crash for no apparent reason. When choosing your provider, make sure they have an option for malware defence and can run daily scans on their servers.
3, Firewall Settings
Hosting providers can also provide additional security protection with Firewalls. These can protect networks from harmful and hostile attacks. A dedicated firewall is especially helpful if your business deals with sensitive customer information and data. When considering a hosting provider, check to see if their Firewall is shared or dedicated.
4, Backups and Restore
Backing up your website and data is a smart idea. However, you also need to ensure that you have a reliable backup and restore system in place. Your web hosting provider should also have a comprehensive backup and restore system that is at the server level. You never know when accidents might happen, or when files get corrupted and you need to restore from backup. Being able to quickly restore a website can make a night and day difference to your business, especially if your business is mostly conducted online.
5, Website Plugin Updates
In order to truly compare apples with apples, do you know what your hosting provide offers you in terms of keeping your website up-to-date? Just like our phones have regular app and software updates to ensure they are best protected from a vulnerability, websites also have plugins that need to be updated regularly. If your website is built on a platform such as WordPress, the developers of the plugins are regularly keeping them up-to-date to ensure the best protection from any vulnerability. Ask your hosting provider if they offer this service as part of your website hosting.
Keeping your website up-to-date is one of the first steps in protecting your website from a malicious attack.
As you can see, finding the right hosting provider will ensure your website is looked after and runs smoothly. Sometimes the cheapest option may not be best as you may be sharing hosting with other users, or the server may be unreliable causing crashes. Worse of all, it can leave your website exposed and vulnerable to attacks, leaving a disastrous and costly impact on your business.

#### What’s the Difference Between Running YouTube Ads on YouTube vs Google Ads?
When it comes to digital marketing, YouTube is one of the most powerful platforms for reaching potential customers. But many businesses are unsure whether they should run ads directly through YouTube or manage them via Google Ads. The truth is, while both options can help promote your business, they offer very different levels of control, targeting, and outcomes.

Running Ads Directly on YouTube
When you upload a video to YouTube, you’ll see an option to “Promote” it. This is YouTube’s built-in way to boost your video views. It’s designed to be simple and beginner-friendly. You set a budget, choose a basic audience, and let YouTube handle the rest.
This method works well if your main goal is to increase views or subscribers. However, the downside is limited control. Targeting is basic (age, gender, location), and you can’t track conversions like website leads or sales. Think of it as a quick visibility boost, not a long-term advertising strategy.
Running YouTube Ads Through Google Ads
For businesses that want more than just views, Google Ads is the smarter choice. By creating a “Video Campaign” in Google Ads, you unlock advanced tools:
&#8211; Precise targeting: In-market audiences, remarketing, keyword targeting, placements, and more.
&#8211; Multiple ad formats: Skippable in-stream, bumper, discovery ads, and more.
&#8211; Conversion tracking: Measure how many viewers turned into leads, customers, or website visitors.
&#8211; Flexible bidding strategies: Choose to pay per view, per click, or optimise for conversions.
This makes Google Ads the better option for serious business growth. It gives you the ability to track ROI, refine campaigns, and integrate YouTube ads with your other Google campaigns (like Search or Display).
Which Should You Choose?
If you’re just starting out and want to test the waters, YouTube’s “Promote” option can be a quick win. But if your goal is to generate leads, sales, or measurable growth, running YouTube ads through Google Ads will give you far more control and better results.
FAQs
1. Can I run YouTube ads without Google Ads?
Yes, but only in a limited way using YouTube’s “Promote” button.
2. Is Google Ads free to use?
Yes, creating an account is free, but you pay for the ads you run.
3. Do YouTube Studio ads track conversions?
No, they only focus on views and engagement.
4. Which option is better for small businesses?
Google Ads is better if you want measurable results.
5. Can I target specific keywords with YouTube Studio ads?
No, keyword targeting is only available through Google Ads.
6. Are YouTube ads expensive?
They can be cost-effective, starting from a few cents per view.
7. Can I retarget website visitors with YouTube ads?
Yes, but only through Google Ads.
8. Do both options allow skippable ads?
Yes, but Google Ads offers more ad format choices.
9. Can I set daily budgets?
Yes, both platforms let you set daily or campaign budgets.
10. Which platform offers better analytics?
A: Google Ads provides far more detailed analytics and reporting.

#### Where Do AI Search Tools Get Their Information From?
AI search tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini don’t crawl the web in real time the way Google does. Instead, they are trained on large volumes of data sourced from publicly available websites, licensed publications and trusted repositories. These tools then generate responses based on patterns found in their training data.

Why Your Website Might Not Be Cited
What many business owners may not realise is that AI platforms usually won’t reference small business websites unless they have domain authority and are widely mentioned, cited or viewed as credible by other well-known sources. This makes third-party citations more important than ever. Being mentioned in news sites, government pages, industry publications or even Wikipedia can help build the authority AI tools rely on.
Some platforms also reference live sources such as Google Search, LinkedIn, Reddit, Quora and YouTube. If your business is mentioned in a Reddit thread, for example, appears in a video or is quoted in an article, it’s possible that AI tools may use that content when generating responses.
Unlike Google, which ranks individual web pages based on SEO signals, AI tools work by generating answers to queries, based on relevance, credibility and recency. They are less about links and rankings, and more about perceived authority.
How to Help AI Find and Use Your Content

Get featured in interviews, articles or guest blogs
Encourage customers and collaborators to mention your brand online
Share and repurpose content across high-visibility channels
Keep your website up to date with credible, fact-based content

What You Need to Know
AI tools don’t rely on your website alone. They use multiple sources to generate content, and your visibility depends on your overall digital footprint. Building a broader presence across trusted platforms is now essential.
There is no better time than the present to see where you stand. Take our free AI Visibility Score at https://www.concept-designs.com.au/ai_visibility_score to check how your business appears in AI search.
Frequently Asked Questions
1. Where do AI search tools get their information from?
AI tools use a mix of training data, live web sources and trusted platforms like Wikipedia, Reddit and major industry websites.
2. Do AI search tools browse the internet like Google?
No. Most do not actively crawl live sites. They generate answers from existing data sets and curated sources.
3. What types of websites do AI platforms trust?
Sources like news outlets, university sites, government pages and heavily cited blogs are typically considered credible.
4. Can AI tools access my website directly?
Not unless your website has high domain authority or is well-cited. Otherwise, it is unlikely to be directly referenced.
5. How do AI tools summarise information?
They identify patterns in large data sets and generate the most relevant or likely response to the user’s query.
6. What does “trusted source” mean in AI search?
It refers to content that is fact-checked, well-maintained and widely cited across other online sources.
7. Are social media platforms used as sources for AI tools?
Yes. Some tools include real-time platforms like Reddit, Quora, YouTube and LinkedIn when generating answers.
8. Does being on Google help me appear in AI search too?
Yes. Google rankings contribute to your authority, which AI tools may use when selecting trusted sources.
9. Should I focus on getting featured in publications?
Definitely. Being mentioned in high-traffic publications or articles increases your AI search visibility.
10. Can I control what AI tools say about my brand?
Not directly. But you can influence it by publishing trustworthy content, being active on credible platforms and earning citations.

#### Why Is My Website Getting Fewer Clicks from Google Lately?
Have you noticed a drop in your website traffic, especially from Google or Bing, even though you’re keeping up with SEO best practices? You’re not alone: many business owners are seeing fewer clicks. So, what’s changed?

The Rise of Zero-Click Searches 
One major reason is the increase in zero-click searches. These are search results where Google provides the answer right on the search page, such as featured snippets, quick answers, or AI-generated overviews from Search Generative Experience (SGE) known as AI Overviews. Users get what they need without ever visiting a website. 
AI Overviews Are Changing User Behaviour 
Google’s Overviews is designed to give users AI-generated summaries at the top of search results. These summaries pull information from various sources to answer queries on the search page, reducing the need for users to click through to individual websites. While this may improve the user experience, it often means your site may be referenced but not clicked. The end result? Reduced website traffic.
Increased Competition in AI and Traditional Search
As more businesses optimise their content, ranking well is no longer enough. AI search tools are pulling information from trusted, cited sources. If your site isn’t being quoted or mentioned in reputable places or earning strong backlinks, you’re less likely to be included in these AI-generated overviews, even if you’ve got good content. 
Changing Search Habits
People aren’t only searching on Google anymore. Many are using ChatGPT, Perplexity, YouTube, and even TikTok to find information. This shift in search behaviour means that relying solely on Google search for visibility is no longer a sustainable strategy.
What You Can Do About It

Check Your Content Format: Is it structured for AI to easily extract? Use clear headings, concise answers, and question-based formatting. 
Focus on Being Cited: Increase your domain authority through backlinks, PR, and mentions in credible blogs or industry sites.
Diversify Your Traffic Sources: Build presence on other platforms like LinkedIn, YouTube, and industry forums.
Start Thinking GEO: Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) can help ensure your content is discoverable by AI tools as well as traditional search. It’s all about being findable by AI.

Take Action Now
Declining clicks doesn&#8217;t mean your content has lost its value. Search is changing, and so should your approach. By understanding AI search and adapting your strategy, you can stay visible where your audience is looking.
Want to see how ready your website is for AI-driven search? Try our AI Visibility Calculator to get started.
Frequently Asked Questions About Declining Google Clicks and AI Search

Why is my website getting fewer clicks from Google?
Because of zero-click searches and AI summaries reducing the need for users to visit websites.
What is a zero-click search?
It’s when Google answers a query directly in the search result, so users don’t need to click on any links.
What is Google SGE?
Google’s Search Generative Experience provides AI-generated overviews that summarise content, often replacing traditional blue links.
Is SEO still effective in 2025?
Yes, but it must be adapted to also support visibility in AI-driven search platforms.
Why am I being mentioned but not getting clicks?
AI tools may reference your site in summaries without sending traffic directly to it.
What is Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO)?
GEO is the process of making your content accessible and quotable for AI search tools.
How can I reverse the drop in website traffic?
Optimise for AI search, build backlinks, and diversify your content strategy across multiple platforms.
Does AI search use Google’s rankings?
Partially, but it also pulls from other trusted sources like Wikipedia, news articles, and industry blogs.
Should I change my SEO strategy?
Yes. Traditional SEO must now work alongside GEO to maintain visibility in both human and AI searches.
Is this drop permanent?
It depends on how quickly you adapt. Businesses that embrace GEO early will have a competitive edge.

#### Why it is essential to have a Strategic Plan for Your Business
What is the goal of your business? Do you have a direction and vision? In other words, do you have a Strategic Plan for your business?
When you started, perhaps you had a business plan in place. However, to be successful in the long term, you will also need to plan strategically. Planning helps you achieve what you set out to do. Whether in business or in life, without a strategy is like navigating an unknown territory with no guidance or a map to follow.
So what does a Strategic Plan look like, is it essential for your business and if so, what should you include in it?

We’ve indicated that a strategic plan is essential for navigating your way around your business, but more than that, your Strategic Plan should examine what your business is doing, and determine what you’re good at (or not!). From there, you can work out where you want to be in the long-term, and allocate your resources accordingly so that you achieve those goals. Here are 5 essential elements to include in your plan:
1. Mission &amp; Vision
So, why do you have a business? What is your vision for your business? You should have a clear idea of what you aspire to be in the future, and an overall direction you want to follow. Examine your Mission – it is what you are doing now – determine your marketplace, customers, and competitors. Describe how you have been doing business, be specific and objective. Are you doing well? What can you improve on?
2. Strengths and Weaknesses
Which leads us to identifying what your business is good at, and what issues you may be facing. Consider a SWOT analysis, this is a strategic analysis that helps you find your Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities and Threats. Once you have a clear picture of where you’re at, then you’re ready to set some goals.
3. Goals &amp; Objectives
This is where you will come up with realistic goals and objectives to accomplish. They should focus on both short-term and long-term time frames, based on the analysis of what issues you need to resolve, while playing out your strengths. These goals will also take advantage of the opportunities identified above.
4. Action Plan
Now that you have your goals listed, you can then prepare a step-by-step plan of how you are going to accomplish those goals. Who, what, when, where and how? What is your budget and what resources do you have to allocate? This will help you remain focused and on track with your operations.
5. Monitor &amp; Review
Once you launch your strategic plan, don’t forget to monitor its progress, observe changes in the marketplace, and review regularly to see if anything needs to be adjusted. It is a good idea to go back and review once every quarter to make sure you are staying on course.
With a strategic plan in place, it provides the springboard to delve into your overall marketing strategy. If you are unsure how to go about setting up your marketing plan, bouncing out of your broader business goals, we can walk through a ‘marketing health check’ of your business, and help you best reach your target market, where you will get the best return on investment for your marketing dollars.

#### Wix vs Squarespace vs WordPress: Limitations and Opportunities for Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO)
Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) is quickly becoming a core part of digital strategy. Traditional SEO focused on ranking in Google, but AI-powered search engines like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity are reshaping how people discover answers. Businesses now need to ensure their websites are not only indexable by Google, but also accessible and trusted by generative AI systems.
If your site is built on Wix, Squarespace, or WordPress, here’s how each platform stacks up when it comes to GEO.

Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) is quickly becoming a core part of digital strategy. Traditional SEO focused on ranking in Google, but AI-powered search engines like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity are reshaping how people discover answers. Businesses now need to ensure their websites are not only indexable by Google, but also accessible and trusted by generative AI systems.
If your site is built on Wix, Squarespace, or WordPress, here’s how each platform stacks up when it comes to GEO.
What Is GEO?
GEO, or Generative Engine Optimisation, is the process of tailoring your site so that AI-driven platforms can easily find, understand, and cite your content. It builds on SEO principles but focuses on visibility within large language models (LLMs) and AI-powered search engines.

For GEO, content quality, structured data, and crawler accessibility are crucial.
Wix and GEO
Wix has been one of the first site builders to embrace GEO directly. In 2024, it launched its AI Visibility Overview, giving businesses insight into how often their brand is cited in AI search and how AI sentiment trends look. It also introduced LLMs.txt, a new file type that provides instructions for AI crawlers.
Benefits of Wix for GEO:

Automatic generation of LocalBusiness schema when you set up your business details.
Ability to add custom JSON-LD structured data (up to 7,000 characters).
Built-in SEO and GEO monitoring tools.

Limitations of Wix:

Only one primary business location is supported in auto schema.
Custom schema has character limits.
Like all hosted platforms, back-end flexibility is restricted.

&nbsp;
Squarespace and GEO
Squarespace has also acknowledged the shift towards AI search. Its support guides encourage businesses to optimise their sites for AI-powered search engines by keeping content structured and crawlable.
Benefits of Squarespace for GEO:

Automatic schema markup for LocalBusiness, Organisation, Products, and more.
Ability to add custom schema via Code Injection or Code Blocks.
Simple design and content structure that search engines can easily interpret.

Limitations of Squarespace:

Auto-generated schema cannot be removed or fully customised.
Duplicate schema entries can arise if you add your own JSON-LD.
Less technical control than open platforms.

&nbsp;
WordPress and GEO
WordPress, the world’s most popular CMS, offers far more flexibility than Wix or Squarespace. Because it is open-source, you can control nearly every element of your site, making it highly adaptable for GEO.
Benefits of WordPress for GEO:

Full control over schema markup through plugins like Rank Math, Yoast SEO, or custom code.
Ability to implement advanced strategies such as FAQs, HowTo schema, multiple business locations, and new features like LLMs.txt.
Vast library of plugins to test and monitor SEO and GEO performance.
Open hosting options let you optimise server performance for speed and crawler access.

Limitations of WordPress:

Requires more technical skill or developer support.
Too many plugins can cause conflicts, security issues, or slow site speed (which affects AI and search crawling).
Quality of GEO optimisation depends heavily on the site builder’s implementation.

&nbsp;
Overall Comparison
Wix: Strong GEO adoption, beginner-friendly, but limited schema flexibility and back-end control.
Squarespace: Easy to use, clean structure, but schema duplication and lack of customisation can hold you back.
WordPress: Most powerful and flexible option, capable of advanced GEO optimisation, but requires more technical know-how and maintenance.
How to Optimise Across All Three Platforms
Regardless of which platform you choose, the fundamentals of GEO remain the same:

Publish clear, concise, high-quality content.
Structure your site with headings, summaries, and FAQs.
Ensure schema markup is accurate and complete.
Allow AI crawlers access to your site.
Monitor performance and adapt as AI search evolves.

Not sure which platform is best for you? Book a consultation today to discuss which website builder is most suited to your digital goals and GEO strategy. We’ll help you make the right choice, based on what actually works.
&nbsp;
FAQs About GEO for Wix, Squarespace, and WordPress

 What is Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO)?

GEO is the process of preparing your website so that AI-powered search engines and LLMs can easily understand and cite your content in generated answers.

 Do Wix websites support GEO?

Yes. Wix has built-in schema generation, custom JSON-LD options, and tools like AI Visibility Overview and LLMs.txt to support GEO.

 Do Squarespace websites support GEO?

Yes, but with limitations. Squarespace automatically generates schema and allows custom JSON-LD, though duplicates and incomplete schema are common.

 Do WordPress websites support GEO?

Absolutely. WordPress is highly customisable, with plugins and manual coding options that allow advanced GEO strategies.

 Which platform is best for beginners focused on GEO?

Wix is the most beginner-friendly option thanks to its automated GEO tools and monitoring features.

 Which platform is best for full GEO control?

WordPress is the strongest choice for advanced users who want full control over schema, crawling, and server performance.

 Can I add FAQ schema on Wix and Squarespace?

Yes. Both platforms support FAQ schema, but you may need to manually add JSON-LD or use code injection.

 Does site speed impact GEO?

Yes. AI crawlers, like traditional search engines, favour faster, well-optimised websites.

 Should I block AI crawlers from my site?

No. Blocking AI crawlers will prevent your content from being cited in AI-generated answers.

 Is GEO replacing SEO?

No. GEO builds on SEO. Both are essential &#8211; SEO gets you visibility on search engines, while GEO ensures visibility in AI search.

#### YouTube Ads – How Do You Analyse Performance?
With nearly 2 billion users logging in each month, YouTube has become an increasingly popular platform for helping businesses reach and attract new audiences through advertising.
YouTube offers four types of ads on videos that are matched to a relevant audience. But how do you go about analysing the performance to maximise your returns? Let’s take a look at the 4 ad types in more detail:
Skippable Ads
These Ads can appear before, during, or after a video. They are skippable because users are able to skip after 5 seconds of viewing time. The focus on analysing skippable ads is examining the data of how many people skipped after the 5-second mark, which you can find under video analytics in YouTube Studio. While the advantage of skippable ads is that you don’t need to pay unless someone watches at least 30 seconds, you should still aim to lengthen viewer retention.
Non-Skippable Ads
Similar to the above, the difference is that viewers are not able to skip and are required to view the full ad with a 15-second limit. Payment is based on impressions, and you can also find the data under YouTube Studio. For this type of ad, you need to look at the number of click-through rates (CTR) to views since the retention rate will naturally be higher as most people will watch the ad through, in order to view the video.
Bumper Ads
These are much shorter ads lasting 6 seconds or less, which are also non-skippable. You’re more likely to keep your audience’s attention given the shorter duration. Again, you will want to see the click-through rates based on the number of views, as well as the cost-effectiveness based on the charge of impressions.
Overlay Ads
These ads appear as an image or banner at the bottom of a YouTube video, allowing users an option to either close the ad (clicking on a cross), or clicking through to a website landing page. You will find data on the performance of these ads in Google Ads reporting since they are not videos. Look for the number of click-throughs vs. closing, compared to the number of people reached.
Maximising your Ads
When analysing the performance of your YouTube Ads, there are several key considerations. If you are reaching a large number of people, but with little or no click-throughs, perhaps you need to improve your video or image. For skippable ads, you should also consider the amount of revenue generated, or new followers gained depending on your goal. Bear in mind that the audience might also need to be tweaked if your ads are not getting as much reach as anticipated.
To maximise your advertising dollar, compare your ads to see which ones are costing you more in terms of results. For example, you might have a costlier Bumper Ad that is getting more click-throughs than a Non-Skippable Ad, in that case, it might be worthwhile combining the advertising budget on the more successful ad.

We can help you determine the most profitable ad type and interpret the performance data. If you need engaging content, our team can also provide professionally designed videos and images.
Get in touch to give your YouTube Ads a boost today.

The Concept Designs &amp; Marketing Team
Concept Designs &amp; Marketing is a team of passionate marketing consultants with a deep focus on results-driven digital marketing strategies. Led by Jenny Godfrey, a seasoned expert in Website Design &amp; Development, SEO, Online Ads and Social Media. Jenny and her team focus on crafting tailored digital marketing strategies that help businesses thrive in an ever-evolving online landscape.
By combining data-driven insights with creative solutions, Concept Designs &amp; Marketing enhances brand visibility, engagement, and lead generation. With a commitment to client success and continuous innovation, we empower businesses to stand out, attract more customers, and achieve long-term growth in the digital space.

Jenny Godfrey is a digital marketing strategist with over 23 years experience, and the Founder and CEO of Concept Designs &amp; Marketing. She’s passionate about helping businesses grow through an awesome online presence which includes a great website that drives leads, SEO, AI Search, social media marketing, content creation, and online advertising. With years of experience, Jenny knows how to craft marketing strategies that cut through the noise and deliver real results. Her approach is all about understanding her clients’ needs and creating tailored strategies that help them thrive in the digital world.
Beyond marketing, Jenny is also a best-selling author. She contributed to She Built It!: Inspiring Strategies and Stories for Women in Business, where she shares her journey as an entrepreneur alongside other inspiring women. The book offers honest insights into the challenges of building a business and the strategies that helped her &#8211; and many others &#8211; succeed. Her story has resonated with readers, making her not just a leader in digital marketing but also an advocate for women in business.
Jenny takes a practical, no-nonsense approach to marketing. She loves getting into the nitty-gritty of strategy, data, and creativity, helping businesses build a strong online presence that attracts customers and drives growth. Whether she’s working on a website, an ad campaign, or social media content, she’s always focused on what actually works.
Driven by innovation and a genuine love for what she does, Jenny continues to help brands stand out, connect with their audience, and achieve long-term success in the digital space.

About Us
The Concept Designs &amp; Marketing Team
Concept Designs &amp; Marketing is a team of passionate marketing consultants with a deep focus on results-driven digital marketing strategies. Led by Jenny Godfrey, a seasoned expert in Website Design &amp; Development, SEO, Online Ads and Social Media. Jenny and her team focus on crafting tailored digital marketing strategies that help businesses thrive in an ever-evolving online landscape.
By combining data-driven insights with creative solutions, Concept Designs &amp; Marketing enhances brand visibility, engagement, and lead generation. With a commitment to client success and continuous innovation, we empower businesses to stand out, attract more customers, and achieve long-term growth in the digital space.

Jenny Godfrey is a digital marketing strategist with over 23 years experience, and the Founder and CEO of Concept Designs &amp; Marketing. She’s passionate about helping businesses grow through an awesome online presence which includes a great website that drives leads, SEO, AI Search, social media marketing, content creation, and online advertising. With years of experience, Jenny knows how to craft marketing strategies that cut through the noise and deliver real results. Her approach is all about understanding her clients’ needs and creating tailored strategies that help them thrive in the digital world.
Beyond marketing, Jenny is also a best-selling author. She contributed to She Built It!: Inspiring Strategies and Stories for Women in Business, where she shares her journey as an entrepreneur alongside other inspiring women. The book offers honest insights into the challenges of building a business and the strategies that helped her &#8211; and many others &#8211; succeed. Her story has resonated with readers, making her not just a leader in digital marketing but also an advocate for women in business.
Jenny takes a practical, no-nonsense approach to marketing. She loves getting into the nitty-gritty of strategy, data, and creativity, helping businesses build a strong online presence that attracts customers and drives growth. Whether she’s working on a website, an ad campaign, or social media content, she’s always focused on what actually works.
Driven by innovation and a genuine love for what she does, Jenny continues to help brands stand out, connect with their audience, and achieve long-term success in the digital space.
